title.zh: 卷一百 列傳第八十八: 序傳
title.raw: 卷一百 列傳第八十八: 序傳 Volume 100 Biographies 88: Preface to Biographies

sentences.zh: 李氏序傳

translations.literal: Preface Biography of the Li Clan
translations.idiomatic: Preface and Biography of the Li Family

sentences.zh: 李氏之先，出自帝顓頊高陽氏。

translations.literal: The ancestors of the Li clan came from Emperor Zhuanxu of the Gaoyang clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Li family traced its descent to Emperor Zhuanxu of the Gaoyang line.

sentences.zh: 當唐堯之時，高陽氏有才子曰庭堅，為堯大理，以官命族，為理氏。

translations.literal: In the time of Tang Yao, the Gaoyang clan had a talented man named Tingjian, who served Yao as Minister of Justice; taking his office as the clan name, they became the Li clan written with the graph for 'justice.'
translations.idiomatic: In the era of Emperor Yao of Tang, a gifted man of the Gaoyang house named Tingjian served as Grand Minister of Justice under Yao; his clan took the name Li from his office, written with the graph for 'justice.'

sentences.zh: 歷夏、殷之季。

translations.literal: They passed through the end of Xia and Shang.
translations.idiomatic: The line continued through the closing ages of Xia and Shang.

sentences.zh: 其後理征字德靈，為翼隸中吳伯，以直道不容，得罪於紂。

translations.literal: Later Li Zheng, styled Deling, was Earl of Zhongwu in Yizhou; because the straight Way would not tolerate him, he offended Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Li Zheng (styled Deling) held the title Earl of Zhongwu in Yizhou; unable to bend to corrupt ways, he fell foul of King Zhou of Shang.

sentences.zh: 其妻契和氏，摧子利貞逃隱伊侯之墟，食木子而得全，遂改理為李氏。

translations.literal: His wife Qiheshi fled with their son Lizhen to hide in the ruins of the Yi Marquis; eating the fruit of a tree, they survived, and thus changed the Li clan of 'justice' to the Li clan of 'plum.'
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Qihe fled with their son Lizhen to the abandoned lands of the Yi Marquis; they survived by eating the fruit of a tree, and the clan name was changed from the Li of 'justice' to the Li of 'plum.'

sentences.zh: 周時，裔孫日乾，聚于益壽氏女嬰敷。

translations.literal: In Zhou times, a descendant named Rigan married Yinfu, daughter of the Yishou clan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhou period, a descendant named Rigan took as his wife Yinfu, daughter of the Yishou family.

sentences.zh: 生子耳，字伯陽，為柱下史。

translations.literal: She bore a son Er, styled Boyang, who became Archivist under the Pillar.
translations.idiomatic: She bore a son named Er, styled Boyang, who served as Keeper of the Archives.

sentences.zh: 子孫散居諸國，或在趙，或在秦。

translations.literal: Descendants scattered among the states, some in Zhao, some in Qin.
translations.idiomatic: His descendants dispersed among the various states, settling in Zhao, Qin, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 在魏者為段干大夫，段干木其後也。

translations.literal: Those in Wei became the Duanmu grandees; Duanmu Mu was their descendant.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei branch produced the Duanmu grandees, of whom Duanmu Mu was a descendant.

sentences.zh: 別孫忄裏為魏文侯興富國之術焉。

translations.literal: A collateral descendant Li Kui devised for Marquis Wen of Wei the methods to enrich the state.
translations.idiomatic: A collateral descendant, Li Kui, devised for Marquis Wen of Wei the policies that would enrich the state.

sentences.zh: 在趙者曰曇，以功封柏人，武安君牧其後也。

translations.literal: The one in Zhao was named Tan; for merit he was enfeoffed at Boren; Lord Wu'an Mu was his descendant.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao branch was headed by Tan, enfeoffed at Boren for his achievements; Lord Wu'an Mu was among his descendants.

sentences.zh: 在秦者名興族，為將軍。

translations.literal: The one in Qin was named Xingzu and became a general.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin branch was represented by Xingzu, who rose to be a general.

sentences.zh: 生子伯祐，建功北狄，封南鄭公。

translations.literal: He bore a son Boyou, who achieved merit against the Northern Di and was enfeoffed as Duke of Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Boyou, who won distinction campaigning against the Northern Di and was enfeoffed as Duke of Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 伯祐生二子，平燕、內德。

translations.literal: Boyou had two sons, Pingyan and Neide.
translations.idiomatic: Boyou had two sons, Pingyan and Neide.

sentences.zh: 子信為秦將，虜燕太子丹。

translations.literal: Son Xin was a Qin general and captured Crown Prince Dan of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xin served as a Qin general and captured Crown Prince Dan of Yan.

sentences.zh: 信孫元曠，仕漢為侍中。

translations.literal: Xin's grandson Yuankuang served Han as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Xin's grandson Yuankuang served the Han as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 元曠弟仲翔，位太尉。

translations.literal: Yuankuang's younger brother Zhongxiang rose to Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankuang's younger brother Zhongxiang rose to the post of Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 仲翔討叛羌於素昌，一名狄道。

translations.literal: Zhongxiang suppressed rebellious Qiang at Suchang, also called Didao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxiang campaigned against rebellious Qiang at Suchang, also known as Didao.

sentences.zh: 仲翔臨陣殞命，葬狄道川，因家焉。

translations.literal: Zhongxiang fell in battle and was buried on the banks of the Didao River; the family settled there.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxiang fell in battle and was buried on the banks of the Didao River, where the family then made its home.

sentences.zh: 《史記李將軍傳》所云其先自槐裏徙居成紀，實始此也。

translations.literal: What the "Biography of General Li" in the Records says about their ancestors moving from Huaili to settle at Chengji in fact begins here.
translations.idiomatic: The account in the Shiji's "Biography of General Li" of the family's move from Huaili to Chengji in fact begins at this point.

sentences.zh: 仲翔曾孫廣，仕漢，曆文、景、武三帝，位前將軍，立功沙漠。

translations.literal: Zhongxiang's great-grandson Guang served Han through the reigns of Wen, Jing, and Wu, rose to General of the Van, and won merit in the desert.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxiang's great-grandson Guang served the Han through the reigns of Emperors Wen, Jing, and Wu, rose to General of the Van, and won distinction in the desert campaigns.

sentences.zh: 廣子當戶、椒、敢。

translations.literal: Guang's sons were Danghu, Jiao, and Gan.
translations.idiomatic: Guang had three sons: Danghu, Jiao, and Gan.

sentences.zh: 當戶子陵，戰歿匈奴。

translations.literal: Danghu's son Ling died in battle against the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Danghu's son Ling fell in battle against the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 椒。

translations.literal: Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao.

sentences.zh: 敢曆侍中、郎中令、關內侯。

translations.literal: Gan successively held the posts of Palace Attendant, Commandant of the Gentlemen, and Marquis within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: Gan served in turn as Palace Attendant, Commandant of the Gentlemen, and Marquis within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 生子禹，位至侍中。

translations.literal: He bore a son Yu, who rose to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Yu, who rose to the post of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 並事具《史》、《漢》。

translations.literal: All these matters are fully recorded in the Records and the Han History.
translations.idiomatic: All of this is recorded in full in the Shiji and the Hanshu.

sentences.zh: 禹生承公。

translations.literal: Yu bore Chenggong.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had a son Chenggong.

sentences.zh: 承公生蜀郡太守先。

translations.literal: Chenggong bore Xian, Governor of Shu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong's son Xian became Governor of Shu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 先生長宗。

translations.literal: Xian bore Changzong.
translations.idiomatic: Xian had a son Changzong.

sentences.zh: 長宗生博士況。

translations.literal: Changzong bore Kuang, an Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: Changzong's son Kuang became an Erudite.

sentences.zh: 況生孝廉本。

translations.literal: Kuang bore Ben, a Filial and Incorrupt graduate.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang's son Ben was a Filial and Incorrupt graduate.

sentences.zh: 本字上明，生巴郡太守次公。

translations.literal: Ben, styled Shangming, bore Cigong, Governor of Ba Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Ben (styled Shangming) had a son Cigong, who became Governor of Ba Commandery.

sentences.zh: 次公生臨淮太守軌。

translations.literal: Cigong bore Gui, Governor of Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Cigong's son Gui became Governor of Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 軌字逸文，生積弩將軍隆。

translations.literal: Gui, styled Yiwen, bore Long, General of the Crossbowmen.
translations.idiomatic: Gui (styled Yiwen) had a son Long, who became General of the Crossbowmen.

sentences.zh: 隆字業緒，生雍。

translations.literal: Long, styled Yexu, bore Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Long (styled Yexu) had a son Yong.

sentences.zh: 雍字俊熙，仁魏，曆尚書郎、濟北、東莞二郡太守。

translations.literal: Yong, styled Junxi, took refuge in Wei and successively served as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and Governor of Jibei and Dongguan commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Yong (styled Junxi) took refuge in Wei and served successively as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and as Governor of Jibei and Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 雍生柔。

translations.literal: Yong bore Rou.
translations.idiomatic: Yong had a son Rou.

sentences.zh: 柔字德遠，晉舉秀才，為相國從事中郎、北地太守。

translations.literal: Rou, styled Deyuan, was recommended as a xiucai under Jin and served as Attendant of the Chancellor and Governor of Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: Rou (styled Deyuan) was recommended as a xiucai under the Jin and served as Attendant of the Chancellor and Governor of Beidi.

sentences.zh: 柔生弇，字秀子，高亮果毅，有智局。

translations.literal: Rou bore Yan, styled Xiuzi, lofty, bright, resolute, and possessed of strategic insight.
translations.idiomatic: Rou had a son Yan (styled Xiuzi), a man of lofty bearing, resolute character, and keen strategic judgment.

sentences.zh: 晉末大亂，與從兄卓居相國晉王保下。

translations.literal: At the end of Jin came great disorder; he and his cousin Zhuo lived under Chancellor Jin Wang Bao.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin empire collapsed into chaos at the end of the dynasty, he and his cousin Zhuo took service under Chancellor Jin Wang Bao.

sentences.zh: 卓位相國從事中郎，保政刑不修，卓率宗族奔于張寔，弇亦隨焉。

translations.literal: Zhuo held the post of Attendant of the Chancellor; when Bao's government and punishments fell into neglect, Zhuo led the clan to flee to Zhang Shi, and Yan followed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo served as Attendant of the Chancellor; when Bao's administration and legal order broke down, Zhuo led the clan to Zhang Shi, and Yan went with them.

sentences.zh: 因仕于張氏，為驍騎左監。

translations.literal: He then entered the service of the Zhang clan as Left Supervisor of the Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He then entered the service of the Zhang family as Left Supervisor of the Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 弇本名良，妻姓梁氏。

translations.literal: Yan's original name was Liang; his wife's surname was also Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's original given name was Liang, and his wife's surname was also Liang.

sentences.zh: 張駿謂弇曰：「卿名良，妻又姓梁，令子孫何以目其舅氏？

translations.literal: Zhang Jun said to Yan: "Your name is Liang and your wife's surname is Liang—how are your descendants to address their maternal uncles?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun said to Yan, "Your given name is Liang and your wife's surname is Liang—how will your descendants address their uncles on the mother's side?

sentences.zh: 昔耿弇以弱年立功，啟中興之業，吾方賴卿，有同耿氏。」

translations.literal: In former times Geng Yan achieved merit in his youth and opened the enterprise of restoration; I now rely on you as I did on the Geng clan.
translations.idiomatic: In former times Geng Yan won distinction while still young and helped launch the restoration; I now place my hopes in you as on the Geng family.

sentences.zh: 乃使名弇。

translations.literal: He then had him take the name Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He then had him adopt the name Yan.

sentences.zh: 曆天水太守、衛將軍，封安西亭侯。

translations.literal: He successively served as Governor of Tianshui and General of the Guard, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Governor of Tianshui and General of the Guard, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十六，贈武衛將軍，建初中，追諡景公。

translations.literal: He died at fifty-six; posthumously he was given the title General of the Martial Guard, and in the Jianchu era was posthumously titled Duke Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-six and was posthumously appointed General of the Martial Guard; in the Jianchu era he was given the posthumous title Duke Jing.

sentences.zh: 子昶，字仲堅，幼有名譽，年十八而亡。

translations.literal: His son Chang, styled Zhongjian, had a fine reputation from youth and died at eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang (styled Zhongjian) enjoyed a fine reputation from childhood but died at the age of eighteen.

sentences.zh: 建初中，追諡簡公。

translations.literal: In the Jianchu era he was posthumously titled Duke Jian.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jianchu era he was given the posthumous title Duke Jian.

sentences.zh: 涼武昭王皓，字玄盛，小字長生，簡公昶之子也。

translations.literal: Martial and Illustrious King Hao of Liang, styled Xuansheng, childhood name Changsheng, was the son of Duke Jian Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Martial and Illustrious King Hao of Liang (styled Xuansheng, childhood name Changsheng) was the son of Duke Jian Chang.

sentences.zh: 遺腹而誕，祖母梁氏，親加撫育。

translations.literal: He was born posthumously; his grandmother, Lady Liang, personally reared him.
translations.idiomatic: He was born after his father's death; his grandmother, Lady Liang of the Liang clan, raised him herself.

sentences.zh: 幼好學，性沈敏寬和，美器度，通涉經史，尤長文義。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning; his nature was deep, keen, generous, and mild, with fine bearing; he ranged widely through the classics and histories and was especially skilled in literary meaning.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he loved learning; he was thoughtful, quick-witted, generous, and mild, with a commanding presence, and he ranged widely through the classics and histories, excelling especially in literary interpretation.

sentences.zh: 及長，頗習武藝，誦孫、吳兵法。

translations.literal: When grown he also studied martial arts and recited the military writings of Sun and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew older he also trained in martial arts and studied the military writings of Sunzi and Wuzi.

sentences.zh: 常與呂光太史令郭霡及其同母弟宋繇同宿。

translations.literal: He often lodged with Lü Guang's Grand Astrologer Guo Mai and his uterine younger brother Song Yao.
translations.idiomatic: He often shared lodgings with Lü Guang's Grand Astrologer Guo Mai and his younger brother by the same mother, Song Yao.

sentences.zh: 霡起謂繇曰：「君當位極人臣，李君必有國土之分。

translations.literal: Mai rose and said to Yao: "You will rise to the highest ministerial rank; Lord Li will surely receive a share of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Mai rose and said to Yao, "You will rise to the highest ministerial rank, and Lord Li is destined to receive a portion of the realm.

sentences.zh: 家有騧黃馬生白額駒。

translations.literal: When a piebald yellow mare at home foals a colt with a white forehead,
translations.idiomatic: When your piebald yellow mare foals a colt with a white forehead,

sentences.zh: 此其時也。」

translations.literal: that will be the time.
translations.idiomatic: that will be the moment.

sentences.zh: 及呂光之末，段業自稱涼州牧，以昭王為效穀令。

translations.literal: At the end of Lü Guang's rule, Duan Ye styled himself Governor of Liang Province and appointed the Illustrious King magistrate of Xiaogu.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Lü Guang's rule, Duan Ye styled himself Governor of Liang Province and appointed the Illustrious King magistrate of Xiaogu.

sentences.zh: 而敦煌護軍馮翊郭謙、沙州中從事敦煌索仙等以昭王溫毅有惠政，推為甯朔將軍、敦煌太守。

translations.literal: But Protector of Dunhuang Guo Qian of Fufeng, Dunhuang Central Attendant Suo Xian, and others, because the Illustrious King was gentle, resolute, and benevolent in government, urged him as General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: But Protector of Dunhuang Guo Qian of Fufeng, Central Attendant of Shazhou Suo Xian of Dunhuang, and others, impressed by the Illustrious King's gentle resolve and benevolent rule, urged him to accept the posts of General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 昭王初難之。

translations.literal: The Illustrious King at first found it difficult to accept.
translations.idiomatic: The Illustrious King was reluctant at first.

sentences.zh: 會宋繇仕於業，告歸，言于昭王曰：「兄忘郭霡言邪？

translations.literal: It happened that Song Yao was serving Ye and asked leave to return; he said to the Illustrious King: "Brother, have you forgotten Guo Mai's words?
translations.idiomatic: At that time Song Yao, who was serving Duan Ye, asked leave to return home and said to the Illustrious King, "Brother, have you forgotten what Guo Mai said?

sentences.zh: 白額駒今已生矣！」

translations.literal: The white-foreheaded colt has now been born!
translations.idiomatic: The white-foreheaded colt has been born!

sentences.zh: 昭王乃從之。

translations.literal: The Illustrious King then accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The Illustrious King then accepted.

sentences.zh: 尋進號冠軍將軍，稱籓於業。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to General Who Conquers Champions and acknowledged Ye as his suzerain.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to General Who Conquers Champions and acknowledged Duan Ye as his suzerain.

sentences.zh: 業僭稱涼王，其右衛將軍索嗣構昭王於業，乃以嗣為敦煌太守，率騎而西，昭王命師擊走之。

translations.literal: Ye presumptuously styled himself King of Liang; his General of the Right Guard Suo Si slandered the Illustrious King to Ye, who then made Si Governor of Dunhuang and sent him west with cavalry; the Illustrious King ordered his troops to attack and drive him off.
translations.idiomatic: When Duan Ye presumptuously styled himself King of Liang, his General of the Right Guard Suo Si slandered the Illustrious King to him; Ye then appointed Si Governor of Dunhuang and sent him west with cavalry, but the Illustrious King ordered his forces to attack and drive him off.

sentences.zh: 於是晉昌太守唐瑤移檄六郡，推昭王為大都督、大將軍、涼公，領秦涼二州牧、護羌校尉，依竇融故事。

translations.literal: Thereupon Governor of Jinchang Tang Yao issued a proclamation to the six commanderies, urging the Illustrious King as Grand Commander-in-Chief, Grand General, and Duke of Liang, bearing the posts of Governor of Qin and Liang provinces and Protector of the Qiang, following the precedent of Dou Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Governor of Jinchang Tang Yao issued a proclamation to the six commanderies, urging the Illustrious King to accept the titles of Grand Commander-in-Chief, Grand General, and Duke of Liang, with governorship of Qin and Liang provinces and the post of Protector of the Qiang, following the precedent of Dou Rong.

sentences.zh: 昭王乃赦境內，建元號庚子，追崇祖考，大開霸府，置左右長史、司馬、從事中郎，備置僚寀。

translations.literal: The Illustrious King then proclaimed an amnesty within his borders, established the era name Gengzi, honored his ancestors, opened a great hegemon's bureau, and appointed Left and Right Chief Clerks, Marshals, and Attendants, fully staffing his officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Illustrious King then proclaimed an amnesty within his borders, established the era name Gengzi, honored his ancestors, opened a great princely administration, and appointed Left and Right Chief Clerks, Marshals, and Attendants, fully staffing his bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 廣辟土宇，屯玉門、陽關，大田積穀，為東討之資。

translations.literal: He broadly expanded his territory, garrisoned Yumenguan and Yangguan, planted fields on a great scale and stored grain, preparing resources for an eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He expanded his territory, garrisoned Yumenguan and Yangguan, planted fields on a large scale and stored grain, building up resources for a future eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 立靖恭堂以議朝政，閱武事焉。

translations.literal: He established the Hall of Tranquil Respect to deliberate on court affairs and review military matters.
translations.idiomatic: He established the Hall of Tranquil Respect for deliberating on state affairs and reviewing military matters.

sentences.zh: 圖贊自古聖帝、明王、忠臣、孝子、烈士、貞女，親為序頌，以明鑒誡之義。

translations.literal: He had painted and eulogized from antiquity sage emperors, enlightened kings, loyal ministers, filial sons, martyrs, and chaste women, personally composing prefaces and hymns to clarify the meaning of mirror and admonition.
translations.idiomatic: He commissioned paintings and eulogies of sage emperors, enlightened kings, loyal ministers, filial sons, martyrs, and chaste women from antiquity, personally writing prefaces and hymns to illustrate the lessons of history.

sentences.zh: 當時文武群公僚佐，亦皆圖贊所志。

translations.literal: At the time the civil and military lords and assistants also all had their aspirations painted and eulogized.
translations.idiomatic: The civil and military officials of his court likewise had their aspirations commemorated in painting and verse.

sentences.zh: 五年，改元為建初。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he changed the era name to Jianchu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he changed the era name to Jianchu.

sentences.zh: 遣舍人黃始、梁興間行歸表于晉。

translations.literal: He sent Gentlemen of the Household Huang Shi and Liang Xing by secret route to return and present a memorial to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Gentlemen of the Household Huang Shi and Liang Xing by secret route to present a memorial to the Jin court.

sentences.zh: 是歲，乃自敦煌徙都酒泉。

translations.literal: That year he moved his capital from Dunhuang to Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: That year he moved his capital from Dunhuang to Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 又以表未報，復遣沙門法泉間行通表建鄴。

translations.literal: Because his memorial had received no reply, he again sent the monk Faquan by secret route to present a memorial at Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: When his memorial received no reply, he again sent the monk Faquan by secret route to present a memorial at Jianye.

sentences.zh: 于時百姓樂業，請勒銘酒泉，乃使儒林祭酒劉彥明為文，刻石頌德。

translations.literal: At that time the people were content in their occupations and requested an inscription at Jiuquan; he had Libationer of the Forest of Scholars Liu Yanming compose the text and carve it in stone to praise his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the people were prosperous and content, and they requested a commemorative inscription at Jiuquan; he had Libationer of the Forest of Scholars Liu Yanming compose the text and carve it in stone to praise his virtue.

sentences.zh: 又有白狼、白兔、白雀、白雉、白鳩等集於園間。

translations.literal: Moreover white wolves, white hares, white sparrows, white pheasants, white doves, and the like gathered in the gardens.
translations.idiomatic: White wolves, white hares, white sparrows, white pheasants, white doves, and other such creatures also gathered in the palace gardens.

sentences.zh: 群下以為白祥，金精所誕，皆應時邕而至；

translations.literal: His subordinates took them as white auspices, born of the essence of metal, all arriving in timely harmony;
translations.idiomatic: His officials regarded these white omens as manifestations of the essence of metal, all arriving in timely harmony;

sentences.zh: 又有神光、甘露、連理、嘉禾眾瑞，請史官記其事。

translations.literal: there were also divine lights, sweet dew, intertwined trees, and fine grain—many portents—and they asked the historiographers to record these events.
translations.idiomatic: and there were also divine lights, sweet dew, intertwined trees, and fine grain—many auspicious signs—and they asked the historiographers to record these events.

sentences.zh: 昭王從之。

translations.literal: The Illustrious King consented.
translations.idiomatic: The Illustrious King agreed.

sentences.zh: 上巳日，宴於曲水，命群僚賦詩，昭王親為之序。

translations.literal: On the Shangsi day he feasted at the winding stream, ordered the officials to compose poems, and the Illustrious King personally wrote the preface.
translations.idiomatic: On the Shangsi festival he held a feast at the winding stream, ordered his officials to compose poems, and personally wrote the preface.

sentences.zh: 於是寫諸葛亮訓誡以勖諸子焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he copied out Zhuge Liang's admonitions to encourage his sons.
translations.idiomatic: He then copied out Zhuge Liang's admonitions to encourage his sons.

sentences.zh: 昭王以緯世之量，為群雄所奉，兵無血刃，遂啟霸業，乃修敦煌舊塞。

translations.literal: The Illustrious King, with the capacity to weave the age together, was upheld by the contending lords; his armies drew no blood from blades, yet he opened a hegemonic enterprise and restored the old passes of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: With the capacity to bring order to a troubled age, the Illustrious King was upheld by rival powers; his armies won victories without bloodshed, and he founded a hegemonic state while restoring the old frontier defenses of Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡曰武昭王，廟號高祖，陵號建世，武昭王十子，譚、歆、讓、愔、恂、翻、豫、宏、眺、亮。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Martial and Illustrious King, temple name Gaozu, tomb name Jianshi; the Martial and Illustrious King had ten sons: Tan, Xin, Rang, Yin, Xun, Fan, Yu, Hong, Tiao, and Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Martial and Illustrious King, with temple name Gaozu and tomb name Jianshi. The Martial and Illustrious King had ten sons: Tan, Xin, Rang, Yin, Xun, Fan, Yu, Hong, Tiao, and Liang.

sentences.zh: 世子譚早卒。

translations.literal: The heir Tan died young.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent Tan died young.

sentences.zh: 後主弟讓，字士遜，雅量凝重，善於謀略，位甯朔將軍，領西羌校尉、輔國將軍、晉敦煌太守、新鄉侯，贈驃騎大將軍，諡曰穆。

translations.literal: The Later Lord's younger brother Rang, styled Shixun, of elegant breadth and grave bearing, skilled in strategy, held the post of General Who Pacifies the North, concurrently Western Qiang Commandant, General Who Assists the State, Jin Governor of Dunhuang, and Marquis of Xinxiang; posthumously given Grand General of Agile Cavalry; posthumous title Mu.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord's younger brother Rang (styled Shixun), a man of elegant breadth and grave bearing skilled in strategy, served as General Who Pacifies the North, concurrently as Western Qiang Commandant, General Who Assists the State, Jin Governor of Dunhuang, and Marquis of Xinxiang; he was posthumously appointed Grand General of Agile Cavalry and given the posthumous title Mu.

sentences.zh: 讓弟愔，字士正，位晉昌、敦煌太守。

translations.literal: Rang's younger brother Yin, styled Shizheng, held the posts of Governor of Jinchang and Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Rang's younger brother Yin (styled Shizheng) served as Governor of Jinchang and Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 愔弟恂，字士如，有幹略，位酒泉、敦煌太守，遇家國之難而終。

translations.literal: Yin's younger brother Xun, styled Shiru, possessed ability and strategy, held the posts of Governor of Jiuquan and Dunhuang, and died in the calamity of state and family.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's younger brother Xun (styled Shiru), a capable and strategic man, served as Governor of Jiuquan and Dunhuang and died in the catastrophe that befell his family and state.

sentences.zh: 恂弟翻，字士舉，小字武疆，英雄秀出，有雄略，位車騎將軍，祈連、酒泉、晉昌郡太守。

translations.literal: Xun's younger brother Fan, styled Shiju, childhood name Wujiang, outstanding among heroes, possessed bold strategy, and held the post of General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Qilian, Jiuquan, and Jinchang commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's younger brother Fan (styled Shiju, childhood name Wujiang), an outstanding hero with bold strategic vision, served as General of Chariots and Cavalry and as Governor of Qilian, Jiuquan, and Jinchang.

sentences.zh: 翻弟豫，字士寧，位西海太守。

translations.literal: Fan's younger brother Yu, styled Shining, held the post of Governor of Xihai.
translations.idiomatic: Fan's younger brother Yu (styled Shining) served as Governor of Xihai.

sentences.zh: 豫弟宏，字士贊，位前將軍、中華令。

translations.literal: Yu's younger brother Hong, styled Shizan, held the posts of General of the Van and Director of Zhonghua.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's younger brother Hong (styled Shizan) served as General of the Van and Director of Zhonghua.

sentences.zh: 宏弟眺，字士遠，位左將軍。

translations.literal: Hong's younger brother Tiao, styled Shiyuan, held the post of General of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's younger brother Tiao (styled Shiyuan) served as General of the Left.

sentences.zh: 眺弟亮，字士融，位右將軍。

translations.literal: Tiao's younger brother Liang, styled Shirong, held the post of General of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: Tiao's younger brother Liang (styled Shirong) served as General of the Right.

sentences.zh: 寶字懷素，小字衍孫，晉昌太守翻之子也。

translations.literal: Bao, styled Huaisu, childhood name Yansun, was the son of Governor of Jinchang Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Bao (styled Huaisu, childhood name Yansun) was the son of Governor of Jinchang Fan.

sentences.zh: 沈雅有度量，驍勇善撫接。

translations.literal: Deep and refined in bearing, with generous measure, valiant and skilled in winning men.
translations.idiomatic: He was thoughtful and refined in bearing, generous in spirit, valiant in battle, and skilled at winning men's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 遇家難，為沮渠蒙遜囚于姑臧。

translations.literal: He met with family calamity and was imprisoned at Guzang by Juqu Mengxun.
translations.idiomatic: When his family met with catastrophe, he was imprisoned at Guzang by Juqu Mengxun.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，與舅唐契北奔伊吾，臣於蠕蠕。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he and his maternal uncle Tang Qi fled north to Yiwu and submitted to the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year, he and his maternal uncle Tang Qi fled north to Yiwu and submitted to the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 其遺眾之歸附者，稍至二千，寶傾身禮接，甚得其心，眾皆為之用，每希報雪。

translations.literal: Those of the remnant followers who came to submit gradually reached two thousand. Bao devoted his whole person to receiving them with courtesy, greatly winning their hearts; all were willing to serve him, each hoping to avenge the wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The remnant followers who came to join him gradually numbered two thousand. Bao received them with every courtesy and won their hearts completely; all were ready to serve him, each longing to avenge past wrongs.

sentences.zh: 屬太武遣將討沮渠無諱于敦煌，無諱捐城遁走。

translations.literal: Just then Emperor Taiwu sent a general to attack Juqu Wuhui at Dunhuang; Wuhui abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Taiwu dispatched a general to attack Juqu Wuhui at Dunhuang, and Wuhui abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 寶自伊吾南歸敦煌，遂修繕城府，規復先業，遣弟懷達，奉表歸誠，太武嘉其忠款，拜懷達散騎常侍、敦煌太守；

translations.literal: Bao returned south from Yiwu to Dunhuang, then repaired the city walls and fortifications, planning to restore the ancestral enterprise; he sent his younger brother Huaida to submit a memorial expressing loyalty. Emperor Taiwu commended their sincerity and appointed Huaida Supervising Cavalry Attendant-in-Ordinary and Administrator of Dunhuang;
translations.idiomatic: Bao returned south from Yiwu to Dunhuang, repaired the city walls and fortifications, and set out to restore the ancestral domain. He sent his younger brother Huaida with a memorial pledging allegiance; Emperor Taiwu praised their loyalty and appointed Huaida Supervising Cavalry Attendant-in-Ordinary and Administrator of Dunhuang;

sentences.zh: 別遣使授寶使持節、侍中、都督西垂諸軍事、鎮西大將軍、開府儀同三司、領護西戎校尉、沙州牧、敦煌公，仍鎮敦煌，四品已下，聽承制假授。

translations.literal: Separately he sent an envoy to invest Bao with the credentials of Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs in the Western Marches, Great General Who Pacifies the West, Director with the Ceremonial of the Three Highest Offices, Colonel Protector of the Western Rong, Governor of Shazhou, and Duke of Dunhuang; he was to continue garrisoning Dunhuang, and for ranks of the fourth grade and below he was permitted to appoint and commission on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent a separate envoy to invest Bao as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs in the Western Marches, Great General Who Pacifies the West, Director with the Ceremonial of the Three Highest Offices, Colonel Protector of the Western Rong, Governor of Shazhou, and Duke of Dunhuang, with orders to continue garrisoning Dunhuang. For offices of the fourth rank and below, he was authorized to appoint and commission at his own discretion.

sentences.zh: 真君五年，因入朝，遂留京師，拜外都大官。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenjun, because he came to court he was detained in the capital and appointed Director of the Outer Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Zhenjun era, he came to court and was kept in the capital, where he was appointed Director of the Outer Court.

sentences.zh: 轉鎮南將軍、并州刺史，還除內部大官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Bingzhou, then upon return was appointed Director of the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Bingzhou, and after returning was appointed Director of the Inner Court.

sentences.zh: 文成初，代司馬文思鎮懷荒，改授鎮北將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Wencheng's reign, he replaced Sima Wensi as Commander of Huaihuang and was reappointed General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Wencheng's reign, he replaced Sima Wensi as commander of Huaihuang and was reassigned as General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 太安五年薨，年五十三，詔賜命服一襲，贈以本官，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tai'an he died at fifty-three. An edict granted one set of funeral robes; he was posthumously given his former office and given the posthumous name Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Tai'an era he died at the age of fifty-three. The court granted him one set of funeral robes, posthumously restored his former office, and gave him the posthumous name Xuan.

sentences.zh: 有六子，承、茂、輔、佐、公業、沖。

translations.literal: He had six sons: Cheng, Mao, Fu, Zuo, Gongye, and Chong.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons: Cheng, Mao, Fu, Zuo, Gongye, and Chong.

sentences.zh: 公業早卒。

translations.literal: Gongye died young.
translations.idiomatic: Gongye died young.

sentences.zh: 承字伯業，少有謀略。

translations.literal: Cheng, courtesy name Boye, had strategic talent from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng, styled Boye, showed strategic talent from an early age.

sentences.zh: 初，寶欲歸款，僚庶多有異議。

translations.literal: Initially, when Bao wished to submit in allegiance, many among his staff and retainers had differing opinions.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao first planned to submit in allegiance, many of his officials and retainers disagreed.

sentences.zh: 承時年十三，勸寶速定大計，於是遂決。

translations.literal: Cheng was then thirteen years old; he urged Bao to decide the great plan quickly, and thus the decision was made.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was then only thirteen; he urged Bao to settle on a decisive course at once, and the plan was adopted.

sentences.zh: 寶仍令承隨表入賀。

translations.literal: Bao then had Cheng accompany the memorial to the capital to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Bao then sent Cheng to accompany the memorial to court to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 太武深相器異，禮遇甚優，賜爵姑臧侯。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu regarded him with exceptional favor and treated him with great courtesy, bestowing the title Marquis of Gucang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu took exceptional notice of him, treated him with great honor, and granted him the title Marquis of Gucang.

sentences.zh: 後遭父憂，居喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: Later he suffered his father's death and was noted for filial piety in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after his father's death, he became known for filial devotion during mourning.

sentences.zh: 承應傳先封，以自有爵，乃以本封讓弟茂，時論多之。

translations.literal: Cheng should have inherited the original enfeoffment, but since he already held a title of nobility he yielded the inherited fief to his younger brother Mao; contemporary opinion widely praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was entitled to inherit the original fief, but since he already held a noble title he yielded the ancestral enfeoffment to his younger brother Mao—an act widely praised at the time.

sentences.zh: 承方裕有鑒裁，為時所重。

translations.literal: Cheng was generous and had discernment, and was respected by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was magnanimous and discerning, and was highly regarded in his day.

sentences.zh: 文成末，以散侯出為龍驤將軍、滎陽太守，為政嚴明，甚著聲稱。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Wencheng's reign, having relinquished his marquisate he went out as General of the Dragon Cavalry and Administrator of Xingyang; his governance was strict and clear, and his reputation was greatly established.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Wencheng's reign, after relinquishing his marquisate he was appointed General of the Dragon Cavalry and Administrator of Xingyang. His administration was strict and clear, and he won great renown.

sentences.zh: 延興五年卒，時年四十五，贈使持節、大將軍、雍州刺史，諡曰穆。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yanxing he died at forty-five. Posthumously he was given the credentials of Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Great General, and Governor of Yongzhou; his posthumous name was Mu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Yanxing era he died at forty-five. He was posthumously invested as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Great General, and Governor of Yongzhou, with the posthumous name Mu.

sentences.zh: 長子韶，字元伯，學涉有器量，與弟彥、虔、蕤並孝文賜名焉。

translations.literal: His eldest son Shao, courtesy name Yuanbo, was learned and possessed capacity and breadth of spirit; together with his brothers Yan, Qian, and Rui, they were all given names by Emperor Xiaowen.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Shao, styled Yuanbo, was broadly learned and possessed great capacity. He and his brothers Yan, Qian, and Rui were all granted their names by Emperor Xiaowen.

sentences.zh: 韶雅為季父沖所知重。

translations.literal: Shao from early on was recognized and esteemed by his uncle Chong.
translations.idiomatic: From early on Shao was recognized and valued by his uncle Chong.

sentences.zh: 延興中，補中書學生，襲爵姑臧侯，除儀曹令。

translations.literal: During Yanxing he was appointed a student of the Palace Secretariat, inherited the marquisate of Gucang, and was appointed Director of the Ceremonial Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yanxing era he entered service as a student of the Palace Secretariat, inherited the marquisate of Gucang, and was appointed Director of the Ceremonial Bureau.

sentences.zh: 時修改車服及羽儀制度，皆令韶典焉。

translations.literal: At that time the regulations for chariots, robes, and ceremonial regalia were being revised, and Shao was put in charge of all of this.
translations.idiomatic: When the regulations governing chariots, robes, and ceremonial regalia were being revised, Shao was placed in charge of the entire undertaking.

sentences.zh: 遷給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate who Serves Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 後依例降侯為伯，兼大鴻臚卿，黃門如故。

translations.literal: Later, following precedent, his marquisate was reduced to a barony; he concurrently served as Grand Master of Ceremonial, retaining his Yellow Gate post.
translations.idiomatic: Later, in accordance with precedent, his marquisate was reduced to a barony. He concurrently served as Grand Master of Ceremonial while retaining his Yellow Gate appointment.

sentences.zh: 孝文將創遷都之計，詔引侍臣，訪以古事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen was planning the move of the capital, he summoned the attendant ministers by edict and inquired of them about ancient precedents.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen was planning to move the capital, he summoned his attendant ministers and asked them about ancient precedents.

sentences.zh: 韶對曰：「洛陽九鼎舊所，七百攸墓，地則土中，實均朝貢，惟王建國，莫尚於此。」

translations.literal: Shao replied: "Luoyang is where the Nine Tripods were formerly kept and where the tombs of the Zhou kings lie; the land is the center of the earth and truly balances tribute from all directions. When a king establishes his state, nothing surpasses this place.
translations.idiomatic: Shao replied: "Luoyang is the ancient seat of the Nine Tripods and the resting place of the Zhou kings. Its land lies at the center of the realm and truly equalizes tribute from every quarter. For a king founding a state, no place is greater than this.

sentences.zh: 帝稱善。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved of this.

sentences.zh: 遷太子右詹事，尋罷左右，仍為詹事、肆州大中正。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Tutor of the Heir Apparent; shortly thereafter the left and right positions were abolished and he remained as Tutor and Chief Rectifier of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Right Tutor of the Heir Apparent. Soon afterward the left and right tutorships were abolished, and he continued as Tutor and Chief Rectifier of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 出為安東將軍、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝自鄴還洛，韶朝于路，帝言及庶人恂事曰：「卿若不出東宮，或未至此也。」

translations.literal: When the Emperor returned from Ye to Luoyang, Shao paid his respects along the route. The Emperor spoke of the affair of the commoner Xun and said: "If you had not left the Eastern Palace, things might not have reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: As the Emperor returned from Ye to Luoyang, Shao met him along the road. The Emperor spoke of the deposed heir Xun and said, "Had you not left the Eastern Palace, matters might never have come to this.

sentences.zh: 宣武初，征拜侍中，領七兵尚書，除撫軍將軍，并州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was summoned and appointed Palace Attendant, Director of the Seven Arms Ministry, General Who Comforts the Army, and Governor of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was summoned to court and appointed Palace Attendant, Director of the Seven Arms Ministry, General Who Comforts the Army, and Governor of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 以從弟伯尚同咸陽王禧之逆，免除官爵。

translations.literal: Because his younger cousin Bo Shang participated in the rebellion of Prince Xianyang Xi, he was stripped of his offices and titles.
translations.idiomatic: Because his younger cousin Bo Shang had joined Prince Xianyang Xi in rebellion, Shao was stripped of his offices and noble titles.

sentences.zh: 久之，兼將作大匠，敕參定朝儀律令。

translations.literal: After some time he concurrently served as Grand Director of Palace Construction and was ordered to help finalize court ritual regulations and statutes.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was additionally appointed Grand Director of Palace Construction and ordered to assist in drafting court ritual and legal codes.

sentences.zh: 及呂苟兒反于秦州，除撫軍將軍、西道都督，行秦州事，與右衛將軍元麗，率眾討之。

translations.literal: When Lu Gou'er rebelled in Qinzhou, Shao was appointed General Who Comforts the Army, Commander of the Western Route, and Acting Administrator of Qinzhou; together with Right Guard General Yuan Li he led troops to suppress the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Gou'er rebelled in Qinzhou, Shao was appointed General Who Comforts the Army, Commander of the Western Route, and Acting Administrator of Qinzhou. Together with Right Guard General Yuan Li, he led forces to suppress the uprising.

sentences.zh: 事平，即真，璽書勞勉，復其先爵。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he received the full appointment; an imperial letter commended and encouraged him and restored his former title of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: Once the campaign was concluded he received full confirmation in office. An imperial letter praised and encouraged him and restored his former noble title.

sentences.zh: 時隴右新經師旅，百姓多不安業，韶善撫納，甚得夷夏之心。

translations.literal: At that time Longyou had recently endured military campaigns and many common people had lost their livelihoods; Shao was skilled at comforting and settling them and won the hearts of both barbarian and Han peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Longyou had recently been ravaged by war, and many people could not maintain their livelihoods. Shao was adept at comforting and resettling them and won the hearts of both tribal and Han populations.

sentences.zh: 孝明初，自相州刺史入為殿中尚書，行雍州事，後除中軍大將軍、吏部尚書，加散騎常侍，出為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaoming's reign, from Governor of Xiangzhou he entered the capital as Director of the Palace Department, acting for Yongzhou affairs; later he was appointed Great General of the Central Army and Director of the Ministry of Personnel, with the additional title of Supervising Cavalry Attendant-in-Ordinary, and went out as Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaoming's reign he left his post as Governor of Xiangzhou to enter the capital as Director of the Palace Department with charge of Yongzhou affairs. He was later appointed Great General of the Central Army and Director of the Ministry of Personnel, with the additional title of Supervising Cavalry Attendant-in-Ordinary, and then sent out as Governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 清簡愛人，甚收名譽，政績之美，聲冠當時。

translations.literal: His governance was clear and simple and he cared for the people; he greatly gained renown, and the excellence of his achievements made his reputation foremost among his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: His administration was clear and unpretentious, and he cared deeply for the people. He won great renown, and the excellence of his record made his reputation foremost in his age.

sentences.zh: 明帝嘉之，就加散騎常侍，遷車騎將軍，賜劍珮、貂蟬各一具，驊騮馬一匹，並衣服寢具。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaoming commended him and on the spot added Supervising Cavalry Attendant-in-Ordinary, promoting him to General of Chariots and Cavalry; he was granted one set of sword and girdle ornament, one cicada fur cap ornament, one Hualiu horse, and bedding and clothing as well.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaoming praised him and on the spot added the title of Supervising Cavalry Attendant-in-Ordinary and promoted him to General of Chariots and Cavalry. He was granted a sword and girdle ornament, a cicada cap ornament, a Hualiu steed, and clothing and bedding.

sentences.zh: 韶以年及懸車，抗表遜位，優旨不許。

translations.literal: Shao, his years having reached the age to hang up his carriage, submitted a memorial resigning his post, but a gracious edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao reached the age of retirement he submitted a memorial requesting to step down, but the Emperor's gracious edict refused him.

sentences.zh: 轉定州刺史，常侍如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Dingzhou, retaining his attendant-in-ordinary title.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Governor of Dingzhou while retaining his attendant-in-ordinary title.

sentences.zh: 及赴中山，冀州父老皆送出西境，相聚而泣。

translations.literal: When he went to Zhongshan, the elders of Jizhou all escorted him to the western border and gathered together weeping.
translations.idiomatic: When he departed for Zhongshan, the elders of Jizhou escorted him to the western border of the prefecture, weeping as they gathered to see him off.

sentences.zh: 二州境既連接，百姓素聞其德，州內大安。

translations.literal: Since the two prefectures shared a border and the people had long heard of his virtue, the prefecture was greatly at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Because the two prefectures bordered each other and the people had long known his reputation for virtue, the region enjoyed great tranquility.

sentences.zh: 正光五年，卒於官，年七十二。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengguang he died in office at seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Zhengguang era he died in office at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 詔贈帛七百匹，贈使持節、散騎常侍、車騎大將軍、司空公、雍州刺史，諡曰文恭。

translations.literal: An edict granted seven hundred bolts of silk posthumously and invested him with the credentials of Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Supervising Cavalry Attendant-in-Ordinary, Great General of Chariots and Cavalry, Duke of Works, and Governor of Yongzhou; his posthumous name was Wengong.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted seven hundred bolts of silk and posthumously invested him as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Supervising Cavalry Attendant-in-Ordinary, Great General of Chariots and Cavalry, Duke of Works, and Governor of Yongzhou, with the posthumous name Wengong.

sentences.zh: 既葬之後，有冀州兵千餘人，戍於荊州，還徑韶墓，相率培塚，數日方還，其遺愛如此。

translations.literal: After the burial, more than a thousand soldiers from Jizhou who were garrisoned in Jingzhou, on their return passed by Shao's tomb and together piled up the mound; only after several days did they return—such was the affection he left behind.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial, more than a thousand Jizhou troops garrisoned in Jingzhou, on their return march, passed Shao's tomb and together raised the mound higher. They did not resume their journey for several days—such was the devotion he had inspired.

sentences.zh: 永安中，以克定秦、隴功，追封安城縣開國伯，邑四百戶。

translations.literal: During the Yong'an era, in recognition of the achievement of pacifying Qin and Long, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Baron Who Foundeds the State of Ancheng with a fief of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yong'an era, in recognition of his role in pacifying Qin and Long, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Baron Who Foundeds the State of Ancheng, with a fief of four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 長子璵，字道璠，溫雅有識量。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yu, courtesy name Daofan, was gentle and refined and possessed discernment and breadth of spirit.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yu, styled Daofan, was gentle and refined, with discernment and breadth of spirit.

sentences.zh: 魏永平二年，釋褐太尉府行參軍，累遷尚書倉部郎中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongping of Wei he began his career as a travelling clerk in the Grand Marshal's office and was repeatedly promoted to Director in the Granaries Section of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Yongping era he entered service as a clerk in the Grand Marshal's office and rose through successive appointments to Director in the Granaries Section of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 後汝南王悅為司州牧，悅性質疏冗，情識不倫，朝廷以璵器望兼美，閑於政事，擢為悅府長史，兼知州務。

translations.literal: Later when Prince of Runan Yue became Governor of Sizhou—Yue by nature was coarse and undisciplined and his judgment uneven—the court, because Yu combined fine reputation and ability and was experienced in government affairs, promoted him to Chief Administrator of Yue's princely establishment and concurrently to manage prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Prince of Runan Yue became Governor of Sizhou, the court noted that Yue was by nature coarse and erratic in judgment. Because Yu combined outstanding reputation and ability with experience in administration, he was promoted to Chief Administrator of Yue's princely establishment with concurrent charge of prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 甚得毗贊之方，因除司州別賀。

translations.literal: He proved very capable in assisting and supporting, and was therefore appointed Branch Administrator of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He proved highly effective in assisting and supporting the prince, and was therefore appointed Branch Administrator of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 遷光祿少卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Office for Ceremonial of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Office for Ceremonial of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 永安初，以本官兼度支尚書，襲封安城縣伯，又除司徒右長史，仍兼尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yong'an he concurrently served as Director of the Treasury at his existing rank, inherited the barony of Ancheng, and was also appointed Right Chief Administrator of the Minister of Works, still concurrently holding the ministry post.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yong'an era he concurrently served as Director of the Treasury at his existing rank, inherited the barony of Ancheng, and was also appointed Right Chief Administrator of the Minister of Works while retaining his ministry appointment.

sentences.zh: 及遷都於鄴，留璵於後，監掌府藏。

translations.literal: When the capital was moved to Ye, Yu was left behind to supervise the storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was moved to Ye, Yu was left behind to supervise the palace storehouses.

sentences.zh: 及撤運宮廟材木，以明幹見稱。

translations.literal: When dismantling and transporting timber from the palace temples, he was noted for his clear efficiency.
translations.idiomatic: In dismantling and transporting timber from the palace temples, he was praised for his clear-headed efficiency.

sentences.zh: 加征南將軍、金紫光祿大夫，尋兼給事黃門侍郎，監典書事。

translations.literal: He was additionally made General Who Pacifies the South and Grand Master for Splendor with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon; shortly he concurrently served as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate who Serves Affairs and supervised the affairs of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Grand Master for Splendor with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon. Soon afterward he concurrently served as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and supervised the affairs of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 出為東徐州刺史，為政清靜，人吏懷之。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of East Xuzhou; his governance was clear and tranquil, and officials and commoners alike cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Governor of East Xuzhou. His administration was clear and tranquil, and both officials and common people held him in affection.

sentences.zh: 解州還，以老疾，不求仕進。

translations.literal: Upon leaving his prefectural post and returning, because of age and illness he sought no further advancement in office.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving his prefectural post and returning home, he sought no further advancement because of age and illness.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，追璵兼前將軍，導從於圜丘行禮。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, Yu was summoned back as Former General to guide and attend the ceremony at the Circular Mound.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the transfer of the mandate, Yu was recalled as Former General to guide and attend the ceremony at the Circular Mound.

sentences.zh: 又攝護軍，陪神武神主入太廟。

translations.literal: He also acted as Protector of the Army and accompanied the spirit tablet of Divine Martial Gao Huan into the Grand Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as acting Protector of the Army and escorted the spirit tablet of Divine Martial Gao Huan into the Grand Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 璵意不願策名兩朝，雖以宿德耆舊被征，過事即絕朝請。

translations.literal: Yu did not wish to hold official rank under two dynasties; though summoned as an elder of established virtue, once the business was done he ceased attending court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had no wish to hold office under two dynasties. Though summoned as a venerable elder of established virtue, once each task was finished he ceased attending court.

sentences.zh: 文宣亦曾命璵預華林宴，顧訪舊事，甚重之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenxuan also once had Yu participate in the Hualin banquet, questioning him about events of old and greatly valuing him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan also once had Yu attend the Hualin banquet, questioning him about events of old and holding him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 天保四年卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianbao he died at seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Tianbao era he died at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 子詮，字世良，任城郡守，贈涇州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Quan, courtesy name Shiliang, was Administrator of Rencheng Prefecture and was posthumously given Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Quan, styled Shiliang, served as Administrator of Rencheng Prefecture and was posthumously appointed Governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 子伯卿，太師府參軍事。

translations.literal: His son Boqing served as an administrative officer in the Grand Preceptor's office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Boqing served as an administrative officer in the Grand Preceptor's office.

sentences.zh: 伯卿子師上，聰敏好學，雅有詞致。

translations.literal: Boqing's son Shishang was clever and fond of learning, and naturally had literary eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: Boqing's son Shishang was clever and devoted to learning, with a natural gift for literary expression.

sentences.zh: 外祖魏收無子，惟有一女，生師上，甚愛重之，童祇便自教屬文，有名於世。

translations.literal: His maternal grandfather Wei Shou had no son but only one daughter, who bore Shishang; Wei greatly loved and valued him and from childhood personally taught him literary composition, and he became renowned in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His maternal grandfather Wei Shou had no sons, only a single daughter who bore Shishang. Wei loved and valued him deeply and personally taught him to compose literary works from childhood; he became famous in his time.

sentences.zh: 後與范陽盧公順俱為符璽郎，待詔文林館。

translations.literal: Later he and Lu Gongshun of Fanyang both served as Seal and Credential Officer, awaiting edicts at the Wenlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and Lu Gongshun of Fanyang both served as Seal and Credential Officers, awaiting edicts at the Wenlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 與博陵崔君洽同志友善，從駕晉陽，寓居僧寺，朝士謂之康寺三少，為物論推許若此。

translations.literal: He was of like mind and friendly with Cui Junqia of Boling; accompanying the imperial carriage to Jinyang they lodged in a Buddhist temple, and court officials called them the Three Young Masters of Kang Temple—such was the esteem in which public opinion held them.
translations.idiomatic: He shared close friendship with Cui Junqia of Boling. When they accompanied the imperial procession to Jinyang and lodged in a Buddhist temple, court officials called them the Three Young Masters of Kang Temple—such was the esteem in which they were held.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝居蕃，奏為王府記室，終於揚州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang of Sui was prince in his fief, Shishang was recommended as Master of Records for the princely establishment; he ended his days in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang of Sui was still a prince, Shishang was recommended as Master of Records for the princely establishment. He died in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 詮弟謐，字世安，位高陽郡守、司農卿、安州刺史。

translations.literal: Quan's younger brother Mi, courtesy name Shi'an, held the posts of Administrator of Gaoyang Prefecture, Minister of Finance, and Governor of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Quan's younger brother Mi, styled Shi'an, served as Administrator of Gaoyang Prefecture, Minister of Finance, and Governor of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 謐子千學，齊武平中尚神武女浮陽長公主，拜駙馬都尉、南青州刺史。

translations.literal: Mi's son Qianxue in the Wuping era of Qi married the Princess of Fuyang, daughter of Divine Martial Gao Huan, and was appointed Commandant of Cavalry and Governor of South Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's son Qianxue, during the Wuping era of Qi, married the Princess of Fuyang, daughter of Divine Martial Gao Huan, and was appointed Commandant of Cavalry and Governor of South Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 謐弟誦，字世業，位假儀同三司、臨漳令。

translations.literal: Mi's younger brother Song, courtesy name Shiye, held the posts of Acting Director with the Ceremonial of the Three Highest Offices and Magistrate of Linzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's younger brother Song, styled Shiye, served as Acting Director with the Ceremonial of the Three Highest Offices and as Magistrate of Linzhang.

sentences.zh: 誦弟世韞，太子舍人、殿中郎。

translations.literal: Song's younger brother Shiyun served as Attendant of the Heir Apparent and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Song's younger brother Shiyun served as Attendant of the Heir Apparent and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 璵子孫繁衍，行人號其宅為李東徐村。

translations.literal: Yu's descendants multiplied, and passers-by called their residence Li's East Xuzhou Village.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's descendants multiplied greatly, and travelers called their residence Li's East Xuzhou Village.

sentences.zh: 璵弟瑾，字道瑜。

translations.literal: Yu's younger brother Jin, courtesy name Daoyu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's younger brother Jin, styled Daoyu.

sentences.zh: 美容貌，有才學，特為韶所鍾愛。

translations.literal: Handsome in appearance and talented in learning, he was especially cherished by Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome in appearance and accomplished in learning, he was especially cherished by Shao.

sentences.zh: 清河王懌甚知賞之。

translations.literal: Prince of Qinghe Yi greatly recognized and appreciated him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qinghe Yi recognized and valued him highly.

sentences.zh: 懌為司徒，辟參軍事。

translations.literal: When Yi became Minister of Works, he recruited Jin as an administrative officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi became Minister of Works, he recruited Jin as an administrative officer in his office.

sentences.zh: 轉著作郎，稍遷通直散騎侍郎，與給事黃門侍郎王遵業、尚書郎盧觀典修儀注。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Institute of Composition, gradually promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Direct-and-Upright Cavalry, and together with Wang Zunye, Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate who Serves Affairs, and Lu Guan, Director of the Ministry, supervised the revision of ceremonial regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Institute of Composition and gradually promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Direct-and-Upright Cavalry. Together with Wang Zunye, Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and Lu Guan, a director in the Ministry of Works, he supervised the revision of ceremonial regulations.

sentences.zh: 王、盧即瑾之外兄。

translations.literal: Wang and Lu were Jin's maternal cousins.
translations.idiomatic: Wang and Lu were Jin's maternal cousins.

sentences.zh: 臨淮王彧謂瑾等三俊，共掌帝儀，可謂舅甥之國。

translations.literal: Prince of Linhuai Yu said that Jin and the other three talents together presided over imperial ceremony—one might call it a domain of uncles and nephews.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Linhuai Yu said that Jin and the other three outstanding men together presided over imperial ceremony—a true domain of uncles and nephews.

sentences.zh: 及明帝崩，上諡策文，瑾所制也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaoming died, the eulogy text for the posthumous title was composed by Jin.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaoming died, Jin composed the eulogy for the posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 莊帝初，于河陰遇害，年三十九，贈冠軍將軍、齊州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuangdi's reign he met his death at Heyin at thirty-nine; posthumously he was given General Who Conquers and Governor of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Zhuangdi's reign he was killed at Heyin at the age of thirty-nine. He was posthumously appointed General Who Conquers and Governor of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 子產之，字孫僑。

translations.literal: His son Chanzhi, courtesy name Sunqiao.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chanzhi, styled Sunqiao.

sentences.zh: 容貌短陋，而撫訓諸弟，愛友篤至。

translations.literal: Short and plain in appearance, yet in raising and instructing his younger brothers his affection and friendship were utterly devoted.
translations.idiomatic: Plain and short in stature, he nevertheless raised and instructed his younger brothers with devoted affection.

sentences.zh: 其舅盧道將稱之曰：「此兒風調，足為李公家孫。」

translations.literal: His maternal uncle Lu Daojiang praised him, saying: "This boy's bearing and temperament fully qualify him as a grandson of the Li house.
translations.idiomatic: His maternal uncle Lu Daojiang praised him, saying, "This boy's bearing and character fully befit a grandson of the house of Li.

sentences.zh: 位北豫州司馬。

translations.literal: He held the post of Military Administrator of North Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Military Administrator of North Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 子仲膺，字公祀。

translations.literal: His son Zhongying, courtesy name Gongsi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongying, styled Gongsi.

sentences.zh: 以學行稱，位太子洗馬。

translations.literal: Renowned for learning and conduct, he held the post of Groom of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Renowned for learning and conduct, he served as Groom of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 仕周，為東京少吏部上士。

translations.literal: Under Zhou he served as Senior Clerk in the Lesser Ministry of Personnel of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Under Northern Zhou he served as Senior Clerk in the Lesser Ministry of Personnel of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，卒于荊州總管司馬。

translations.literal: During the Kaihuang era of Sui he died as Military Administrator under the Commander-in-Chief of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaihuang era of Sui he died while serving as Military Administrator under the Commander-in-Chief of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 產之弟茜之，字曼容，清通，好文學。

translations.literal: Chanzhi's younger brother Qianzhi, courtesy name Manrong, was clear-minded and perceptive and fond of literature.
translations.idiomatic: Chanzhi's younger brother Qianzhi, styled Manrong, was clear-minded and perceptive and devoted to literature.

sentences.zh: 齊天保初，曆太子洗馬，行陽翟郡守，為政清靜，吏人稱之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao in Qi he successively served as Groom of the Heir Apparent and Acting Administrator of Yangzhai Prefecture; his governance was clear and tranquil, and officials and commoners praised him.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianbao era in Qi he served successively as Groom of the Heir Apparent and Acting Administrator of Yangzhai Prefecture. His administration was clear and tranquil, and officials and commoners praised him.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書考功郎中，遇文宣昏縱，見害，時人冤之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director in the Merit-Evaluation Section of the Ministry; encountering the licentious excess of Emperor Wenxuan, he was killed, and contemporaries considered it a great injustice.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Director in the Merit-Evaluation Section of the Ministry. When Emperor Wenxuan's reckless excesses took hold, Qianzhi was killed, and people of the time regarded it as a grave injustice.

sentences.zh: 茜之弟壽之，位梁州中從事，性貞介，不負於人。

translations.literal: Qianzhi's younger brother Shouzhi held the post of Army Supervising Secretary of Liangzhou; by nature upright and firm, he never failed others.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi's younger brother Shouzhi served as Army Supervising Secretary of Liangzhou. Upright and principled by nature, he never failed others.

sentences.zh: 壽之弟禮之，位司徒騎兵參軍。

translations.literal: Shouzhi's younger brother Lizhi held the post of Cavalry Administrative Officer under the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhi's younger brother Lizhi served as Cavalry Administrative Officer under the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 與妻鄭氏相重，妻先亡，遺言終不獨死。

translations.literal: He and his wife Lady Zheng cherished each other deeply; his wife died first, and he left a testament that he would never die alone.
translations.idiomatic: He and his wife Lady Zheng loved each other deeply. When she died first, he declared that he would never die alone—and followed her in death.

sentences.zh: 未幾，禮之腳上發腫，夢妻雲，煮小麥漬之即差，如其言，反創而卒。

translations.literal: Before long, Lizhi's foot began to swell. He dreamed his wife said: "Boil wheat and soak it in the swelling and it will be cured." As she had said, the remedy instead caused a wound and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Lizhi's foot began to swell. He dreamed his wife saying, "Boil wheat and soak the foot in it, and the swelling will heal." He did as she said, but the treatment caused a wound instead, and he died.

sentences.zh: 禮之弟行之，字義通，小字師子。

translations.literal: Lizhi's younger brother Xingzhi, courtesy name Yitong, childhood name Shizi.
translations.idiomatic: Lizhi's younger brother Xingzhi, styled Yitong, childhood name Shizi.

sentences.zh: 簡靜，善守門業，多識前言往行，而不以文學自名。

translations.literal: Simple and quiet, skilled at preserving the family heritage, well versed in the words and deeds of the ancients, yet he did not make a name for himself through literary accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: Reserved and quiet, he was skilled at preserving the family heritage and well versed in the words and deeds of the ancients, yet he never sought renown through literary accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 居喪盡禮，與兄弟深相友愛。

translations.literal: In mourning he fulfilled every ritual requirement; with his brothers he was deeply affectionate and loyal.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning he observed every ritual requirement, and with his brothers he was deeply affectionate and loyal.

sentences.zh: 仕齊，歷位都水使者、齊郡太守，帶青州長史。

translations.literal: He served Qi, successively holding the posts of Commissioner of Waterways, Administrator of Qi Prefecture, and concurrently Long-term Administrator of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served Northern Qi, successively as Commissioner of Waterways, Administrator of Qi Prefecture, and concurrently Long-term Administrator of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 任城王敬憚之，州人號曰李御史。

translations.literal: The Prince of Rencheng respected and feared him; the people of the province called him Censor Li.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Rencheng respected and feared him, and the people of the province called him Censor Li.

sentences.zh: 仕周，為冬官府司寺下大夫。

translations.literal: He served Zhou as a Lesser Grand Master in the Court Bureau of the Winter Palace Office.
translations.idiomatic: Under Northern Zhou he served as Lesser Grand Master in the Court Bureau of the Winter Palace Office.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，封固始縣男，除唐州下溠郡太守，稱疾不行，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kaihuang era of Sui he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Gushi, appointed Administrator of Xiaza Prefecture in Tangzhou, claimed illness and did not take up the post, and died.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Kaihuang era of Sui he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Gushi and appointed Administrator of Xiaza Prefecture in Tangzhou, but he pleaded illness and declined the post, then died.

sentences.zh: 行之風素夷坦，為士友所稱。

translations.literal: Xingzhi's character was mild and straightforward, and he was praised by scholarly friends.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzhi's character was mild and straightforward, and he was praised by scholarly friends.

sentences.zh: 其舅子盧思道深所愛好，常贈詩云：「水衡稱逸人，潘、楊有世親，形骸預冠蓋，心思出囂塵。」

translations.literal: His nephew by marriage Lu Sidao deeply admired him and often sent him a poem, saying: "The Director of Waterways acclaimed a recluse; the Pan and Yang families had marriage alliances; his body took part in official rank, yet his mind rose above the dust of the world.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew by marriage Lu Sidao deeply admired him and often sent him a poem: "The Director of Waterways acclaimed a man of leisure; the Pan and Yang families were joined by marriage; though his person moved among officials' carriages, his mind dwelt beyond the dust of the world.

sentences.zh: 時人以為實錄。

translations.literal: People of the time regarded it as a faithful record.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time regarded it as a faithful portrait.

sentences.zh: 及疾，內外多為求醫，行之曰：「居常待終，士之道也。

translations.literal: When he fell ill, relatives inside and outside the family sought doctors for him in many cases. Xingzhi said: "In normal times one awaits one's end—such is the way of a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill, relatives inside and outside the family sought doctors for him on many occasions. Xingzhi said, "In ordinary times one awaits one's end—that is the way of a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 貧既愈富，何知死不如生？」

translations.literal: If poverty can be cured, who is to say death is not better than life?
translations.idiomatic: If poverty can be cured, who is to say that death is not better than life?

sentences.zh: 一皆抑絕。

translations.literal: He refused them all.
translations.idiomatic: He refused them all.

sentences.zh: 臨終，命家人薄葬，口授墓誌以紀其志曰：「隴西李行之，以某年某月終於某所。

translations.literal: At the point of death he ordered his family to bury him simply and dictated an epitaph to record his intent, saying: "Li Xingzhi of Longxi died at such-and-such a place in such-and-such a year and month.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he ordered his family to give him a simple burial and dictated an epitaph recording his intent: "Li Xingzhi of Longxi died at such-and-such a place in such-and-such a year and month.

sentences.zh: 年將六紀，官曆四朝，道協希夷，事忘可否。

translations.literal: Nearing the age of sixty, he had served through four dynasties; his Way accorded with quietude and emptiness, and in affairs he forgot approval and disapproval.
translations.idiomatic: Nearing sixty years of age, he had served through four dynasties. His conduct accorded with quiet detachment, and in public affairs he cared nothing for praise or blame.

sentences.zh: 雖碩德高風，有傾先構；

translations.literal: Although great virtue and lofty character might overturn ancestral achievements,
translations.idiomatic: Though great virtue and lofty character might have overturned ancestral achievements,

sentences.zh: 而立身行己，無愧夙心。

translations.literal: yet in establishing himself and conducting himself he had no shame before his lifelong convictions.
translations.idiomatic: in how he lived and conducted himself he had no shame before the convictions he had held all his life.

sentences.zh: 以為氣變則生，生化曰死，蓋生者物之用，死者人之終，有何憂喜於其間哉！

translations.literal: He held that when qi transforms there is life, and when life transforms there is death; life is merely the functioning of things, and death is humanity's end—what sorrow or joy is there between them?
translations.idiomatic: He held that when vital force transforms, life arises, and when life transforms, death follows; life is merely the functioning of things, and death is humanity's end—what room is there for sorrow or joy between them?

sentences.zh: 乃為銘曰：人生若寄，視死如歸。

translations.literal: He then had an inscription composed, saying: "Human life is like lodging; view death as returning home."
translations.idiomatic: He then composed an inscription: "Human life is like lodging; view death as returning home."

sentences.zh: 茫茫大夜，何是何非。」

translations.literal: In the vast dark night, what is right and what is wrong?
translations.idiomatic: In the vast dark night, what is right and what is wrong?

sentences.zh: 言終而絕，二子，夷、道。

translations.literal: When he finished speaking he died. He had two sons, Yi and Dao.
translations.idiomatic: When he finished speaking he died. He had two sons, Yi and Dao.

sentences.zh: 行之弟凝之，字惠堅。

translations.literal: Xingzhi's younger brother Ningzhi, courtesy name Huijian.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzhi's younger brother Ningzhi, styled Huijian.

sentences.zh: 光州中從事，非其所好，僶俛而就，秩滿，徑還冀州棗強野舍。

translations.literal: Army Supervising Secretary of Guangzhou—it was not to his liking; he took the post reluctantly, and when his term ended he went straight back to his farmhouse retreat in Zaoqiang, Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Army Supervising Secretary of Guangzhou, a post that did not suit him; he accepted it only reluctantly, and when his term ended he went straight back to his farmhouse retreat in Zaoqiang, Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 凝之明本草藥性，恆以服餌自持，雖年將耄及，而志力不衰。

translations.literal: Ningzhi understood the properties of materia medica and constantly used dietary tonics to maintain himself; even as he neared old age his spirit and strength did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: Ningzhi understood the properties of materia medica and constantly used dietary tonics to sustain himself; even as he approached old age his spirit and strength did not fail.

sentences.zh: 篤好古文，精心典禮，以之終老，未嘗懈倦。

translations.literal: He devoted himself to ancient texts and painstakingly studied ritual propriety, continuing this until his death without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to ancient texts and painstakingly studied ritual propriety, continuing until his death without ever slackening.

sentences.zh: 隋仁壽中卒。

translations.literal: He died during the Renshou era of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Renshou era of Sui.

sentences.zh: 產之兄弟，並有器望。

translations.literal: Chanzhi's brothers all possessed talent and reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Chanzhi's brothers all possessed talent and reputation.

sentences.zh: 邢子才為禮之墓誌云：「食有奇味，相待乃餐，衣無常主，易之而出。」

translations.literal: Xing Zicai wrote in Lizhi's epitaph: "They only ate when they encountered special delicacies and waited to dine together; clothes had no fixed owner—whoever needed them exchanged and wore them out.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Zicai wrote in Lizhi's epitaph: "They ate only when they found something especially fine and waited to dine together; clothes had no fixed owner—whoever needed them took them and wore them out.

sentences.zh: 時以為實錄。

translations.literal: People of the time regarded it as a faithful record.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time regarded it as a faithful portrait.

sentences.zh: 諸歸相親，皆如姊妹。

translations.literal: The sisters-in-law from marriage were all as close as sisters among themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The sisters-in-law who had married into the family were as close to one another as sisters.

sentences.zh: 茜之死，諸弟不避當時兇暴，行喪極哀。

translations.literal: When Qianzhi died, the younger brothers did not avoid the fierce brutality of the times and observed mourning with utmost grief.
translations.idiomatic: When Qianzhi died, the younger brothers did not shrink from the fierce brutality of the times and observed mourning with the deepest grief.

sentences.zh: 趙郡李榮來吊之，歎曰：「此家風範，海內所稱，今始見之，真吾師也。」

translations.literal: Li Rong of Zhao Commandery came to offer condolences and sighed, saying: "This family's exemplary conduct, renowned throughout the realm—I am truly seeing it for the first time. They are truly my teachers.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rong of Zhao Commandery came to offer condolences and sighed, saying, "This family's exemplary conduct, renowned throughout the realm—I am seeing it for the first time. They are truly my teachers.

sentences.zh: 欲與連類，即日自名勞之。

translations.literal: Wishing to be counted among such men, that very day he came forward himself to honor them.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to be counted among such men, that very day he came forward himself to honor them.

sentences.zh: 瑾弟贊，字道璋。

translations.literal: Jin's younger brother Zan, courtesy name Daozhang.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's younger brother Zan, styled Daozhang.

sentences.zh: 少有風尚，辟司徒參軍事。

translations.literal: From youth he had refined character; he was recruited as an administrative officer under the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he had refined character and was recruited as an administrative officer under the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈漢陽郡太守。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously appointed Administrator of Hanyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed Administrator of Hanyang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 子脩年，開府參軍，早亡。

translations.literal: His son Xiunian served as an administrative officer in the Ministry of Works and died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiunian served as an administrative officer in the Ministry of Works and died young.

sentences.zh: 韶弟彥，字次仲，有學業。

translations.literal: Shao's younger brother Yan, courtesy name Cizhong, had scholarly attainments.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's younger brother Yan, styled Cizhong, had scholarly attainments.
