sentences.zh: 孝文初，舉秀才，除中書博士，轉諫議大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign he was selected as a cultivated talent, appointed Doctor of the Secretariat, and transferred to Remonstrance and Criticism Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaowen's reign he was selected as a cultivated talent, appointed Doctor of the Secretariat, and transferred to Remonstrance and Criticism Grandee.

sentences.zh: 後因考課，降為元士。

translations.literal: Later, due to merit evaluation, he was demoted to Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after a merit evaluation, he was demoted to Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 尋行主客曹事，徙郊廟下大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he handled affairs in the Guests Section, then transferred to Lower Grandee of the Suburban and Ancestral Temples.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he handled affairs in the Guests Section, then transferred to Lower Grandee of the Suburban and Ancestral Temples.

sentences.zh: 時朝儀典章，咸未周備，彥留心考定，號為稱職。

translations.literal: At the time court ritual and regulations were not yet fully complete; Yan painstakingly examined and established them and was regarded as thoroughly competent.
translations.idiomatic: At the time court ritual and regulations were not yet fully complete; Yan painstakingly examined and established them and was regarded as thoroughly competent in his duties.

sentences.zh: 孝文南伐，彥諫曰：「臣以為蕞爾江、閩，未足親勞鑾駕。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen campaigned south, Yan remonstrated, saying: "Your subject believes that the tiny Jiang and Min regions are not worth personally troubling the imperial chariot.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen campaigned south, Yan remonstrated, saying, "Your subject believes that the tiny Jiang and Min regions are not worth the trouble of the imperial chariot in person.

sentences.zh: 頻表雖不見納，而以至誠見嘉。

translations.literal: Although his repeated memorials were not accepted, his utmost sincerity was praised.
translations.idiomatic: Although his repeated memorials were not accepted, his utmost sincerity was praised.

sentences.zh: 及六軍次於淮南，征為廣陵王羽長史，加恢武將軍、西翼副將。

translations.literal: When the six armies halted at Huainan, Yan was summoned as Long-term Administrator under Prince of Guangling Yu, with the additional titles General Who Resolves Military Affairs and Deputy Commander of the Western Wing.
translations.idiomatic: When the six armies halted at Huainan, Yan was summoned as Long-term Administrator under Prince of Guangling Yu, with the additional titles General Who Resolves Military Affairs and Deputy Commander of the Western Wing.

sentences.zh: 軍還，除冀州趙郡王幹長史。

translations.literal: After the armies returned he was appointed Long-term Administrator under Prince of Zhao Commandery Gan in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the armies returned he was appointed Long-term Administrator under Prince of Zhao Commandery Gan in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 轉青州廣陵王羽長史，帶齊郡太守。

translations.literal: He transferred to Long-term Administrator under Prince of Guangling Yu in Qingzhou, concurrently serving as Administrator of Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He transferred to Long-term Administrator under Prince of Guangling Yu in Qingzhou, concurrently serving as Administrator of Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 征為龍驤將軍、司徒右長史，轉左長史、秦州大中正。

translations.literal: He was summoned as General of the Flying Dragons and Right Long-term Administrator under the Minister of Works, then transferred to Left Long-term Administrator and Chief Rectifier of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as General of the Flying Dragons and Right Long-term Administrator under the Minister of Works, then transferred to Left Long-term Administrator and Chief Rectifier of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 出行揚州事，尋征拜河南尹，還至汝陰，復敕行徐州事。

translations.literal: He went out to handle Yangzhou affairs; soon he was summoned and appointed Governor of Henan, returned to Ruyin, and was again ordered to handle Xuzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to handle Yangzhou affairs; soon he was summoned and appointed Governor of Henan, returned to Ruyin, and was again ordered to handle Xuzhou affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋徽拜平北將軍、平州刺史，遷平東將軍，徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned and appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Pingzhou, then transferred to General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned and appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Pingzhou, then transferred to General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 延昌二年夏，大霖雨，川瀆皆溢。

translations.literal: In the summer of the second year of Yanchang, torrential rains fell and rivers and canals all overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the second year of Yanchang, torrential rains fell and rivers and canals overflowed everywhere.

sentences.zh: 彥相水陸形勢，隨便疏通，得無淹漬之害。

translations.literal: Yan assessed the terrain by water and land and dredged where appropriate, avoiding flood damage.
translations.idiomatic: Yan assessed the terrain by water and land and dredged where appropriate, so that no flood damage occurred.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉之，頻詔勞勉。

translations.literal: The court praised him with repeated edicts of commendation and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised him with repeated edicts of commendation and encouragement.

sentences.zh: 入為河南尹，遷金紫光祿大夫、光祿勳，轉度支尚書。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Governor of Henan, transferred to Grandee of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and Minister of the Imperial Household, then transferred to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Governor of Henan, transferred to Grandee of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and Minister of the Imperial Household, then transferred to Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 出為撫軍將軍、秦州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as General of the Pacification Army and Governor of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as General of the Pacification Army and Governor of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 時破六韓拔陵等反於北鎮，二夏、豳、涼，所在蜂起，而彥刑政甚嚴。

translations.literal: At that time Poliuhan Baling and others rebelled at the Northern Garrisons; in Xia, Bin, Liang, and other regions rebellions erupted everywhere, while Yan's penal administration was extremely strict.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Poliuhan Baling and others rebelled at the Northern Garrisons; in Xia, Bin, Liang, and other regions rebellions erupted everywhere, while Yan's penal administration was extremely strict.

sentences.zh: 正光五年六月，城人薛珍、劉慶、杜超等因四方離叛，突入州門害彥，推其党莫折大提為帥。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Zhengguang, city men Xue Zhen, Liu Qing, Du Chao, and others, taking advantage of rebellion throughout the four directions, burst into the prefectural gate and killed Yan, installing their fellow Moqi Dati as commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Zhengguang, city men Xue Zhen, Liu Qing, Du Chao, and others, taking advantage of rebellion throughout the realm, burst into the prefectural gate and killed Yan, installing their fellow Moqi Dati as commander.

sentences.zh: 永安中，追贈侍中、驃騎大將軍、司徒公、雍州刺史，諡曰孝貞。

translations.literal: During the Yongan period he was posthumously given Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of Fast Cavalry, Minister of Works, and Governor of Yongzhou, with the posthumous name Xiao Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongan period he was posthumously given Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of Fast Cavalry, Minister of Works, and Governor of Yongzhou, with the posthumous name Xiao Zhen.

sentences.zh: 子燮，字德諧，少有風望，位司徒主簿。

translations.literal: His son Xie, courtesy name Dehe, had refined reputation from youth and held the post of Chief Secretary under the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xie, styled Dehe, had refined reputation from youth and served as Chief Secretary under the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太常少卿。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously appointed Vice Minister of the Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed Vice Minister of the Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 子士萬，有雅望，位高都太守。

translations.literal: His son Shiwani had refined reputation and held the post of Administrator of Gaodu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shiwani had refined reputation and served as Administrator of Gaodu.

sentences.zh: 燮弟爽，字德明。

translations.literal: Xie's younger brother Shuang, courtesy name Deming.
translations.idiomatic: Xie's younger brother Shuang, styled Deming.

sentences.zh: 弟充，字德廣。

translations.literal: Younger brother Chong, courtesy name Deguang.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Chong, styled Deguang.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，太學博士。

translations.literal: In his early adulthood he was an Erudite at the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In early adulthood he was an Erudite at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 大將軍蕭寶夤西討，德廣為行台郎，募眾而征，戰捷，乃手刃仇人，啖其肝肺。

translations.literal: When Grand General Xiao Baoyin marched west on punitive campaign, Deguang served as staff officer on the field headquarters, recruited troops and marched, achieved victory in battle, then personally cut down his enemy and devoured the enemy's liver and lungs.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand General Xiao Baoyin marched west on punitive campaign, Deguang served as staff officer on the field headquarters, raised troops and marched, won the battle, then personally cut down his enemy and devoured the enemy's liver and lungs.

sentences.zh: 覺寶夤有異志，挺身歸闕，朝廷加爵，辭而不受。

translations.literal: Perceiving that Baoyin harbored rebellious intent, he boldly returned to the court; the court offered him ennobled rank, but he refused.
translations.idiomatic: Perceiving that Baoyin harbored rebellious intent, he boldly returned to the court. The court offered him ennobled rank, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 寶夤遂與万俟醜奴同反，大行台爾天光討之，請德廣為從事中郎。

translations.literal: Baoyin then rebelled together with Moqi Chounu. Grand Field Headquarters Erzhu Tianguang campaigned against them and requested Deguang as Administrative Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin then rebelled together with Moqi Chounu. Grand Field Headquarters Erzhu Tianguang campaigned against them and requested Deguang as Administrative Officer.

sentences.zh: 天光用其計，遂定秦、隴。

translations.literal: Tianguang adopted his plans and thus pacified Qin and Long.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang adopted his plans and thus pacified Qin and Long.

sentences.zh: 以功除中散大夫。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed Middle Regular Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was appointed Middle Regular Grandee.

sentences.zh: 痛父非命，終身不食酒肉。

translations.literal: Grieving his father's unnatural death, he never ate wine or meat for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: Grieving his father's unnatural death, he never ate wine or meat for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 妹夫盧元明嗟重之。

translations.literal: His brother-in-law Lu Yuanming sighed and deeply valued him.
translations.idiomatic: His brother-in-law Lu Yuanming sighed and deeply valued him.

sentences.zh: 子士英，有文才，王遵業以女妻之。

translations.literal: His son Shiying had literary talent; Wang Zunye gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shiying had literary talent, and Wang Zunye gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 次僧伽，修整篤業，不應辟命。

translations.literal: Next was Sengqie, upright and devoted to his vocation, who did not respond to summons for office.
translations.idiomatic: Next was Sengqie, upright and devoted to his vocation, who declined every summons to office.

sentences.zh: 時鄭子默有名於世，僧伽曰：「行不適道，文勝其質，郭林宗所謂牆高基下，雖得必喪，此之徒也。」

translations.literal: At the time Zheng Zimo was famous in the world. Sengqie said: "His conduct does not accord with the Way, though his writing exceeds his substance—what Guo Linzong called a high wall on a low foundation, gaining yet certain to lose—just such a person.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zheng Zimo was famous throughout the world. Sengqie said, "His conduct does not accord with the Way, though his writing exceeds his substance—what Guo Linzong called a high wall on a low foundation, gaining yet certain to lose—just such a person.

sentences.zh: 竟如其言。

translations.literal: In the end it happened exactly as he said.
translations.idiomatic: In the end it happened exactly as he said.

sentences.zh: 尚書袁叔德來候僧伽，先滅僕從，然後入門，曰：「見此賢，令吾羞對軒冕。」

translations.literal: Minister Shangshu Yuan Shude came to visit Sengqie, first dismissing his attendants before entering, and said: "Meeting this worthy makes me ashamed to face official rank and cap.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Shangshu Yuan Shude came to visit Sengqie, first dismissing his attendants before entering, and said, "Meeting this worthy man makes me ashamed to face official rank and cap.

sentences.zh: 及卒，叔德為懷舊詩曰：「平生寡俗累，終身無世言。」

translations.literal: When Sengqie died, Shude composed a poem of remembrance, saying: "In life few worldly burdens; in a lifetime no worldly words."
translations.idiomatic: When Sengqie died, Shude composed a poem of remembrance: "In life, few worldly burdens; in a lifetime, no worldly words."

sentences.zh: 其見重如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 僧伽弟法藏，內清介，位員外郎。

translations.literal: Sengqie's younger brother Fazang was inwardly pure and upright and held the post of Supernumerary Director.
translations.idiomatic: Sengqie's younger brother Fazang was inwardly pure and upright and served as Supernumerary Director.

sentences.zh: 德廣弟德顯，位散騎侍郎，贈東秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Deguang's younger brother Dexian held the post of Attendant Gentleman without Regular Appointment and was posthumously given Governor of East Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Deguang's younger brother Dexian served as Attendant Gentleman without Regular Appointment and was posthumously given Governor of East Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 德顯弟德明，敦重有器局，位高陽太守，贈光祿少卿、光州刺史。

translations.literal: Dexian's younger brother Deming was solid and serious with great capacity; he held the post of Administrator of Gaoyang and was posthumously given Vice Minister of the Imperial Household and Governor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dexian's younger brother Deming was solid and serious with great capacity; he served as Administrator of Gaoyang and was posthumously given Vice Minister of the Imperial Household and Governor of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 彥弟虔，字叔恭。

translations.literal: Yan's younger brother Qian, courtesy name Shugong.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's younger brother Qian, styled Shugong.

sentences.zh: 太和初，為中書學生，遷秘書中散，轉冀州驃騎府長史、太子中舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taihe era he was a student at the Secretariat School, transferred to Regular Scrivener in the Secretariat, then transferred to Long-term Administrator under the General of Fast Cavalry's Office in Jizhou and Attendant in the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Taihe era he was a student at the Secretariat School, transferred to Regular Scrivener in the Secretariat, then transferred to Long-term Administrator under the General of Fast Cavalry's Office in Jizhou and Attendant in the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 宣武初，遷太尉從事中郎，出為清河太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he transferred to Administrative Officer under the Minister of Works, then went out as Administrator of Qinghe Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he transferred to Administrative Officer under the Minister of Works, then went out as Administrator of Qinghe Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 屬京兆王愉反，虔棄郡奔闕。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jingzhao Yu rebelled, Qian abandoned his commandery and rushed to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Jingzhao Yu rebelled, Qian abandoned his commandery and rushed to the capital.

sentences.zh: 宣武聞虔至，謂左右曰：「李虔在冀州日久，恩信著物，今拔難而來，眾情自解矣。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu heard that Qian had arrived, he told his attendants: "Li Qian was long in Jizhou, with kindness and trust widely known among the people; now that he has broken through hardship to come, popular sentiment will naturally resolve itself.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu heard that Qian had arrived, he told his attendants, "Li Qian was long in Jizhou, with kindness and trust widely known among the people; now that he has broken through hardship to come, popular sentiment will naturally settle.

sentences.zh: 乃授虔別將，令軍前慰勞。

translations.literal: He then gave Qian the title of Separate Commander and ordered him to proceed with the army to reassure and comfort the troops.
translations.idiomatic: He then gave Qian the title of Separate Commander and ordered him to proceed with the army to reassure and comfort the troops.

sentences.zh: 事平，轉長樂太守。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he transferred to Administrator of Changle Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs were settled he transferred to Administrator of Changle Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 延昌初，冀州大乘賊起，令虔以本官為別將，與都督元遙討平之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanchang, the Dacheng bandits rose in Jizhou; Qian was ordered with his original rank as Separate Commander together with Commander-in-Chief Yuan Yao to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yanchang, the Dacheng bandits rose in Jizhou; Qian was ordered, with his original rank as Separate Commander, to join Commander-in-Chief Yuan Yao in suppressing and pacifying them.

sentences.zh: 遷後將軍、燕州刺史。

translations.literal: He transferred to Rear General and Governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He transferred to Rear General and Governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 還為光祿大夫，加平西將軍，兼大司農。

translations.literal: Returning to court he became Grandee of the Imperial Household, with the additional titles General Who Pacifies the West and concurrent Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to court he became Grandee of the Imperial Household, with the additional titles General Who Pacifies the West and concurrent Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 出為散騎常侍、安東將軍、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the East, and Governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the East, and Governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 追論平冀州之功，賜爵高平男。

translations.literal: To commemorate his merit in pacifying Jizhou he was given the title Viscount of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: To commemorate his merit in pacifying Jizhou he was given the title Viscount of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 還京，除河南邑中正，遷領軍將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital he was appointed Chief Rectifier of Henan County and transferred to General of the Guards and Grandee of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to the capital he was appointed Chief Rectifier of Henan County and transferred to General of the Guards and Grandee of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，授特進、車騎大將軍、儀同三司、散騎常侍，又進號驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was given Special Counselor, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Honors Equal to the Three Highest Ministers, and Attendant-in-Ordinary, then advanced in title to General of Fast Cavalry and Honorably Equivalent to the Three Highest Ministers with an Office of First Rank.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was given Special Counselor, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Honors Equal to the Three Highest Ministers, and Attendant-in-Ordinary, then advanced in title to General of Fast Cavalry and Honorably Equivalent to the Three Highest Ministers with an Office of First Rank.

sentences.zh: 永安三年薨，年七十四，贈侍中、驃騎大將軍、太尉公、都督冀定瀛三州諸軍事、冀州刺史，諡宣景。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongan he died at seventy-four; posthumously he was given Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of Fast Cavalry, Duke and Minister of Works, Commander-in-Chief over military affairs of Ji, Ding, and Ying prefectures, Governor of Jizhou, with the posthumous name Xuan Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongan he died at seventy-four. He was posthumously given Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of Fast Cavalry, Duke and Minister of Works, Commander-in-Chief over military affairs of Ji, Ding, and Ying prefectures, Governor of Jizhou, with the posthumous name Xuan Jing.

sentences.zh: 長子喚，字仁明，位尚書左外兵郎。

translations.literal: His eldest son Huan, courtesy name Renming, held the post of Outer Director of the Military Section in the Ministry Left.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Huan, styled Renming, served as Outer Director of the Military Section in the Ministry Left.

sentences.zh: 莊帝初，于河陰遇害，年四十，贈度支尚書、安東將軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuangdi's reign he met his death at Heyin at forty; posthumously he was given Minister of Revenue, General Who Pacifies the East, and Governor of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Zhuangdi's reign he was killed at Heyin at the age of forty. He was posthumously given Minister of Revenue, General Who Pacifies the East, and Governor of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 子裒，章武郡守。

translations.literal: His son Pou held the post of Administrator of Zhangwu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pou served as Administrator of Zhangwu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 裒弟匹，汲郡守。

translations.literal: Pou's younger brother Pi held the post of Administrator of Jijun Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Pou's younger brother Pi served as Administrator of Jijun Commandery.

sentences.zh: 並以幹局見知。

translations.literal: Both were known and appreciated for their competence and capacity for affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Both were recognized for their competence and administrative ability.

sentences.zh: 喚弟仁曜，位員外散騎侍郎、太尉錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Huan's younger brother Renyao held the posts of Supernumerary Attendant Gentleman without Regular Appointment and Administrative Officer for Records under the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Huan's younger brother Renyao served as Supernumerary Attendant Gentleman without Regular Appointment and Administrative Officer for Records under the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 與兄喚同于河陰遇害，年三十八，贈散騎常侍、左將軍、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Together with his elder brother Huan he met his death at Heyin at thirty-eight; posthumously he was given Attendant-in-Ordinary, Left General, and Governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Together with his elder brother Huan he was killed at Heyin at the age of thirty-eight. He was posthumously given Attendant-in-Ordinary, Left General, and Governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 子捴，字道熾，學尚有風儀。

translations.literal: His son Cong, courtesy name Daochi, was learned and possessed refined bearing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cong, styled Daochi, was learned and carried himself with refined bearing.

sentences.zh: 魏武定中，司空長流參軍。

translations.literal: During the Wuding era of Wei he was Long-term Administrative Officer under the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wuding era of Wei he served as Long-term Administrative Officer under the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 齊天保末，為尚書郎，終於光州司馬。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao in Qi he became a Director in the Ministry of Works and died in the post of Vice Governor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianbao era in Qi he became a Director in the Ministry of Works and died while serving as Vice Governor of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 仁曜弟皓，字仁昭，位散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Renyao's younger brother Hao, courtesy name Renzhao, held the post of Attendant Gentleman without Regular Appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Renyao's younger brother Hao, styled Renzhao, served as Attendant Gentleman without Regular Appointment.

sentences.zh: 亦遇害河陰，贈征虜將軍、涼州刺史。

translations.literal: He too met his death at Heyin and was posthumously given General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He too was killed at Heyin and was posthumously given General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 子士元、士操、武定中，並儀同開府參軍事。

translations.literal: His sons Shiyuan and Shicao, during the Wuding era, both held the post of Military Advisor in an Office of First Rank with Honors Equal to the Three Highest Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Shiyuan and Shicao, during the Wuding era, both served as military advisors in offices of first rank with honors equal to the Three Highest Ministers.

sentences.zh: 皓弟曉，事列於後。

translations.literal: Hao's younger brother Xiao—his affairs are recorded later.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's younger brother Xiao is treated in a later section.

sentences.zh: 虔弟蕤，字延賓，曆步兵校尉、東郡太守、司農少卿。

translations.literal: Qian's younger brother Rui, courtesy name Yanbin, successively held the posts of Colonel of Footsoldiers, Administrator of Dongjun Commandery, and Vice Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's younger brother Rui, styled Yanbin, successively served as Colonel of Footsoldiers, Administrator of Dongjun Commandery, and Vice Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈龍驤將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously given General of the Flying Dragon and Governor of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously given General of the Flying Dragon and Governor of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 承弟茂，字仲宗。

translations.literal: Cheng's younger brother Mao, courtesy name Zhongzong.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng's younger brother Mao, styled Zhongzong.

sentences.zh: 文成末，襲父爵鎮西將軍、敦煌公。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Wencheng's reign he inherited his father's title of General Who Guards the West and Duke of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Emperor Wencheng's reign he inherited his father's title of General Who Guards the West and Duke of Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 孝文初，除長安鎮都將，轉西汾州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign he was appointed Chief Commander of Chang'an Garrison, transferred to Governor of West Fenzhou, and kept his general's title unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaowen's reign he was appointed chief commander of the Chang'an garrison, transferred to Governor of West Fenzhou, and retained his general's title.

sentences.zh: 入為光祿大夫，曆西兗州刺史，例降為侯。

translations.literal: Entering court he became Grandee of the Imperial Household, successively served as Governor of West Yanzhou, and by precedent was demoted to Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Grandee of the Imperial Household, served successively as Governor of West Yanzhou, and by precedent was reduced in rank to marquis.

sentences.zh: 茂性謙慎，以弟沖寵盛，懼于盈滿，以疾求遜位。

translations.literal: Mao's nature was modest and cautious; because his younger brother Chong enjoyed great favor, he feared the peril of fullness and asked to yield his post on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Mao was modest and cautious. Because his younger brother Chong enjoyed great favor at court, he feared the dangers of excess and asked to resign on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 孝文不奪其志，聽食大夫祿，還私第。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen did not override his wish, allowed him to receive a grandee's stipend, and sent him back to his private residence.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen did not override his wish, allowed him to retain a grandee's stipend, and let him return to private life.

sentences.zh: 因居中山，自是優遊裏舍，不入京師。

translations.literal: Thereupon he settled in Zhongshan; from then on he lived at ease in his home and did not enter the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He then settled in Zhongshan and thereafter lived at ease in his home, no longer entering the capital.

sentences.zh: 卒年七十一，諡曰恭侯。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-one; his posthumous title was Marquis Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-one and was given the posthumous title Marquis Gong.

sentences.zh: 子靜，字紹安，襲，位東平原太守。

translations.literal: His son Jing, courtesy name Shao'an, inherited the title and held the post of Administrator of East Pingyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jing, styled Shao'an, inherited the title and served as Administrator of East Pingyuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 卒，子遐，字智遠，襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Xia, courtesy name Zhiyuan, inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his son Xia, styled Zhiyuan, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 遐有幾案才，位河內太守。

translations.literal: Xia had talent for desk work and held the post of Administrator of Henei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xia had a talent for administrative work and served as Administrator of Henei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 從孝莊南度河，于河陰遇亂兵所害。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Xiaozhuang south across the river, he met his death at Heyin at the hands of mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: Following Emperor Xiaozhuang south across the river, he was killed at Heyin by mutinous troops.

sentences.zh: 事甯，追贈散騎常侍、車騎大將軍、尚書右僕射、秦州刺史，封盧鄉伯。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he was posthumously given Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Works, and Governor of Qinzhou, and enfeoffed as Baron of Luxiang.
translations.idiomatic: When peace was restored he was posthumously given Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Works, and Governor of Qinzhou, and enfeoffed as Baron of Luxiang.

sentences.zh: 靜弟孚，字仲安。

translations.literal: Jing's younger brother Fu, courtesy name Zhong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's younger brother Fu, styled Zhong'an.

sentences.zh: 恭慎篤厚，曆汝南、中山二郡太守。

translations.literal: Respectful, cautious, and sincere, he successively held the posts of Administrator of Runan and Zhongshan commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Respectful, cautious, and sincere, he successively served as administrator of Runan and Zhongshan commanderies.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，以外親超授撫軍將軍、金紫光祿大夫，出為鎮東將軍、滄州刺史，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, because of imperial kinship he was exceptionally promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army and Grandee of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, then sent out as General Who Guards the East and Governor of Cangzhou, with the additional title Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, because of his connection to the imperial family he was exceptionally promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army and Grandee of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, then sent out as General Who Guards the East and Governor of Cangzhou with the additional title Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 孚弟季安，粗涉書史，位北海王顥撫軍長史。

translations.literal: Fu's younger brother Ji'an had a rough acquaintance with books and history and held the post of Long-term Administrator under Prince of Beihai Hao's Pacifying Army.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's younger brother Ji'an had a rough acquaintance with books and history and served as long-term administrator under Prince of Beihai Hao's Pacifying Army.

sentences.zh: 顥為關西都督，復引為長史，委以戎政。

translations.literal: When Hao became Governor-General of Guanxi, he again brought Ji'an on as Long-term Administrator and entrusted him with military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao became governor-general of Guanxi, he again brought Ji'an on as long-term administrator and entrusted him with military affairs.

sentences.zh: 卒於軍，贈征虜將軍、涼州刺史。

translations.literal: He died in camp and was posthumously given General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died in camp and was posthumously given General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 茂弟輔，字叔直。

translations.literal: Mao's younger brother Fu, courtesy name Shuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Mao's younger brother Fu, styled Shuzhi.

sentences.zh: 有器望，解褐中書博士，遷司徒議曹掾。

translations.literal: He had capacity and reputation; leaving the commoner's garb he became Doctor of the Secretariat and transferred to Administrative Officer in the Secretariat's Advisory Section.
translations.idiomatic: He had capacity and reputation. He began his career as Doctor of the Secretariat and transferred to administrative officer in the Secretariat's advisory section.

sentences.zh: 太和中，孝文為咸陽王禧納其女為妃，除鎮遠將軍、潁川太守，帶長社戍。

translations.literal: During the Taihe era Emperor Xiaowen took Fu's daughter as consort for Prince of Xianyang Xi and appointed Fu General Who Pacifies the Distant and Administrator of Yingchuan Commandery, with charge over the Changshe garrison.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era Emperor Xiaowen took Fu's daughter as consort for Prince of Xianyang Xi and appointed him General Who Pacifies the Distant and Administrator of Yingchuan Commandery, with charge over the Changshe garrison.

sentences.zh: 輔綏懷招集，甚得邊和。

translations.literal: Fu mollified and gathered the people and won great harmony on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Fu mollified and rallied the people and won great harmony on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 卒於郡，贈征虜將軍、秦州刺史，諡曰襄武侯。

translations.literal: He died in his commandery and was posthumously given General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Governor of Qinzhou, with the posthumous title Marquis Xiangwu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his commandery and was posthumously given General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Governor of Qinzhou, with the posthumous title Marquis Xiangwu.

sentences.zh: 長子伯尚，少有重名，弱冠除秘書郎。

translations.literal: His eldest son Boshang had great renown from youth; at twenty he was appointed Secretary Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Boshang had great renown from youth, and at twenty he was appointed Secretary Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 孝文每云：「此李氏之千里駒。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen often said: "This is a thousand-li colt of the Li clan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen often said, "This is a thousand-li colt of the Li family.

sentences.zh: 稍遷通直散騎侍郎，敕撰《太和起居注》。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Direct Attendant Gentleman without Regular Appointment and ordered to compile the Records of the Taihe Reign.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to Direct Attendant Gentleman without Regular Appointment and ordered to compile the Records of the Taihe Reign.

sentences.zh: 宣武初，兼給事黃門侍郎，坐與咸陽王禧謀反誅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he concurrently served as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and was executed for plotting rebellion with Prince of Xianyang Xi.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he concurrently served as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and was executed for plotting rebellion with Prince of Xianyang Xi.

sentences.zh: 伯尚弟仲尚，儀貌甚美，少以文學知名。

translations.literal: Boshang's younger brother Zhongshang was very handsome in bearing and became famous early for literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Boshang's younger brother Zhongshang was very handsome in bearing and became famous early for his literary talent.

sentences.zh: 年二十，著《前漢功臣序贊》，及季父司空沖誄。

translations.literal: At twenty he wrote the Preface and Encomium to Meritorious Ministers of the Former Han and a eulogy for his uncle the Minister of Works Chong.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he wrote the Preface and Encomium to Meritorious Ministers of the Former Han and a eulogy for his uncle the Minister of Works Chong.

sentences.zh: 高聰、邢巒見而歎曰：「後生可畏，非虛言也。」

translations.literal: Gao Cong and Xing Luan read them and sighed: "The young are to be feared—no empty saying.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cong and Xing Luan read them and sighed, "The young are to be feared—no empty saying.

sentences.zh: 起家京兆王愉府參軍。

translations.literal: He began his career as administrative officer in Prince of Jingzhao Yu's household.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as administrative officer in Prince of Jingzhao Yu's household.

sentences.zh: 坐兄事，賜死。

translations.literal: Because of his elder brother's affair he was ordered to take his own life.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his elder brother's affair he was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 仲尚弟季凱，沈敏有識量。

translations.literal: Zhongshang's younger brother Jikai was deep, quick-witted, and discerning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshang's younger brother Jikai was deep, quick-witted, and discerning.

sentences.zh: 坐兄事，與母弟俱徙邊，久之，會赦免。

translations.literal: Because of his elder brother's affair he was exiled to the frontier together with his mother and younger brothers; after a long time he was pardoned and released.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his elder brother's affair he was exiled to the frontier together with his mother and younger brothers; after a long time he was pardoned and released.

sentences.zh: 遂寓居晉陽，沈廢積年。

translations.literal: Thereupon he lived in exile at Jinyang, lying low for many years.
translations.idiomatic: He then lived in exile at Jinyang, lying low for many years.

sentences.zh: 後歷位并州安北府長史。

translations.literal: Later he successively held the post of Long-term Administrator of the Pacifying North Office in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he successively served as long-term administrator of the Pacifying North Office in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 孝明崩，爾硃榮陰圖義舉，季凱豫謀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaoming died, Erzhu Rong secretly plotted a righteous uprising, and Jikai took part in the planning.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaoming died, Erzhu Rong secretly plotted a righteous uprising, and Jikai took part in the planning.

sentences.zh: 及莊帝踐祚，征拜給事黃門侍郎，封博平縣侯，加散騎常侍、秘書監、中軍將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang took the throne, Jikai was summoned and appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, enfeoffed as Marquis of Boping County, and given the additional titles Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Secretariat, and General of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang took the throne, Jikai was summoned and appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, enfeoffed as Marquis of Boping County, and given the additional titles Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Secretariat, and General of the Central Army.

sentences.zh: 後爾硃世隆以榮之死，謂季凱通知，於是見害。

translations.literal: Later Erzhu Shilong, on account of Rong's death, believed Jikai had been party to the notification, and thereupon had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Erzhu Shilong, on account of Rong's death, believed Jikai had been party to the plot, and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，追贈侍中、驃騎將軍、吏部尚書、定州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was posthumously given Palace Attendant, General of Fast Cavalry, Minister of Personnel, and Governor of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was posthumously given Palace Attendant, General of Fast Cavalry, Minister of Personnel, and Governor of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 季凱弟延慶，位陳留太守、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Jikai's younger brother Yanqing held the posts of Administrator of Chenliu Commandery and Grandee of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Jikai's younger brother Yanqing served as Administrator of Chenliu Commandery and Grandee of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 延慶弟延度，衛將軍、安德太守。

translations.literal: Yanqing's younger brother Yandu held the titles Guard General and Administrator of Ande Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing's younger brother Yandu held the titles Guard General and Administrator of Ande Commandery.

sentences.zh: 輔弟佐，字季翼，有文武才幹。

translations.literal: Fu's younger brother Zuo, courtesy name Jiyi, had both civil and military talent.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's younger brother Zuo, styled Jiyi, had both civil and military talent.

sentences.zh: 孝文初，兼散騎常侍使高麗，以稱旨，還拜常山太守、真定縣子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign he concurrently served as Attendant-in-Ordinary on a mission to Goguryeo; because his performance pleased the emperor, on return he was appointed Administrator of Changshan Commandery and given the title Viscount of Zhending County.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaowen's reign he concurrently served as Attendant-in-Ordinary on a mission to Goguryeo. Because his performance pleased the emperor, on his return he was appointed Administrator of Changshan Commandery and given the title Viscount of Zhending County.

sentences.zh: 遷懷州刺史，進爵山陽侯，加安南將軍、河內公，轉相州刺史，所在有稱績。

translations.literal: He transferred to Governor of Huaizhou, advanced to Marquis of Shanyang, given the additional titles General Who Pacifies the South and Duke of Henei, then transferred to Governor of Xiangzhou; everywhere he won praise for his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He transferred to Governor of Huaizhou, advanced to Marquis of Shanyang, given the additional titles General Who Pacifies the South and Duke of Henei, then transferred to Governor of Xiangzhou, everywhere winning praise for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 後拜安遠將軍，敕與征南將軍城陽王鸞、安南將軍盧陽烏等攻赭陽，各不相節度。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distant and ordered together with General Who Conquers the South Prince of Chengyang Luan, General Who Pacifies the South Lu Yangwu, and others to attack Zheyang, but each commander lacked unified discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distant and ordered together with General Who Conquers the South Prince of Chengyang Luan, General Who Pacifies the South Lu Yangwu, and others to attack Zheyang, but the commanders lacked unified discipline.

sentences.zh: 諸軍以敵強故班師，佐逆戰，為賊所敗，坐徙瀛州。

translations.literal: The armies withdrew because the enemy was strong; Zuo fought a rear-guard action, was defeated by the rebels, and was banished to Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The armies withdrew because the enemy was strong. Zuo fought a rear-guard action, was defeated by the rebels, and was banished to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 車駕征宛、鄧，復起佐，假平遠將軍、統軍，以功封涇陽縣子。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage marched on Wan and Deng, Zuo was recalled and given Acting General Who Pacifies the Distant and Commander-in-Chief; for his merit he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Jingyang County.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage marched on Wan and Deng, Zuo was recalled and given Acting General Who Pacifies the Distant and Commander-in-Chief. For his merit he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Jingyang County.

sentences.zh: 沔北既平，以佐為廣陽王嘉鎮南府長史，加輔國將軍，別鎮新野。

translations.literal: After the north bank of the Han was pacified, Zuo was made Long-term Administrator of Prince of Guangyang Jia's Pacifying South Office, given the additional title General Who Assists the State, and separately garrisoned Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: After the north bank of the Han was pacified, Zuo was made long-term administrator of Prince of Guangyang Jia's Pacifying South Office, given the additional title General Who Assists the State, and separately garrisoned Xinye.

sentences.zh: 及大軍凱旋，孝文執佐手曰：「沔北，洛陽南門，卿勉為朕善守。」

translations.literal: When the great army returned in triumph, Emperor Xiaowen took Zuo's hand and said: "The north bank of the Han is the southern gate of Luoyang. Do your utmost to guard it well for me.
translations.idiomatic: When the great army returned in triumph, Emperor Xiaowen took Zuo's hand and said, "The north bank of the Han is the southern gate of Luoyang. Do your utmost to guard it well for me.

sentences.zh: 孝文崩，遣敕以佐行荊州事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen died, a final edict had Zuo act as governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen died, a final edict had Zuo act as governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 佐在州，威信大行，邊人悅附，前後歸者二萬許家。

translations.literal: While Zuo was in the province his authority and trust were widely established, border people gladly submitted, and about twenty thousand households returned before and after.
translations.idiomatic: While Zuo was in the province his authority and trust were widely established, border people gladly submitted, and about twenty thousand households returned in all.

sentences.zh: 尋正刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was confirmed as governor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was confirmed as governor.

sentences.zh: 宣武初，征兼都官尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was summoned and concurrently appointed Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was summoned and concurrently appointed Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十一，贈秦州刺史，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-one and was posthumously given Governor of Qinzhou, with the posthumous name Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-one and was posthumously given Governor of Qinzhou, with the posthumous name Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子遵襲。

translations.literal: His son Zun inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zun inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 遵豪爽有父風，卒于司空司馬，贈洛州刺史。

translations.literal: Zun was bold and open with his father's bearing; he died as Vice Governor under the Minister of Works and was posthumously given Governor of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zun was bold and open with his father's bearing. He died while serving as vice governor under the Minister of Works and was posthumously given Governor of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 子果襲，位司空諮議參軍，坐通西魏見殺。

translations.literal: His son Guo inherited and held the post of Advisory Officer under the Minister of Works; for communicating with Western Wei he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guo inherited the title and served as advisory officer under the Minister of Works, but was executed for communicating with Western Wei.

sentences.zh: 遵弟柬，字休賢。

translations.literal: Zun's younger brother Jian, courtesy name Xiuxian.
translations.idiomatic: Zun's younger brother Jian, styled Xiuxian.

sentences.zh: 郡辟功曹，以父憂去職，遂終身不食酒肉，因屏居鄉里。

translations.literal: The commandery recruited him as Merit Officer; on his father's death he left office and thereafter never ate meat or drank wine, retiring to live in his home district.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery recruited him as merit officer. On his father's death he left office and never ate meat or drank wine again, retiring to live in his home district.

sentences.zh: 司空、任城王澄嘉其操尚，以為參軍事，累遷濟州刺史。

translations.literal: The Minister of Works and Prince of Rencheng Cheng admired his integrity and appointed him administrative officer; he rose to Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Works and Prince of Rencheng Cheng admired his integrity and appointed him administrative officer. He rose to Governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈殿中尚書、相州刺史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously given Director in the Palace and Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously given Director in the Palace and Governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 柬弟挺，字神俊，小名提。

translations.literal: Jian's younger brother Ting, courtesy name Shenjun, childhood name Ti.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's younger brother Ting, styled Shenjun, with the childhood name Ti.

sentences.zh: 少以才學知名，為太常劉芳所賞。

translations.literal: From youth he was known for talent and learning and was admired by Minister of Ceremonies Liu Fang.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was known for talent and learning and was admired by Minister of Ceremonies Liu Fang.

sentences.zh: 歷位中書侍郎、太常少卿、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Vice Director of the Secretariat, Vice Minister of Ceremonies, and Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as Vice Director of the Secretariat, Vice Minister of Ceremonies, and Governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時梁將曹敬宗來寇，攻圍積時，又引水灌城，城不沒者數板，神俊循撫兵人，戮力固守。

translations.literal: At that time the Liang general Cao Jingzong came to raid; he besieged the city for a long time and also diverted water to flood it, yet the city was not submerged by only a few boards' thickness. Shenjun comforted the troops and with united effort held firm.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Liang general Cao Jingzong came to raid. He besieged the city for a long time and also diverted water to flood it, yet only a few boards' thickness kept the city from being submerged. Shenjun comforted the troops, and with united effort they held firm.

sentences.zh: 詔遣都督崔暹、別將王羆、裴衍等赴援，敬宗退走。

translations.literal: An edict sent Commander-in-Chief Cui Xian, Separate Commander Wang Bi, Pei Yan, and others to relieve the siege, and Jingzong withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Commander-in-Chief Cui Xian, Separate Commander Wang Bi, Pei Yan, and others to relieve the siege, and Jingzong withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時寇賊之後，城外有露骸，神俊令收葬之。

translations.literal: After the bandit attacks there were exposed corpses outside the city; Shenjun ordered them collected and buried.
translations.idiomatic: After the bandit attacks there were exposed corpses outside the city, and Shenjun ordered them collected and buried.

sentences.zh: 征拜大司農。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 孝明末，除鎮軍將軍，行相州事，時葛榮南逼，神俊憂懼，乃故墜馬傷足，仍停汲郡，有詔追還。

translations.literal: Near the end of Emperor Xiaoming's reign he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Army and acted as governor of Xiangzhou; when Ge Rong pressed south Shenjun was fearful and deliberately fell from his horse and injured his foot, stopping at Jijun Commandery until an edict recalled him.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Xiaoming's reign he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Army and acted as governor of Xiangzhou. When Ge Rong pressed south Shenjun was fearful and deliberately fell from his horse and injured his foot, stopping at Jijun Commandery until an edict recalled him.

sentences.zh: 莊帝即位，以神俊人望，拜散騎常侍、殿中尚書，追論固守荊州功，封千乘縣侯，轉中書監、吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang took the throne, because of Shenjun's public esteem he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director in the Palace; his steadfast defense of Jingzhou was rewarded with enfeoffment as Marquis of Qiancheng County, then he transferred to Director of the Secretariat and Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang took the throne, because of Shenjun's public esteem he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director in the Palace. His steadfast defense of Jingzhou was rewarded with enfeoffment as Marquis of Qiancheng County, and he then transferred to Director of the Secretariat and Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 神俊意尚風流，情在推引人物，爾硃榮有所用人，神俊不從。

translations.literal: Shenjun's aspirations tended toward refinement and elegance, and his heart lay in promoting men of talent; when Erzhu Rong wanted to use certain people Shenjun would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjun's aspirations tended toward refinement and elegance, and his heart lay in promoting men of talent. When Erzhu Rong wanted to use certain people Shenjun would not agree.

sentences.zh: 見怒，懼，啟求解官，除右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Rong grew angry; in fear Shenjun petitioned to resign and was made Right Grandee of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: Rong grew angry. In fear Shenjun petitioned to resign and was made Right Grandee of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 尋屬爾硃兆入京，乘輿幽執，神俊遂逃人間。

translations.literal: Soon after, when Erzhu Zhao entered the capital and the imperial carriage was seized and held in confinement, Shenjun fled into hiding among the people.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, when Erzhu Zhao entered the capital and the emperor was seized and held in confinement, Shenjun fled into hiding among the people.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，歸闕，拜散騎常侍、驃騎大將軍、左光祿大夫、儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he returned to court and was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of Fast Cavalry, Left Grandee of the Imperial Household, and Honors Equal to the Three Highest Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he returned to court and was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of Fast Cavalry, Left Grandee of the Imperial Household, and Honors Equal to the Three Highest Ministers.

sentences.zh: 孝靜初，除驃騎大將軍、華州刺史，入為侍中，薨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaojing's reign he was appointed General of Fast Cavalry and Governor of Huazhou, entered court as Palace Attendant, and died.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaojing's reign he was appointed General of Fast Cavalry and Governor of Huazhou, entered court as Palace Attendant, and died.

sentences.zh: 年六十四，贈尚書左僕射、司徒公，雍州刺史。

translations.literal: At sixty-four he was posthumously given Vice Minister of the Left in the Ministry of Works, Duke and Minister of Education, and Governor of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of sixty-four he was posthumously given Vice Minister of the Left in the Ministry of Works, Duke and Minister of Education, and Governor of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 神俊風韻秀舉，博學多聞，朝廷舊章及人倫氏族，多所諳記。

translations.literal: Shenjun's bearing was elegant and distinguished; he was broadly learned and well informed and knew much of the court's old regulations and the lineages of families.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjun's bearing was elegant and distinguished. He was broadly learned and well informed and knew much of the court's old regulations and the lineages of eminent families.

sentences.zh: 篤學好文雅，老而不輟。

translations.literal: He devoted himself to learning and loved refinement, never ceasing even in old age.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to learning and loved refinement, never ceasing even in old age.

sentences.zh: 凡所交遊，皆一時名士，汲引後生，為其光價，四方才子，咸宗附之。

translations.literal: All his associates were leading figures of the age; he drew up the younger generation and lent them prestige, and talented men from all quarters gathered around him.
translations.idiomatic: All his associates were leading figures of the age. He drew up the younger generation and lent them prestige, and talented men from all quarters gathered around him.

sentences.zh: 滎陽鄭伯獻常云：「從舅為人物宗主。」

translations.literal: Zheng Boxian of Xingyang often said: "My maternal uncle is the patron of men of talent.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Boxian of Xingyang often said, "My maternal uncle is the patron of men of talent.

sentences.zh: 在洛京時，琅邪王誦亦美神俊，故名其子曰俊，庶其似之。

translations.literal: When in Luoyang, Prince of Langye Song also admired Shenjun and therefore named his son Jun, hoping he would resemble him.
translations.idiomatic: When in Luoyang, Prince of Langye Song also admired Shenjun and therefore named his son Jun, hoping he would resemble him.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝雅重其名，常云：「彼若遣李神俊來聘，我當今劉孝綽往。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang greatly valued his name and often said: "If they send Li Shenjun on an embassy, I shall dispatch Liu Xiaochuo in return.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang greatly valued his name and often said, "If they send Li Shenjun on an embassy, I shall dispatch Liu Xiaochuo in return.

sentences.zh: 其見重如此。

translations.literal: Thus highly was he esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 頸多鼠乳。

translations.literal: His neck had many small moles.
translations.idiomatic: His neck bore many small moles.

sentences.zh: 而性通率，不持檢度，至於少年之徒，皆與褻狎。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was free and direct and he did not restrain himself; he even became familiar and intimate with young men in improper ways.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his nature was free and direct and he did not restrain himself; he even became improperly familiar with young men.

sentences.zh: 北遷鄴，于路見狗，溫子升戲曰：「為是宋鵲？

translations.literal: When moving north to Ye, on the road they saw a dog; Wen Zisheng jested and said: "Is it Song Que?
translations.idiomatic: During the northward move to Ye, they encountered a dog on the road. Wen Zisheng quipped, "Could this be Song Que?

sentences.zh: 為是韓盧？」

translations.literal: Or is it Han Lu?
translations.idiomatic: Or is it Han Lu?

sentences.zh: 神俊曰：「為逐丞相東走？

translations.literal: Shenjun said: "Is it chasing the chancellor fleeing east?
translations.idiomatic: Shenjun replied, "Is it chasing the chancellor as he flees east?

sentences.zh: 為共帝女南徂？」

translations.literal: Or is it going south with Lord Gong's daughter?
translations.idiomatic: Or is it accompanying Lord Gong's daughter on her journey south?

sentences.zh: 沙苑之敗，神俊策眇馬而走，曰：「丁掾力。」

translations.literal: At the defeat at Shayuan, Shenjun spurred a one-eyed horse and fled, saying: "Clerk Ding has strength."
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Shayuan, Shenjun galloped away on a one-eyed horse, crying, "Clerk Ding knows his horses!"

sentences.zh: 馬倒，曰：「丁掾誤我。」

translations.literal: The horse fell, and he said: "Clerk Ding has misled me."
translations.idiomatic: When the horse went down, he said, "Clerk Ding has led me astray."

sentences.zh: 其不拘若此。

translations.literal: His lack of restraint was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his unrestrained manner.

sentences.zh: 既不能方重，識者以此為譏。

translations.literal: Since he could not be upright and grave, those who understood took this as grounds for mockery.
translations.idiomatic: Because he could not maintain proper dignity, discerning observers held this against him.

sentences.zh: 喪二妻，又欲娶鄭嚴祖妹，神俊之從甥也。

translations.literal: He lost two wives and again wished to marry the younger sister of Zheng Yanzu, Shenjun's younger cousin by a maternal aunt.
translations.idiomatic: After losing two wives, he sought to marry the sister of Zheng Yanzu, who was Shenjun's cousin on his mother's side.

sentences.zh: 盧元明亦將為婚。

translations.literal: Lu Yuanming also intended to marry her.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuanming also intended to marry her.

sentences.zh: 遂至紛兢，二家鬩于嚴祖之門。

translations.literal: This reached fierce rivalry; the two families quarreled at Yanzu's gate.
translations.idiomatic: Rivalry erupted, and the two families came to blows at Zheng Yanzu's door.

sentences.zh: 鄭卒歸元明，神俊惆悵不已。

translations.literal: Zheng ultimately gave her to Yuanming, and Shenjun remained deeply dejected.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng ultimately gave her to Yuanming, and Shenjun remained deeply dejected.

sentences.zh: 時人以神俊為鳳德之衰。

translations.literal: People of the time regarded Shenjun as a decline in phoenix virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries saw in Shenjun a falling away from the nobility for which he had once been known.

sentences.zh: 沖字思順，承少弟也，本名思沖，孝文改焉。

translations.literal: Chong, courtesy name Sishun, was Cheng's youngest brother; his original name was Sichong, and Emperor Xiaowen changed it.
translations.idiomatic: Chong, courtesy name Sishun, was Cheng's youngest brother. His original name was Sichong, which Emperor Xiaowen changed.

sentences.zh: 少孤，為承訓養。

translations.literal: He was orphaned young and was raised and educated by Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he was raised and educated by Cheng.

sentences.zh: 承常言，此兒器重非恆，方為門戶所寄。

translations.literal: Cheng often said that this child's capacity was not ordinary and that the clan would rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng often said that the boy's talents were exceptional and that the family would one day depend on him.

sentences.zh: 沖雅有大量，隨兄至滎陽，時牧守子弟多侵亂人庶，輕有乞奪，沖與承長子韶獨清簡皎然，無所求取，時人美焉。

translations.literal: Chong had great magnanimity. When he followed his elder brother to Xingyang, at that time the sons of regional governors often harassed the common people and lightly seized what they begged for or simply took; Chong and Cheng's eldest son Shao alone were pure, restrained, and bright, seeking and taking nothing, and people of the time praised them for it.
translations.idiomatic: Chong possessed great magnanimity. When he accompanied his elder brother to Xingyang, the sons of regional governors often preyed on common people, freely demanding and seizing what they wanted. Only Chong and Cheng's eldest son Shao remained spotlessly upright and took nothing for themselves, earning widespread admiration.

sentences.zh: 獻文末，為中書學生，沖善交遊，不妄戲雜，流輩重之。

translations.literal: Near the end of Emperor Xianwen's reign, he became a student at the Secretariat; Chong was skilled in friendship and did not idly fool around, and his peers held him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Xianwen's reign, he became a student at the Secretariat. Chong was skilled at friendship and did not idly fool around, and his peers held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 孝文初，以例遷秘書中散，典禁中文字。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, he was transferred by precedent to Secretariat Attendant and oversaw writing within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, he was transferred by precedent to Secretariat Attendant and oversaw writing within the palace.

sentences.zh: 以修敕繁慧，漸見寵待，遷內秘書令，南部給事中。

translations.literal: Because of his polished elegance and keen intelligence, he gradually won favor and was promoted to Inner Secretariat Director and Attendant in the Southern Department.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his polished elegance and keen intelligence, he gradually won favor and was promoted to Inner Secretariat Director and Attendant in the Southern Department.

sentences.zh: 舊無三長，唯立宗主主督護，所以我隱冒，五十、三十家方為一戶。

translations.literal: Formerly there were no Three Chiefs; only clan heads were established to supervise and protect, so people could conceal and misreport, and only when fifty or thirty households were gathered did they count as one household.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly there were no Three Chiefs; only clan heads were appointed to supervise and protect households, so people could conceal their numbers and misreport, and only when fifty or thirty households were gathered did they count as one household.

sentences.zh: 沖以三正所由來遠，於是創三長之制上之。

translations.literal: Chong held that the Three Chiefs system derived from antiquity, and so he created the Three Chiefs system and submitted it upward.
translations.idiomatic: Chong held that the Three Chiefs system derived from antiquity, and so he devised the Three Chiefs system and submitted it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 文明太后覽而稱善，引見公卿議之，群臣多有不同。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming read it and praised it, summoned the high ministers to discuss it, and many ministers disagreed.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming read it and praised it, summoned the high ministers to discuss it, and many ministers disagreed.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「立三長則課有常准，賦有常分，包廕之戶可出，僥倖之人可止，何為不可？」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said: "If we establish Three Chiefs, then tax assessments will have fixed standards and tax apportionment fixed shares; households that enjoyed shelter can be brought out, and those who counted on luck can be stopped — why should this not be done?
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "If we establish Three Chiefs, tax assessments will have fixed standards and tax apportionment fixed shares; sheltered households can be brought to light, and those who evade duty through luck can be stopped. Why should this not be done?

sentences.zh: 詞議雖有乖異，然惟以變法為難，更無異議，遂立三長，公私便之。

translations.literal: Though the debate had differences, the only further objection was that reform was difficult; there were no other objections, and the Three Chiefs were established, to the convenience of public and private alike.
translations.idiomatic: Though the debate had its differences, the only remaining objection was that reform would be difficult; there were no other objections, and the Three Chiefs were established, to the benefit of both public and private interests.

sentences.zh: 遷中書令，加散騎常侍，給事中如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Secretariat, given the additional title of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and remained Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Secretariat, given the additional title of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and remained Attendant as before.

sentences.zh: 尋轉南部尚書，賜爵順陽侯。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Minister of the Southern Department and was granted the title Marquis of Shunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Minister of the Southern Department and was granted the title Marquis of Shunyang.

sentences.zh: 沖為文明太后所幸，恩寵日盛，賞賜月必數千萬，進爵隴西公，密緻珍寶服禦以充其第，外人莫得而知。

translations.literal: Chong was favored by Empress Dowager Wenming; his grace and favor grew daily, and rewards each month invariably reached tens of millions; he was advanced to Duke of Longxi, and fine treasures and imperial robes filled his residence, unknown to outsiders.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was favored by Empress Dowager Wenming; his grace and favor grew daily, and rewards each month invariably reached tens of millions. He was advanced to Duke of Longxi, and fine treasures and imperial robes filled his residence, unknown to outsiders.

sentences.zh: 沖家素清貧，於是室富。

translations.literal: Chong's family had always been poor; now their house was wealthy.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's family had always been poor; now their house was wealthy.

sentences.zh: 而謙以自牧，積而能散，近自姻族，逮於鄉閭，莫不分及。

translations.literal: Yet he was modest in self-restraint, and though he accumulated wealth he could also disperse it; from close kin to distant neighbors, none went without a share.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was modest in self-restraint, and though he accumulated wealth he could also disperse it; from close kin to distant neighbors, none went without a share.

sentences.zh: 虛己接物，垂念羈寒，衰舊淪屈由之躋敘者，亦以多矣，時以此稱之。

translations.literal: He emptied himself in dealing with others, looked after the stranded and poor, and many who had fallen into decline or obscurity rose in rank through him; people of the time praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: He emptied himself in dealing with others, looked after the stranded and poor, and many who had fallen into decline or obscurity rose in rank through him. People of the time praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 初，沖兄佐與河南太守來崇同自涼州入國，素有微嫌，佐因構成崇罪，餓死獄中。

translations.literal: Initially, Chong's elder brother Zuo and Lai Chong, Governor of Henan, had entered the realm together from Liangzhou and had long harbored slight enmity; Zuo fabricated charges against Lai Chong, who starved to death in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, Chong's elder brother Zuo and Lai Chong, Governor of Henan, had entered the realm together from Liangzhou and had long harbored slight enmity. Zuo fabricated charges against Lai Chong, who starved to death in prison.

sentences.zh: 後崇子護為南部郎，深慮為沖陷，常求退避，沖每慰撫之。

translations.literal: Later Lai Chong's son Hu became an officer in the Southern Department; deeply fearing that Chong would set a trap for him, he often sought to withdraw and avoid contact, and Chong always comforted and reassured him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lai Chong's son Hu became an officer in the Southern Department. Deeply fearing that Chong would set a trap for him, he often sought to withdraw and avoid contact, and Chong always comforted and reassured him.

sentences.zh: 護後坐贓罪，懼必不濟，沖具奏與護本末嫌隙，乞原恕之，遂得不坐。

translations.literal: Later Hu was charged with corruption and feared he would not survive; Chong submitted a full memorial describing the original enmity between himself and Hu, begging forgiveness, and Hu was therefore not punished.
translations.idiomatic: Later Hu was charged with corruption and feared he would not survive. Chong submitted a full memorial describing the original enmity between himself and Hu, begging forgiveness, and Hu was therefore not punished.

sentences.zh: 沖從甥陰始孫貧，來沖家，至如子侄。

translations.literal: Chong's maternal cousin Yin Shisun was poor and came to Chong's house, where he was treated like a son or nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's maternal cousin Yin Shisun was poor and came to Chong's house, where he was treated like a son or nephew.

sentences.zh: 有人求官，因其納馬於沖，始孫輒受而不言。

translations.literal: When someone seeking office gave a horse to Chong through him, Shisun accepted it without saying anything.
translations.idiomatic: When someone seeking office gave a horse to Chong through him, Shisun accepted it without saying anything.

sentences.zh: 後假方便，借沖。

translations.literal: Later, finding a convenient moment, he borrowed Chong's horse.
translations.idiomatic: Later he contrived an opportunity to borrow Chong's horse.

sentences.zh: 此馬主見沖乘馬而不得官，後自陳首始末。

translations.literal: The owner of the horse saw Chong riding the horse but did not receive office; afterward he came forward himself and explained the whole affair.
translations.idiomatic: The owner of the horse saw Chong riding the horse but did not receive office; afterward he came forward himself and explained the whole affair.

sentences.zh: 沖聞大驚，執始孫，以狀款奏，始孫坐死。

translations.literal: When Chong heard this he was greatly shocked; he seized Shisun and submitted a full confession memorial, and Shisun was executed for his crime.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong heard this he was greatly shocked. He seized Shisun and submitted a full confession memorial, and Shisun was executed for his crime.

sentences.zh: 其處要自厲，不念愛惡，皆此類也。

translations.literal: In important matters he was strict with himself and did not consider personal liking or hatred; all his actions were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: In important matters he was strict with himself and did not let personal liking or hatred sway him; all his actions were of this kind.

sentences.zh: 時循舊，王公重臣皆呼名，孝文帝謂沖為中書而不名之。

translations.literal: At the time according to custom, princes and great ministers were all addressed by name, but Emperor Xiaowen called him Secretariat Director rather than by name.
translations.idiomatic: At the time according to custom, princes and great ministers were all addressed by name, but Emperor Xiaowen called him Secretariat Director rather than by name.

sentences.zh: 文明太后崩後，孝文居喪，引見待接有加。

translations.literal: After Empress Dowager Wenming died, Emperor Xiaowen was in mourning; he summoned Chong and treated him with special favor.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Dowager Wenming died, Emperor Xiaowen was in mourning. He summoned Chong and treated him with special favor.

sentences.zh: 及議律令，潤飾辭旨，刊定輕重，孝文雖自下筆，無不使訪焉。

translations.literal: When laws and statutes were discussed, their wording was polished and penalties calibrated; even when Emperor Xiaowen wrote himself, he never failed to consult Chong.
translations.idiomatic: When laws and statutes were discussed, their wording was polished and penalties calibrated. Even when Emperor Xiaowen wrote himself, he never failed to consult Chong.

sentences.zh: 沖竭忠奉上，知無不盡，出入憂勤，形於顏色，雖舊臣戚輔，莫能逮之，俱服其明斷慎密而歸心焉。

translations.literal: Chong exhausted his loyalty in serving the throne and held nothing back of what he knew; his concern and diligence in coming and going showed in his countenance; even old ministers and kinsmen who assisted could not match him, and all admired his clarity, decisiveness, and discretion and gave him their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Chong exhausted his loyalty in serving the throne and held nothing back of what he knew. His concern and diligence showed plainly in his face. Even old ministers and kinsmen who assisted the throne could not match him, and all admired his clarity, decisiveness, and discretion and gave him their hearts.

sentences.zh: 於是天下翕然。

translations.literal: Thereupon the empire fell into unanimous accord.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the empire fell into unanimous accord.

sentences.zh: 及殊方聽望，咸宗奇之。

translations.literal: Reaching to far regions that heard and looked toward him, all honored him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Even in distant lands, those who heard of him looked to him with admiration.

sentences.zh: 孝文亦深相仗信，親敬彌甚，君臣之間，情義莫二。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen also deeply relied on and trusted him; his personal respect grew ever greater; between ruler and minister their bond was singular.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen also deeply relied on and trusted him, and his personal respect grew ever greater. Between ruler and minister their bond was singular.

sentences.zh: 及置百司，開建五等，以沖參定典式，封滎陽侯，拜廷尉卿，遷侍中、吏部尚書、咸陽王師。

translations.literal: When the hundred offices were established and the five ranks of nobility inaugurated, Chong helped fix the canonical forms; he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xingyang, appointed Minister of Justice, and promoted to Palace Attendant, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and Tutor to the Prince of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the hundred offices were established and the five ranks of nobility inaugurated, Chong helped fix the canonical forms. He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xingyang, appointed Minister of Justice, and promoted to Palace Attendant, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and Tutor to the Prince of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 東宮建，拜太子少傅。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Palace was established, he was appointed Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Palace was established, he was appointed Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 孝文初依《周禮》置夫嬪之列，以沖女為夫人。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen initially, following the Rites of Zhou, established ranks of consorts, and made Chong's daughter a Lady.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen initially, following the Rites of Zhou, established ranks of consorts and made Chong's daughter a Lady.

sentences.zh: 及營明堂，詔沖領將作大匠，與司空、長樂公亮共監興繕。

translations.literal: When the Bright Hall was planned, an edict appointed Chong to lead the Master of Construction, and together with the Minister of Works and Duke of Changle, Liang, to jointly supervise construction.
translations.idiomatic: When the Bright Hall was planned, an edict appointed Chong to lead the Master of Construction, and together with the Minister of Works and Duke of Changle, Liang, to jointly supervise construction.

sentences.zh: 車駕南伐，加沖輔國大將軍，統眾翼從。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage marched south on campaign, Chong was given the additional title of Grand General Who Supports the State and commanded troops in support.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage marched south on campaign, Chong was given the additional title of Grand General Who Supports the State and commanded troops in support.

sentences.zh: 自發都至洛陽，霖雨不霽，仍詔六軍發軫，孝文戎服執鞭，禦馬而出，群臣稽顙于馬首之前。

translations.literal: From departing the capital to reaching Luoyang, the rains did not clear; still an edict ordered the six armies to set out; Emperor Xiaowen in military dress held the whip, mounted his horse, and rode out, and the ministers bowed with foreheads to the ground before his horse's head.
translations.idiomatic: From the time they left the capital until they reached Luoyang, the rains did not let up. Still an edict ordered the six armies to set out. Emperor Xiaowen in military dress took the whip, mounted his horse, and rode out, and the ministers bowed with foreheads to the ground before his horse's head.

sentences.zh: 孝文曰：「今大軍將邁，公等更欲何雲？」

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen said: "Now the great army is about to advance — what more do you wish to say?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said, "Now the great army is about to advance — what more do you wish to say?

sentences.zh: 沖進，請曰：「發都淫雨，士馬困弊，矜喪反旆，於義為允。」

translations.literal: Chong stepped forward and petitioned: "Since leaving the capital there has been soaking rain; soldiers and horses are weary and worn; to take pity and turn the banners back would be proper in principle."
translations.idiomatic: Chong stepped forward and pleaded, "Since we left the capital, the rains have not let up and our troops and horses are exhausted. It would be right to show mercy and bring the army home."

sentences.zh: 孝文曰：「已至於此，何容停駕！」

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen said: "We have come this far — how can we halt the chariot!"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said, "We have come this far — how can we halt the chariot!"

sentences.zh: 沖又進曰：「今者之舉，天下所不願，敢以死請。」

translations.literal: Chong stepped forward again and said: "This present expedition is what the empire does not wish; I dare beg with my life."
translations.idiomatic: Chong stepped forward again and said, "This present expedition is what the empire does not wish. I dare beg with my life."

sentences.zh: 孝文大怒曰：「方欲經營宇宙，而卿等儒生，屢疑大計，斧鉞有常，卿勿復言！」

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen was greatly angered and said: "I am just now planning to govern all under heaven, yet you Confucian scholars repeatedly doubt the grand plan; the axe and halberd have their fixed law — speak no more!"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen was greatly angered and said, "I am just now planning to govern all under heaven, yet you Confucian scholars repeatedly doubt the grand plan. The axe and halberd have their fixed law — speak no more!"

sentences.zh: 策馬將出，

translations.literal: He whipped his horse and was about to ride out.
translations.idiomatic: He whipped his horse and was about to ride out.

sentences.zh: 大司馬安定王休、兼左僕射任城王澄等並殷勤泣諫，孝文乃喻群臣曰：「今者興動不小，勤而無成，何以示後？

translations.literal: Grand Marshal, Prince of Anding, Xiu, Acting Left Vice Director and Prince of Rencheng, Cheng, and others all earnestly wept and remonstrated; Emperor Xiaowen then explained to the ministers: "Today's undertaking is no small matter — if we exert ourselves yet achieve nothing, how shall we face posterity?
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal, Prince of Anding, Xiu, Acting Left Vice Director and Prince of Rencheng, Cheng, and others all earnestly wept and remonstrated. Emperor Xiaowen then explained to the ministers, "Today's undertaking is no small matter — if we exert ourselves yet achieve nothing, how shall we face posterity?

sentences.zh: 若不南鑾，即當移都於此。

translations.literal: If we do not proceed south with the imperial carriage, we should move the capital here.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not proceed south with the imperial carriage, we should move the capital here.

sentences.zh: 光宅土中，幾亦時矣，王公等以為何如？

translations.literal: To dwell in glory in the Central Land — the time is nearly ripe; what do you princes and ministers think?
translations.idiomatic: To dwell in glory in the Central Land — the time is nearly ripe. What do you princes and ministers think?

sentences.zh: 議之所決，不得旋踵，欲遷者左，不欲遷者右。」

translations.literal: What the deliberation decides cannot be delayed; those who wish to move, stand left; those who do not, stand right.
translations.idiomatic: What the deliberation decides cannot be delayed. Those who wish to move, stand left; those who do not, stand right.

sentences.zh: 安定王休等相率如右。

translations.literal: Prince of Anding Xiu and the others all followed one another to the right.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Anding Xiu and the others all followed one another to the right.

sentences.zh: 前南安王楨進曰：「愚者暗于成事，智者見於未行，見至德者不議于俗，成大功者不謀於眾。

translations.literal: Former Prince of Nan'an, Zhen, stepped forward and said: "The fool is blind to what is already accomplished; the wise see what has not yet been done; those who perceive supreme virtue do not debate with the vulgar; those who achieve great deeds do not take counsel from the multitude.
