translations.idiomatic: Former Prince of Nan'an, Zhen, stepped forward and said, "The fool is blind to what is already accomplished; the wise see what has not yet been done. Those who perceive supreme virtue do not debate with the vulgar; those who achieve great deeds do not take counsel from the multitude.

sentences.zh: 非常之事。

translations.literal: This is an extraordinary undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: This is an extraordinary undertaking.

sentences.zh: 廓神都以延王業，都中土以制帝京，周公啟之于前，陛下行之于後，固其宜也。

translations.literal: To expand the sacred capital and extend the royal enterprise, to establish the capital in the Central Land and regulate the imperial city — the Duke of Zhou initiated it in former times, Your Majesty carries it out afterward — this is indeed fitting.
translations.idiomatic: To expand the sacred capital and extend the royal enterprise, to establish the capital in the Central Land and regulate the imperial city — the Duke of Zhou initiated it in former times, and Your Majesty carries it out afterward. This is indeed fitting.

sentences.zh: 請上安聖躬，下慰人望，光宅中原，輟彼南伐。

translations.literal: We beg Your Majesty to settle the sacred person above and comfort human hopes below, to dwell in glory in the Central Plains and halt that southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: We beg Your Majesty to settle the sacred person above and comfort the people's hopes below, to dwell in glory in the Central Plains and halt that southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 此臣等之願，亦蒼生幸甚。

translations.literal: This is our ministers' wish, and great fortune for the common people as well.
translations.idiomatic: This is our ministers' wish, and great fortune for the common people as well.

sentences.zh: 群臣鹹唱萬歲。

translations.literal: All the ministers cried "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: All the ministers cried, "Ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 孝文初謀南遷，恐眾心戀舊，乃示為大舉，因以脅定群情，外名南伐，其實遷也。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen had initially planned to move the capital south; fearing that hearts would cling to the old capital, he displayed a great campaign as a pretense to coerce and settle the people's feelings — outwardly named a southern campaign, but in truth it was relocation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen had initially planned to move the capital south. Fearing that hearts would cling to the old capital, he staged a great campaign as a pretense to coerce and settle the people's feelings — outwardly named a southern campaign, but in truth it was relocation.

sentences.zh: 舊人懷土，多所不願，內憚南征，無敢言者，於是定都洛陽。

translations.literal: The old retainers clung to their native soil and mostly did not wish it; inwardly they dreaded the southern expedition but none dared speak — and so the capital was fixed at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The old retainers clung to their native soil and mostly did not wish it. Inwardly they dreaded the southern expedition but none dared speak, and so the capital was fixed at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 尋以沖為鎮南將軍，侍中、少傅如故。

translations.literal: Soon Chong was made General Who Guards the South; Palace Attendant and Junior Tutor as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chong was made General Who Guards the South; Palace Attendant and Junior Tutor as before.

sentences.zh: 委以營構之任，改封陽平郡侯。

translations.literal: He was entrusted with construction duties and his enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Yangping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was entrusted with construction duties and his enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Yangping Commandery.

sentences.zh: 車駕南征，以沖兼左僕射，留守洛陽，遷尚書左僕射，仍領少傅，改封清泉縣侯。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south, Chong was made Acting Left Vice Director, left behind to guard Luoyang, promoted to Left Vice Director of the Ministry of State Affairs, still leading as Junior Tutor, and his enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Qingquan County.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage campaigned south, Chong was made Acting Left Vice Director and left behind to guard Luoyang. He was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Ministry of State Affairs, still leading as Junior Tutor, and his enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Qingquan County.

sentences.zh: 及太子恂廢，沖罷少傅。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Xun was deposed, Chong was removed as Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Xun was deposed, Chong was removed as Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 孝文引見公卿于清徽常曰：「今徙極中天，創居嵩、洛，雖大構未成，要自條紀略舉。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen summoned the high ministers to the Clear and Serene Hall and said: "Now we have moved to the center of heaven and established residence at Song and Luo — though the great structures are not yet complete, the basic order has in essence been set forth.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen summoned the high ministers to the Clear and Serene Hall and said, "Now we have moved to the center of heaven and established residence at Song and Luo. Though the great structures are not yet complete, the basic order has in essence been set forth.

sentences.zh: 但南有未賓之豎，兼凶蠻密邇，朕取南之計決矣，所行之謀必定。

translations.literal: But to the south there are unsubmitting petty foes, and fierce barbarians press close as well; my decision to take the south is settled, and the plan to be carried out is firm.
translations.idiomatic: But to the south there are unsubmitting petty foes, and fierce barbarians press close as well. My decision to take the south is settled, and the plan to be carried out is firm.

sentences.zh: 頃來陰陽卜術之士鹹勸，朕今征必克。

translations.literal: Recently yin-yang and divination masters have all urged that if I campaign now, we are sure to conquer.
translations.idiomatic: Recently yin-yang and divination masters have all urged that if I campaign now, we are sure to conquer.

sentences.zh: 此既家國大事，宜其君臣各盡所見。」

translations.literal: This concerns the great affairs of family and state; ruler and ministers alike should each offer their full view.
translations.idiomatic: This concerns the great affairs of family and state. Ruler and ministers alike should each offer their full view.

sentences.zh: 沖曰：「征戰之法，先之人事，然後卜筮。

translations.literal: Chong said: "The method of warfare places human affairs first, and only then divination.
translations.idiomatic: Chong said, "The method of warfare places human affairs first, and only then divination.

sentences.zh: 卜筮雖吉，猶恐人事未備。

translations.literal: Even if divination is auspicious, one still fears that human affairs are not yet ready.
translations.idiomatic: Even if divination is auspicious, one still fears that human affairs are not yet ready.

sentences.zh: 京師始遷，行業未定，加之征戰，以為未可。」

translations.literal: The capital has only just been moved, livelihoods are not yet settled — to add warfare on top of this, I deem it inadvisable."
translations.idiomatic: The capital has only just been moved and livelihoods are not yet settled. To add warfare on top of this, I deem it inadvisable."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「僕射之言，非為不合朕意。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The Vice Director's words are not that they fail to accord with my intent.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "The Vice Director's words are not that they fail to accord with my intent.

sentences.zh: 然咫尺寇戎，無以自安，理須如此。

translations.literal: Yet the enemy is at our doorstep; there is no way to rest secure — reason demands that it be so.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the enemy is at our doorstep; there is no way to rest secure. Reason demands that it be so.

sentences.zh: 若待人事備，復非天時，將若之何？

translations.literal: If we wait until human affairs are ready, the heavenly timing will again be wrong — what then shall we do?
translations.idiomatic: If we wait until human affairs are ready, the heavenly timing will again be wrong. What then shall we do?

sentences.zh: 如僕射之言，便終無征理。」

translations.literal: If we follow the Vice Director's words, there will never be grounds for campaigning at all."
translations.idiomatic: If we follow the Vice Director's words, there will never be grounds for campaigning at all."

sentences.zh: 沖機敏有巧思，北京明堂、圓丘、太廟，及洛都初基，安處郊兆，新起宮寢，皆資於沖。

translations.literal: Chong was quick-witted and inventive in design; the Bright Hall, Round Mound, and Imperial Temple in the Northern capital, as well as the first laying out of Luoyang, the placing of suburban precincts, and the raising of new palace halls — all relied on Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was quick-witted and inventive in design. The Bright Hall, Round Mound, and Imperial Temple in the Northern capital, as well as the first laying out of Luoyang, the placing of suburban precincts, and the raising of new palace halls — all relied on Chong.

sentences.zh: 勤志強力，孜孜無怠，且理文簿，兼營匠制，幾案盈積，剞劂在前，初不勞厭也。

translations.literal: He pursued his duties with vigor, tirelessly and without slackening; he managed documents even while directing craftsmen's designs — desks piled high, carving blocks before him — and he never showed weariness.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued his duties with vigor, tirelessly and without slackening. He managed documents even while directing craftsmen's designs — desks piled high, carving blocks before him — and he never showed weariness.

sentences.zh: 然顯貴門族，榮益六姻，兄弟子侄，皆有官爵，一家歲祿，萬匹有餘。

translations.literal: Yet his was a distinguished and honored clan; glory enriched all six degrees of kinship — brothers, sons, and nephews all held office and rank, and the family's yearly stipends exceeded ten thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his was a distinguished and honored clan. Glory enriched all six degrees of kinship — brothers, sons, and nephews all held office and rank, and the family's yearly stipends exceeded ten thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 年才四十，而鬢髮斑白，姿貌甚美，未有衰狀。

translations.literal: He was only forty years old, yet his temples were already streaked with white; his bearing was very fine and showed no sign of decline.
translations.idiomatic: He was only forty years old, yet his temples were already streaked with white. His bearing was very fine and showed no sign of decline.

sentences.zh: 李彪之入京也，孤微寡援而自立不群，以沖好士，傾心宗附。

translations.literal: When Li Biao entered the capital, he was isolated, humble, with few patrons, yet stood apart with self-reliance; because Chong loved worthy men, Biao devoted himself and attached to him as to a patron.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Biao entered the capital, he was isolated, humble, with few patrons, yet stood apart with self-reliance. Because Chong loved worthy men, Biao devoted himself and attached to him as to a patron.

sentences.zh: 沖亦重其器學，禮而納焉，每言之入孝文，公私共相援益。

translations.literal: Chong also prized his talent and learning, treated him courteously and took him in; whenever Biao spoke to Emperor Xiaowen, both in public and private they mutually aided and benefited one another.
translations.idiomatic: Chong also prized his talent and learning, treated him courteously and took him in. Whenever Biao spoke to Emperor Xiaowen, both in public and private they mutually aided and benefited one another.

sentences.zh: 及彪為中尉、尚書，為孝文知待，便謂非復藉沖，更相輕背，唯公坐斂袂而已，無復宗敬之意。

translations.literal: When Biao became Commandant of Justice and Minister, and won Emperor Xiaowen's recognition and favor, he decided he no longer needed Chong; they turned to mutual disdain and estrangement, and at public audiences he only drew in his sleeves — no longer any reverence as to a patron.
translations.idiomatic: When Biao became Commandant of Justice and Minister and won Emperor Xiaowen's recognition and favor, he decided he no longer needed Chong. They turned to mutual disdain and estrangement, and at public audiences he only drew in his sleeves — no longer any reverence as to a patron.

sentences.zh: 沖頗銜之。

translations.literal: Chong harbored considerable resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Chong harbored considerable resentment.

sentences.zh: 後孝文南征，沖與吏部尚書、任城王澄並以彪倨傲無禮，遂禁止之，奏其罪狀。

translations.literal: Later when Emperor Xiaowen campaigned south, Chong together with the Minister of Personnel and Prince of Rencheng Cheng all deemed Biao arrogant and without propriety; they placed him under restraint and memorialized his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Later when Emperor Xiaowen campaigned south, Chong together with the Minister of Personnel and Prince of Rencheng Cheng all deemed Biao arrogant and without propriety. They placed him under restraint and memorialized his crimes.

sentences.zh: 沖手自作表，家人不知，辭甚激切，因以自劾。

translations.literal: Chong personally drafted the memorial without his family's knowledge; its language was very fierce, and in it he also impeached himself.
translations.idiomatic: Chong personally drafted the memorial without his family's knowledge. Its language was very fierce, and in it he also impeached himself.

sentences.zh: 孝文覽其表，嗟歎久之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen read the memorial and sighed for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen read the memorial and sighed for a long time.

sentences.zh: 既而曰：「道固可謂隘也，僕射亦為滿矣！」

translations.literal: Then he said: "The Way may indeed be called narrow — and the Vice Director has reached his limit as well!
translations.idiomatic: Then he said, "The Way may indeed be called narrow — and the Vice Director has reached his limit as well!

sentences.zh: 沖時震怒，數責彪前後愆悖，瞋目大呼，投折幾案，盡收御史，皆泥首面縛，大罵辱詈。

translations.literal: Chong was at once enraged; he repeatedly reproached Biao for his past transgressions and insolence, glared and shouted, threw down and smashed desk legs, seized all the censor officials, made them bow with foreheads in mud and bound their faces, and reviled them with great abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was at once enraged. He repeatedly reproached Biao for his past transgressions and insolence, glared and shouted, threw down and smashed desk legs, seized all the censor officials, made them bow with foreheads in mud and bound their faces, and reviled them with great abuse.

sentences.zh: 沖素性溫柔，而一朝暴恚，遂發病荒悸，言語亂錯，猶扼腕叫詈，稱李彪小人。

translations.literal: Chong was by nature gentle and mild, but in a single morning he flew into violent rage; he then fell ill with delirium and palpitations, his speech became confused and erratic, yet he still clutched his wrists and shouted curses, calling Li Biao a petty man.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was by nature gentle and mild, but one morning he flew into violent rage. He then fell ill with delirium and palpitations, his speech became confused and erratic, yet he still clutched his wrists and shouted curses, calling Li Biao a petty man.

sentences.zh: 醫藥所不能療，或謂肝藏傷裂，旬餘日卒。

translations.literal: Medicine could not cure him; some said his liver was torn and ruptured; after a little more than ten days he died.
translations.idiomatic: Medicine could not cure him. Some said his liver was torn and ruptured, and after a little more than ten days he died.

sentences.zh: 時年四十九。

translations.literal: He was then forty-nine years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was then forty-nine years old.

sentences.zh: 孝文始聞沖病狀，謂右衛宋弁曰：「僕射執我樞衡，總厘朝務，使我無後顧之憂，一朝忽有此患，朕甚愴懷。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen first heard of Chong's illness, he said to the Right Guard Song Bian: "The Vice Director holds my pivot and balance, overseeing and ordering court affairs, so that I am free of worries behind me — yet in a single morning this affliction has suddenly come; I am deeply sorrowful.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen first heard of Chong's illness, he said to the Right Guard Song Bian, "The Vice Director holds my pivot and balance, overseeing and ordering court affairs, so that I am free of worries behind me — yet in a single morning this affliction has suddenly come. I am deeply sorrowful.

sentences.zh: 及聞沖卒，為舉哀於縣瓠，發聲悲泣，不能自勝。

translations.literal: When he heard that Chong had died, he held mourning at Xianhu, breaking into wailing and weeping beyond his control.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that Chong had died, he held mourning at Xianhu, breaking into wailing and weeping beyond his control.

sentences.zh: 詔書褒述其美曰：「可謂國之賢也，朝之望也。」

translations.literal: An imperial edict praised and described his virtues, saying: "He may be called a worthy of the state, the hope of the court.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict praised and described his virtues, saying, "He may be called a worthy of the state, the hope of the court.

sentences.zh: 於是贈司空公，給東園秘器一具、衣一襲，贈錢三十萬、布五百匹、蠟二百斤。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was posthumously made Duke of the Ministry of Works, given one set of Eastern Garden secret burial implements and one suit of clothing, and granted three hundred thousand cash, five hundred bolts of cloth, and two hundred catties of wax.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was posthumously made Duke of the Ministry of Works, given one set of Eastern Garden secret burial implements and one suit of clothing, and granted three hundred thousand cash, five hundred bolts of cloth, and two hundred catties of wax.

sentences.zh: 有司奏諡曰文穆。

translations.literal: The responsible officials memorialized that his posthumous name should be Wenmu.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials memorialized that his posthumous name should be Wenmu.

sentences.zh: 葬于覆舟山，近杜預塚，孝文之意也。

translations.literal: He was buried on Mount Fuzhou, near Du Yu's tomb — at Emperor Xiaowen's wish.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried on Mount Fuzhou, near Du Yu's tomb — at Emperor Xiaowen's wish.

sentences.zh: 後車駕自鄴還洛，經沖墓，左右以聞。

translations.literal: Later when the imperial carriage returned from Ye to Luoyang and passed Chong's tomb, those about the emperor reported this.
translations.idiomatic: Later when the imperial carriage returned from Ye to Luoyang and passed Chong's tomb, those about the emperor reported this.

sentences.zh: 孝文臥疾，望墳掩涕久之，遣太常致祭。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen was ill in bed; he gazed at the tomb and wiped away tears for a long time, then sent the Minister of Rites to perform the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen was ill in bed. He gazed at the tomb and wiped away tears for a long time, then sent the Minister of Rites to perform the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 及與留京百官相見，皆敘沖亡沒之故，言及流淚，其相痛惜如此。

translations.literal: When he met with the officials remaining in the capital, each recounted the circumstances of Chong's death; as they spoke they wept, and their mutual grief was so great.
translations.idiomatic: When he met with the officials remaining in the capital, each recounted the circumstances of Chong's death. As they spoke they wept, and their mutual grief was so great.

sentences.zh: 子延寔，字禧，性溫良，少為太子舍人。

translations.literal: His son Yan Shi, styled Xi, was gentle and kind; in youth he served as Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan Shi, styled Xi, was gentle and kind. In youth he served as Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 宣武初，襲父爵清泉縣侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he inherited his father's title, Marquis of Qingquan County.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he inherited his father's title, Marquis of Qingquan County.

sentences.zh: 莊帝即位，以母舅之尊，超授侍中、太保，封濮陽郡王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangdi ascended the throne, by virtue of being the emperor's maternal uncle he was directly appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Tutor, and enfeoffed as Prince of Puyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangdi ascended the throne, by virtue of being the emperor's maternal uncle he was directly appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Tutor and enfeoffed as Prince of Puyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 延寔乙太保犯祖諱，又以王爵非庶姓所宜，抗表固辭，徙封濮陽郡公，改授太傅。

translations.literal: Since Yan Shi's title of Grand Tutor violated an ancestral taboo and a princely title was not fitting for a common surname, he submitted a resolute memorial declining; he was transferred to Duke of Puyang Commandery and instead appointed Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yan Shi's title of Grand Tutor violated an ancestral taboo and a princely title was not fitting for a common surname, he submitted a resolute memorial declining. He was transferred to Duke of Puyang Commandery and instead appointed Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 尋轉司徒公，出為使持節、侍中、太傅、錄尚書事、東道大行台、都督、青州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to Duke of the Ministry of Works and sent out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Mentor, Director of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, Great Commissioner's Office of the Eastern Route, Commander-in-Chief, and Governor of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred to Duke of the Ministry of Works and sent out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Mentor, Director of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, Great Commissioner's Office of the Eastern Route, Commander-in-Chief, and Governor of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 爾硃兆入京，乘與幽縶，延實以外戚見害于州館。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao entered the capital, the imperial carriage was detained in confinement; Yan Shi, as a maternal relative of the throne, was killed in the provincial guesthouse.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao entered the capital, the imperial carriage was detained in confinement. Yan Shi, as a maternal relative of the throne, was killed in the provincial guesthouse.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝初，反葬洛陽，贈使持節、侍中、太師、太尉公、錄尚書事、都督、雍州刺史，諡曰孝懿。

translations.literal: In the early years of Emperor Xiaowu, his remains were re-interred in Luoyang; he was posthumously given the titles Bearer of the Staff, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Preceptor, Duke of Grand Commandant, Director of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, Commander-in-Chief, and Governor of Yong Province, with the posthumous name Xiaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the early years of Emperor Xiaowu, his remains were re-interred in Luoyang. He was posthumously given the titles Bearer of the Staff, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Preceptor, Duke of Grand Commandant, Director of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, Commander-in-Chief, and Governor of Yong Province, with the posthumous name Xiaoyi.

sentences.zh: 長子彧，字子文，尚莊帝姊豐亭公主，封東平郡公，位侍中、左光祿大夫、中書監、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yu, styled Ziwen, married Princess Fengting, elder sister of Emperor Zhuangdi; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Dongping Commandery and held the offices of Attendant-in-Ordinary, Left Grand Master of Splendor and Virtue, Director of the Secretariat, General of Aggressive Cavalry, Grand General with staff equal in honor to a Three Excellency, and Governor of Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yu, styled Ziwen, married Princess Fengting, elder sister of Emperor Zhuangdi. He was enfeoffed as Duke of Dongping Commandery and held the offices of Attendant-in-Ordinary, Left Grand Master of Splendor and Virtue, Director of the Secretariat, General of Aggressive Cavalry, Grand General with staff equal in honor to a Three Excellency, and Governor of Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 彧性膏俠，爾硃榮之死也，武毅之士，皆彧所進。

translations.literal: Yu was by nature lavish and chivalrous; when Erzhu Rong died, the firm and resolute warriors had all been promoted through Yu's recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was by nature lavish and chivalrous. When Erzhu Rong died, the firm and resolute warriors had all been promoted through Yu's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 孝靜初，陷法見害。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaojing's reign he was killed for violating the law.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaojing's reign he was killed for violating the law.

sentences.zh: 尋詔復本爵。

translations.literal: Soon an edict restored his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict restored his original rank.

sentences.zh: 子道端襲。

translations.literal: His son Daoduan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daoduan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 彧七子，並彭城王勰女豐亭公主所生，以道、德、仁、義、禮、智、信為名。

translations.literal: Yu had seven sons, all born of Princess Fengting, daughter of Prince of Pengcheng Xie; they were named with the characters for Way, Virtue, Benevolence, Righteousness, Propriety, Wisdom, and Trust.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had seven sons, all born of Princess Fengting, daughter of Prince of Pengcheng Xie. They were named with the characters for Way, Virtue, Benevolence, Righteousness, Propriety, Wisdom, and Trust.

sentences.zh: 第四子義雄，有識悟，勤學，手不釋書。

translations.literal: The fourth son Yixiong had insight and understanding; he studied diligently and never put aside his books.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth son Yixiong had insight and understanding. He studied diligently and never put aside his books.

sentences.zh: 仕齊，位琅邪郡守。

translations.literal: He served in Qi and reached the office of Administrator of Langya Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He served in Qi and reached the office of Administrator of Langya Commandery.

sentences.zh: 義雄弟禮成，最知名。

translations.literal: Yixiong's younger brother Licheng was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Yixiong's younger brother Licheng was the most renowned.

sentences.zh: 禮成字孝諧，年七歲，與姑之子蘭陵太守滎陽鄭顥隨魏武帝入關。

translations.literal: Licheng, styled Xiaoxie, was seven years old when he followed Zheng Hao of Xingyang, Prefect of Lanling and son of his aunt by marriage, as they entered the passes with Emperor Xiaowu of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Licheng, styled Xiaoxie, was seven years old when he followed Zheng Hao of Xingyang, Prefect of Lanling and son of his aunt by marriage, as they entered the passes with Emperor Xiaowu of Wei.

sentences.zh: 顥母每謂入曰：「此兒平生，未嘗回顧，當為重器。」

translations.literal: Hao's mother would often say to those present: "This boy in all his life has never once looked back — he will be a vessel of consequence.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's mother would often say to those present, "This boy in all his life has never once looked back — he will be a vessel of consequence.

sentences.zh: 及長，沈深有行檢，不妄通賓客。

translations.literal: When he grew up he was deep and reserved, with proper conduct; he did not recklessly receive guests.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he was deep and reserved, with proper conduct. He did not recklessly receive guests.

sentences.zh: 在魏，曆著作郎、太子洗馬、員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In Wei he successively held the offices of Gentleman of Composition, Groom of the Crown Prince's Household, and Acting Outer Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei he successively held the offices of Gentleman of Composition, Groom of the Crown Prince's Household, and Acting Outer Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 周受禪，拜平東將軍、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Zhou received the abdication he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou received the abdication he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 于時貴公子皆竟習弓馬，被服多為軍容。

translations.literal: At that time the sons of noble families all vied in practicing archery and horsemanship, and their dress mostly took a military style.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the sons of noble families all vied in practicing archery and horsemanship, and their dress mostly took a military style.

sentences.zh: 禮成雖善騎射，而從容儒服，不失素望。

translations.literal: Although Licheng was skilled in riding and shooting, he wore the robes of a scholar with composure and did not lose the reputation he had long held.
translations.idiomatic: Although Licheng was skilled in riding and shooting, he wore the robes of a scholar with composure and did not lose the reputation he had long held.

sentences.zh: 後以軍功拜車騎大將軍、儀同三司，賜爵脩陽侯，拜遷州刺史。

translations.literal: Later for military merit he was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry, Commissioner Equal in Honor to a Three Excellency, enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiuyang, and appointed Governor of Qian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later for military merit he was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry, Commissioner Equal in Honor to a Three Excellency, enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiuyang, and appointed Governor of Qian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷有所徵發，禮成度以蠻夷不可擾，擾必為亂，上表固諫，武帝從之。

translations.literal: When the court at that time had levies and requisitions, Licheng judged that the barbarians could not be disturbed — if disturbed they would surely rebel — and submitted a resolute memorial remonstrating; Emperor Wu accepted his advice.
translations.idiomatic: When the court at that time had levies and requisitions, Licheng judged that the barbarians could not be disturbed — if disturbed they would surely rebel. He submitted a resolute memorial remonstrating, and Emperor Wu accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 伐齊之役，從帝圍晉陽，齊將席毗羅精兵拒帝，禮成力戰擊退之。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Qi he followed the emperor in besieging Jinyang; the Qi general Xi Piluo with picked troops resisted the emperor, and Licheng fought hard and drove him back.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Qi he followed the emperor in besieging Jinyang. The Qi general Xi Piluo with picked troops resisted the emperor, and Licheng fought hard and drove him back.

sentences.zh: 加開府，進封冠軍縣公，曆北徐州刺史、戶部中大夫。

translations.literal: He was granted a grand staff office, advanced in rank to Duke of Guanjun County, and successively held the offices of Governor of Northern Xu Province and Chief Clerk in the Household Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a grand staff office, advanced in rank to Duke of Guanjun County, and successively held the offices of Governor of Northern Xu Province and Chief Clerk in the Household Bureau.

sentences.zh: 禮成妻竇氏早沒，知隋文帝有非常之表，遂聘帝妹為繼室。

translations.literal: Licheng's wife, née Dou, died young; knowing that Emperor Wen of Sui showed extraordinary promise, he then took the emperor's younger sister as his new wife.
translations.idiomatic: Licheng's wife, née Dou, died young. Knowing that Emperor Wen of Sui showed extraordinary promise, he then took the emperor's younger sister as his new wife.

sentences.zh: 及帝為丞相，進位上大將軍，遷司武上大夫，委以心膂，及受禪，拜陝州刺史，進封絳郡公，賞賜優洽。

translations.literal: When the emperor became Chancellor he was promoted to Senior Grand General, transferred to Senior Commissioner of Martial Affairs, and entrusted as a right-hand man; when the emperor received the abdication he was appointed Governor of Shan Province, advanced to Duke of Jiang Commandery, and richly rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor became Chancellor he was promoted to Senior Grand General, transferred to Senior Commissioner of Martial Affairs, and entrusted as a right-hand man. When the emperor received the abdication he was appointed Governor of Shan Province, advanced to Duke of Jiang Commandery, and richly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 累遷襄州總管、左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Prefect of Xiang Prefecture and Left Guard Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to Prefect of Xiang Prefecture and Left Guard Grand General.

sentences.zh: 時突厥屢為寇患，緣邊要害，多委重臣，由是拜甯州刺史。

translations.literal: At that time the Turks repeatedly raided as a scourge; key frontier posts were often entrusted to important ministers, and for this reason he was appointed Governor of Ning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Turks repeatedly raided as a scourge. Key frontier posts were often entrusted to important ministers, and for this reason he was appointed Governor of Ning Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以疾征還京，終於家。

translations.literal: Recalled to the capital on account of illness, he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to the capital on account of illness, he died at home.

sentences.zh: 子世師，位度支侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Shishi held the office of Vice Minister in the Revenue Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shishi held the office of Vice Minister in the Revenue Bureau.

sentences.zh: 禮成弟智源，有器重。

translations.literal: Licheng's younger brother Zhiyuan had talent and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Licheng's younger brother Zhiyuan had talent and capacity.

sentences.zh: 仕齊，卒于高都郡守。

translations.literal: He served in Qi and died as Administrator of Gaodu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He served in Qi and died as Administrator of Gaodu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 智源弟信則，方雅廉慎。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan's younger brother Xinze was square in bearing, elegant, and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan's younger brother Xinze was square in bearing, elegant, and cautious.

sentences.zh: 齊武平中，位南陽王大司馬屬。

translations.literal: In the Wuping era of Northern Qi he held the office of Staff member to the Grand Marshal of Prince of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wuping era of Northern Qi he held the office of Staff member to the Grand Marshal of Prince of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 信則形短，中書侍郎頓丘李若戲之曰：「弟為府屬，可謂名以定體。」

translations.literal: Xinze was short in stature; Li Ruo of Dunqiu, Attendant of the Secretariat, teased him, saying: "Younger brother, as a staff member of the prince's household — one may say the name defines the form.
translations.idiomatic: Xinze was short in stature. Li Ruo of Dunqiu, Attendant of the Secretariat, teased him, saying, "Younger brother, as a staff member of the prince's household — one may say the name defines the form.

sentences.zh: 信則曰：「名以定體，豈過劣弱？」

translations.literal: Xinze said: "The name defines the form — how could it surpass being inferior and weak?
translations.idiomatic: Xinze said, "The name defines the form — how could it surpass being inferior and weak?

sentences.zh: 尋除尚書倉部郎中。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Chief of the Granaries Section in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed Chief of the Granaries Section in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 入周，為東京司門下大夫。

translations.literal: After entering Zhou he served as Vice Director in the Eastern Capital Bureau of Gates.
translations.idiomatic: After entering Zhou he served as Vice Director in the Eastern Capital Bureau of Gates.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，卒于沔州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he died as Governor of Mian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he died as Governor of Mian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 彧弟彬，字子儒。

translations.literal: Yu's younger brother Bin, styled Ziru.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's younger brother Bin, styled Ziru.

sentences.zh: 其父延寔既別封，彬襲祖爵清泉縣侯。

translations.literal: Since his father Yan Shi had been separately enfeoffed, Bin inherited his grandfather's title, Marquis of Qingquan County.
translations.idiomatic: Since his father Yan Shi had been separately enfeoffed, Bin inherited his grandfather's title, Marquis of Qingquan County.

sentences.zh: 位中書侍郎，卒于左光祿大夫，贈驃騎大將軍、光祿勳、齊州刺史，諡曰獻。

translations.literal: He held the office of Attendant of the Secretariat; he died while holding the office of Left Grand Master of Splendor and Virtue, and was posthumously given the titles General of Aggressive Cavalry, Minister of Splendor and Virtue, and Governor of Qi Prefecture, with the posthumous name Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He held the office of Attendant of the Secretariat and died while holding the office of Left Grand Master of Splendor and Virtue. He was posthumously given the titles General of Aggressive Cavalry, Minister of Splendor and Virtue, and Governor of Qi Prefecture, with the posthumous name Xian.

sentences.zh: 子桃杖襲。

translations.literal: His son Taozhang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Taozhang succeeded.

sentences.zh: 彬弟彰，位通直散騎侍郎，從父在青州，同時遇害。

translations.literal: Bin's younger brother Zhang held the office of Supervising Regular Attendant; he followed his father in Qing Province and was killed at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: Bin's younger brother Zhang held the office of Supervising Regular Attendant. He followed his father in Qing Province and was killed at the same time.

sentences.zh: 贈左將軍、瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the titles Left General and Governor of Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given the titles Left General and Governor of Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 延寔弟休纂，小字鍾羌，頗有父風。

translations.literal: Yan Shi's younger brother Xiuzuan, byname Zhongqiang, bore much of his father's character.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shi's younger brother Xiuzuan, byname Zhongqiang, bore much of his father's character.

sentences.zh: 位終太子舍人，贈驃騎大將軍、尚書令、司徒公、雍州刺史，追封樂涫縣公，後進封高陽郡公。

translations.literal: He ended his career as Attendant of the Heir Apparent; posthumously given General of Aggressive Cavalry, Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke of the Ministry of Works, and Governor of Yong Prefecture; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Letao County, later advanced to Duke of Gaoyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Attendant of the Heir Apparent. He was posthumously given the titles General of Aggressive Cavalry, Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke of the Ministry of Works, and Governor of Yong Prefecture, posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Letao County, and later advanced to Duke of Gaoyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 子昂襲。

translations.literal: His son Ang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ang succeeded.

sentences.zh: 昂，魏末為廣平郡太守，齊天保中，卒於光祿卿。

translations.literal: Ang, at the end of Wei served as Administrator of Guangping Commandery; in the Tianbao era of Qi he died while holding the office of Minister of Splendor and Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Ang, at the end of Wei served as Administrator of Guangping Commandery. In the Tianbao era of Qi he died while holding the office of Minister of Splendor and Virtue.

sentences.zh: 昂子道隆，有才識，明剖斷。

translations.literal: Ang's son Daolong had talent and insight, and was clear in judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Ang's son Daolong had talent and insight, and was clear in judgment.

sentences.zh: 仕齊，位並省尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He served in Qi and held the office of Left Assistant Director in the Joint Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served in Qi and held the office of Left Assistant Director in the Joint Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，為尚書比部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he served as Vice Minister in the Comparative Section of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he served as Vice Minister in the Comparative Section of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 休纂弟延孝，位尚書屯田郎中。

translations.literal: Xiuzuan's younger brother Yanxiao held the office of Chief of the Agricultural Colonies Section in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzuan's younger brother Yanxiao held the office of Chief of the Agricultural Colonies Section in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 于河陰遇害，贈侍中、車騎大將軍、司空公、定州刺史，進封臨潁縣公。

translations.literal: He was killed at Heyin; posthumously given Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Duke of the Ministry of Works, Governor of Ding Prefecture, and advanced in rank to Duke of Linying County.
translations.idiomatic: He was killed at Heyin. He was posthumously given the titles Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Duke of the Ministry of Works, and Governor of Ding Prefecture, and advanced in rank to Duke of Linying County.

sentences.zh: 韶從弟仲遵，有器業，彭城王勰為定州，請為定州開府參軍，累遷營州刺史。

translations.literal: Shao's cousin Zhongzun had talent and accomplishment; when Prince of Pengcheng Xie was in Ding Prefecture he invited Zhongzun as Opening Staff Officer of Ding Prefecture, and Zhongzun was promoted in succession to Governor of Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's cousin Zhongzun had talent and accomplishment. When Prince of Pengcheng Xie was in Ding Prefecture he invited Zhongzun as Opening Staff Officer of Ding Prefecture, and Zhongzun was promoted in succession to Governor of Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時四方州鎮，逆叛相續，營州城內，鹹有異心。

translations.literal: At that time in prefectures and garrisons throughout the realm rebellions followed one after another; within the walls of Ying Prefecture all had mutinous intent.
translations.idiomatic: At that time in prefectures and garrisons throughout the realm rebellions followed one after another. Within the walls of Ying Prefecture all had mutinous intent.

sentences.zh: 仲遵單車赴州，及至，與大使盧同以恩信懷誘，率皆安帖。

translations.literal: Zhongzun went alone in a single carriage to the prefecture; when he arrived, he together with the Commissioner Lu Tong used kindness and trust to win and persuade them, and all for the most part settled into peace.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzun went alone in a single carriage to the prefecture. When he arrived, he together with the Commissioner Lu Tong used kindness and trust to win and persuade them, and all for the most part settled into peace.

sentences.zh: 後明帝又詔盧同為行台，北出慰勞，同疑人情難信，聚兵將往。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Mingdi again issued an edict appointing Lu Tong as Commissioner of the Mobile Office to go north to offer comfort and rewards; Tong doubted that men's hearts could be trusted and gathered troops to set out.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Mingdi again issued an edict appointing Lu Tong as Commissioner of the Mobile Office to go north to offer comfort and rewards. Tong doubted that men's hearts could be trusted and gathered troops to set out.

sentences.zh: 城人劉安定、就德興等先有異志，謂欲圖己，逐仲遵害之。

translations.literal: The townspeople Liu Anding, Qiu Dexing, and others had earlier harbored rebellious intent; thinking that he meant to plot against them, they drove out Zhongzun and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The townspeople Liu Anding, Qiu Dexing, and others had earlier harbored rebellious intent. Thinking that he meant to plot against them, they drove out Zhongzun and killed him.

sentences.zh: 韶從祖抗，自涼州渡江左，仕宋，曆晉壽、安陸、東萊三郡太守。

translations.literal: Shao's collateral ancestor Kang, from Liang Province crossed the Yangtze to the left bank, served Song, and successively held the governorships of three commanderies: Jinshou, Anlu, and Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's collateral ancestor Kang, from Liang Province crossed the Yangtze to the left bank and served Song. He successively held the governorships of three commanderies: Jinshou, Anlu, and Donglai.

sentences.zh: 抗子思穆，字叔仁。

translations.literal: Kang's son Simu, styled Shuren.
translations.idiomatic: Kang's son Simu, styled Shuren.

sentences.zh: 有度量，善談論，工草隸，為當時所談。

translations.literal: He had breadth of mind, was skilled at discourse, and was adept at clerical and draft script; he was a subject of conversation among his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: He had breadth of mind, was skilled at discourse, and was adept at clerical and draft script. He was a subject of conversation among his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 太和十七年，攜家累自漢中歸魏，位都水使者。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Taihe he brought his household dependents from Hanzhong back to Wei and held the office of Commissioner for Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Taihe he brought his household dependents from Hanzhong back to Wei and held the office of Commissioner for Waterways.

sentences.zh: 及車駕南伐，以本官兼直閣將軍，從平南陽，以功賜爵樂平子。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south he served in his original office concurrently as Direct Gate General, followed in pacifying Nanyang, and for merit was granted the title Viscount of Yueping.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage campaigned south he served in his original office concurrently as Direct Gate General, followed in pacifying Nanyang, and for merit was granted the title Viscount of Yueping.

sentences.zh: 宣武踐祚，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu ascended the throne he was advanced in rank to Count.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu ascended the throne he was advanced in rank to Count.

sentences.zh: 累遷京兆內史，在郡八年，頗有政績。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Interior Minister of Jingzhao; in eight years in the commandery he achieved considerable administrative merit.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to Interior Minister of Jingzhao. In eight years in the commandery he achieved considerable administrative merit.

sentences.zh: 卒于營州刺史，贈安東將軍、華州刺史。

translations.literal: He died while holding the office of Governor of Ying Prefecture and was posthumously given the titles General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He died while holding the office of Governor of Ying Prefecture and was posthumously given the titles General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 有子十四人。

translations.literal: He had fourteen sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had fourteen sons.

sentences.zh: 嫡子斌襲，位散騎侍郎，早卒。

translations.literal: The eldest son Bin succeeded; he held the office of Regular Attendant and died young.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Bin succeeded. He held the office of Regular Attendant and died young.

sentences.zh: 斌兄獎，字道休，為莊帝所親，超贈思穆衛將軍、中書監、左光祿大夫，諡曰宣武。

translations.literal: Bin's elder brother Jiang, styled Daoxiu, was favored by Emperor Zhuangdi; the emperor exceptionally posthumously ennobled Simu as Guard General, Director of the Secretariat, and Left Grand Master of Splendor and Virtue, with the posthumous name Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: Bin's elder brother Jiang, styled Daoxiu, was favored by Emperor Zhuangdi. The emperor exceptionally posthumously ennobled Simu as Guard General, Director of the Secretariat, and Left Grand Master of Splendor and Virtue, with the posthumous name Xuanwu.

sentences.zh: 獎以戚裏恩澤，賜爵廣平侯。

translations.literal: Jiang, through favor as a maternal relative, was granted the title Marquis of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang, through favor as a maternal relative, was granted the title Marquis of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 曆中書侍郎、兼散騎常侍、聘梁使主、黃門郎、司徒左長史，行瀛州事。

translations.literal: He successively held Attendant of the Secretariat, Concurrent Regular Attendant, Chief Envoy on a Mission to Liang, Yellow Gate Gentleman, Left Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Works, and administered the affairs of Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He successively held Attendant of the Secretariat, Concurrent Regular Attendant, Chief Envoy on a Mission to Liang, Yellow Gate Gentleman, Left Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Works, and administered the affairs of Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 齊天保初，兼侍中、冀瀛滄三州大使，觀察風俗，還，拜魏尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao in Qi he concurrently served as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Commissioner to the three prefectures of Ji, Ying, and Cang, inspecting local customs; on his return he was appointed Intendant of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao in Qi he concurrently served as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Commissioner to the three prefectures of Ji, Ying, and Cang, inspecting local customs. On his return he was appointed Intendant of Wei.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈濟州刺史、中書令。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously given Governor of Ji Prefecture and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On his death he was posthumously given Governor of Ji Prefecture and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子瑰，位中書舍人黃門郎。

translations.literal: His son Gui held the offices of Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat and Yellow Gate Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gui held the offices of Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat and Yellow Gate Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 韶族弟琰之，字景珍，小字墨蠡。

translations.literal: Shao's clansman younger cousin Yanzhi, styled Jingzhen, childhood name Molí.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's clansman younger cousin Yanzhi, styled Jingzhen, childhood name Molí.

sentences.zh: 少知名，號曰神童，從父沖雅所歎異。

translations.literal: Renowned from youth, called a child prodigy; his father's younger cousin Chong sighed in wonder at him.
translations.idiomatic: Renowned from youth, he was called a child prodigy. His father's younger cousin Chong sighed in wonder at him.

sentences.zh: 每曰：「興吾宗者，其此兒乎！」

translations.literal: He often said: "The one who will revive our clan — is it not this boy!
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "The one who will revive our clan — is it not this boy!

sentences.zh: 恆資給所須，愛同己子。

translations.literal: He constantly supplied whatever was needed and loved him as his own son.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly supplied whatever was needed and loved him as his own son.

sentences.zh: 弱冠舉秀才，不行。

translations.literal: At coming of age he was nominated as a Fine Talent candidate but did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: At coming of age he was nominated as a Fine Talent candidate but did not take office.

sentences.zh: 曾遊河內北山，便欲有隱遁意。

translations.literal: Once while traveling on the Northern Mountains of Henei he felt an impulse toward reclusion.
translations.idiomatic: Once while traveling on the Northern Mountains of Henei he felt an impulse toward reclusion.

sentences.zh: 會彭城王勰辟為行軍參軍，苦相敦引，沖又遣信喻之，久乃應召。

translations.literal: When Prince of Pengcheng Xie invited him as Staff Officer on Campaign, Xie urgently pressed him; Chong also sent a letter to persuade him, and only after a long time did he answer the summons.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Pengcheng Xie invited him as Staff Officer on Campaign, Xie urgently pressed him. Chong also sent a letter to persuade him, and only after a long time did he answer the summons.

sentences.zh: 尋為中尉李彪啟兼著作佐郎，修撰國史。

translations.literal: Soon Li Biao the Commandant of Justice memorialized to appoint him Concurrent Assistant Gentleman of Composition to compile the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Li Biao the Commandant of Justice memorialized to appoint him Concurrent Assistant Gentleman of Composition to compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 稍遷國子博士，領尚書儀曹郎中，轉中書侍郎、司農少卿、黃門郎，修國史。

translations.literal: Gradually promoted to Erudite of the National University, concurrently Chief of the Rituals Section in the Ministry of Revenue, then transferred to Attendant of the Secretariat, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue for Agriculture, Yellow Gate Gentleman, compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Gradually promoted to Erudite of the National University, concurrently Chief of the Rituals Section in the Ministry of Revenue, then transferred to Attendant of the Secretariat, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue for Agriculture, and Yellow Gate Gentleman, compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 遷國子祭酒，轉秘書監，兼七兵尚書，遷太常師。

translations.literal: Promoted to Rector of the National University, transferred to Director of the Secretariat Bureau, concurrently Minister of the Seventh Military Section, promoted to Mentor of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Rector of the National University, transferred to Director of the Secretariat Bureau, concurrently Minister of the Seventh Military Section, and promoted to Mentor of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 琰之少機警，善談論，經史百家，無不悉覽，朝廷疑事，多所訪質。

translations.literal: Yanzhi from youth was quick-witted and alert, skilled in discussion; the classics, histories, and the hundred schools — none did he not read thoroughly; for doubtful matters at court, many came to consult him.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yanzhi was quick-witted and alert, skilled in debate. He read thoroughly through the classics, histories, and every school of thought. When the court faced doubtful matters, many came to him for guidance.

sentences.zh: 每云：「崔博而不精，劉精而不博，我既精且博，學兼二子。」

translations.literal: He often said: "Cui is broad but not precise; Liu is precise but not broad. I am both precise and broad — my learning combines the two men.
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "Cui is broad but lacks precision; Liu is precise but lacks breadth. I am both precise and broad — my learning combines the strengths of both men.

sentences.zh: 謂崔光、劉芳也。

translations.literal: He referred to Cui Guang and Liu Fang.
translations.idiomatic: He was speaking of Cui Guang and Liu Fang.

sentences.zh: 論者許其博，未許其精，當時議咸共宗之。

translations.literal: Critics acknowledged his breadth but did not acknowledge his precision; at the time discussions all took him together as their authority.
translations.idiomatic: Critics acknowledged his breadth but not his precision. At the time, scholarly debate everywhere took him as its standard.

sentences.zh: 又自誇文章，從姨兄常景笑而不許。

translations.literal: He also boasted of his literary compositions; his cousin older brother on his mother's side Chang Jing laughed but did not concede.
translations.idiomatic: He also boasted of his literary compositions. His maternal cousin Chang Jing laughed but would not grant the claim.

sentences.zh: 每休閒之際，恆閉門讀書，不交人事。

translations.literal: Whenever he had leisure, he always shut his doors to read and had no dealings with worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In his leisure hours he always shut his doors to read and kept clear of worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 常謂人曰：「吾所以好讀書者，不求身後之名。

translations.literal: He often said to people: "The reason I love reading is not that I seek fame after death.
translations.idiomatic: He often told others, "I love reading not because I seek posthumous fame.

sentences.zh: 但異見異聞，心之願也，是以孜孜搜討，欲罷不能。

translations.literal: It is simply that encountering the strange in sight and the novel in hearing is what the heart desires — therefore I search and investigate tirelessly, wishing to stop but unable.
translations.idiomatic: It is simply that the heart delights in seeing what is unusual and hearing what is new. That is why I search and investigate without rest, unable to stop even when I wish to.

sentences.zh: 豈為聲名，疾勞世人也？

translations.literal: How could it be for reputation's sake, wearing myself out to impress the world?
translations.idiomatic: Surely I am not exhausting myself before the world merely for the sake of renown?

sentences.zh: 此乃天性，非為力強。」

translations.literal: This is innate nature, not forced effort.
translations.idiomatic: This is my nature, not something I force upon myself.

sentences.zh: 前後再居史事，無所編緝。

translations.literal: He twice held posts in historical compilation but produced nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Though he twice held posts in historical compilation, he produced nothing.

sentences.zh: 安豐王延明博聞多識，每有疑滯，常就琰之辨析，自以為不及也。

translations.literal: Prince of Anfeng Yanming was widely learned and knowledgeable; whenever he encountered difficult points, he often went to Yanzhi for analysis, considering himself Yanzhi's inferior.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Anfeng Yanming was widely learned and knowledgeable. Whenever he hit a difficult point, he would go to Yanzhi for analysis and considered himself Yanzhi's inferior.

sentences.zh: 二子綱、慧，並從孝武帝入關中。

translations.literal: His two sons Gang and Hui both followed Emperor Xiaowu into Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: His two sons Gang and Hui both followed Emperor Xiaowu into the Guanzhong region.

sentences.zh: 綱位宜州刺史，儀同三司。

translations.literal: Gang held the office of Inspector of Yizhou with rank equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Gang served as Inspector of Yizhou with rank equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 子充節，少慷慨，有英略。

translations.literal: His son Chongjie was generous-spirited from youth and possessed bold strategy.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chongjie was open-handed from youth and possessed bold strategic vision.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，頻以行軍總管擊突厥有功，位上柱國、武陽郡公、朔州總管。

translations.literal: During the Kaihuang era of Sui, he repeatedly served as Commander on Campaign against the Turks with merit, rising to Upper Pillar of State, Duke of Wuyang Commandery, and Commander of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaihuang era of Sui, he repeatedly led campaigns against the Turks as Commander on Campaign with distinction, rising to Upper Pillar of State, Duke of Wuyang Commandery, and Commander of Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 甚有威名，為虜所憚，後有人譖有謀反，征還京師。

translations.literal: He enjoyed great renown and was feared by the barbarians; later someone slandered him for plotting rebellion, and he was summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He enjoyed great renown and was feared by the enemy. Later someone slandered him for plotting rebellion, and he was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 上怒之，充節素剛，憂憤卒。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry with him; Chongjie was by nature stubborn; distressed and indignant, he died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged. Chongjie, stubborn by nature, died of grief and indignation.

sentences.zh: 子大亮。

translations.literal: His son was Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Daliang.

sentences.zh: 曉字仁略，太尉虔之子也。

translations.literal: Xiao, styled Renlüe, was the son of Grand Commandant Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao, styled Renlüe, was the son of Grand Commandant Qian.

sentences.zh: 少而簡素，博涉經史，早有時譽，釋褐員外散騎侍郎，爾硃榮之立孝莊，曉兄弟四人，與百僚俱將迎焉。

translations.literal: From youth he was simple and unadorned, widely versed in the classics and histories, and early gained reputation in his day; upon leaving the cloth he became Supernumerary Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Palace Steeds; when Erzhu Rong established Emperor Xiaozhuang, Xiao and his four brothers joined the hundred officials in going to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was plain and unadorned, widely versed in the classics and histories, and early won renown. Upon entering office he became Supernumerary Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Palace Steeds. When Erzhu Rong enthroned Emperor Xiaozhuang, Xiao and his four brothers went with the hundred officials to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 其夜，曉衣冠為鼠噬，不成行而免。

translations.literal: That night rats gnawed Xiao's hat and robes so he could not join the procession and thus escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: That night rats gnawed through Xiao's hat and robes, so he could not join the procession and thus escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 其上三兄皆遇害。

translations.literal: His three elder brothers above him were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: All three of his elder brothers were killed.

sentences.zh: 曉乃攜諸猶子，微服潛行，避難東郡。

translations.literal: Xiao then took his nephews, dressed in plain clothes, and traveled secretly to take refuge in Dong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao then took his nephews, dressed in common clothes, and stole away in secret to take refuge in Dong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 行至成皋，為滎陽令天水閻信所疑，辟易左右，謂曉曰：「觀君儀貌，豈是常倫？

translations.literal: When he reached Chenggao he was suspected by Yan Xin of Tianshui, magistrate of Xingyang; Xin stepped aside from his attendants and said to Xiao: "Judging by your bearing and appearance — are you an ordinary sort?
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Chenggao, Yan Xin of Tianshui, magistrate of Xingyang, grew suspicious of him. Xin dismissed his attendants and said to Xiao, "Judging by your bearing and appearance — surely you are no ordinary man?

sentences.zh: 古人相知，未必在早，必有急難，須悉心以告。

translations.literal: People who truly know each other need not meet early; if you are in urgent distress you must confide in me wholeheartedly.
translations.idiomatic: True friendship need not begin early in life. If you are in urgent distress, you must confide in me with all your heart.

sentences.zh: 天下豈獨北海孫賓碩乎？」

translations.literal: Surely the world holds more men besides Sun Bingshuo of Beihai?
translations.idiomatic: Surely the world holds more worthy men than Sun Bingshuo of Beihai alone?

sentences.zh: 曉以能有長者之言，乃具告情實。

translations.literal: Hearing such words from an elder, Xiao told him the full truth.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing words so worthy of an elder, Xiao told him the whole truth.

sentences.zh: 信乃厚相資給以免。

translations.literal: Xin then generously supplied him and saw him safely away.
translations.idiomatic: Xin then gave him generous support and saw him safely on his way.

sentences.zh: 永安初，授輕車將軍、尚書左右主客郎，仍轉征虜將軍、中散大夫，又除前將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: In the early Yongan period he was appointed General of Light Chariots and Clerk for Foreign Guests in the Left and Right Sections of the Ministry of State, then transferred to General Who Subdues Barbarians and Palace Gentleman of Merit, and later appointed Forward General and Palace Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yongan period he was appointed General of Light Chariots and Clerk for Foreign Guests in the Left and Right Sections of the Ministry of State, then transferred to General Who Subdues Barbarians and Palace Gentleman of Merit, and later made Forward General and Palace Counselor.

sentences.zh: 天平初，遷都於鄴，曉便寓居清河，依從母兄崔甗鄉宅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping, when the capital moved to Ye, Xiao took up residence in Qinghe, staying at the country home of his maternal cousin Cui Yan.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping, when the capital moved to Ye, Xiao settled in Qinghe, lodging at the country estate of his maternal cousin Cui Yan.

sentences.zh: 甗給良田三十頃，曉遂築室居焉。

translations.literal: Yan granted him thirty qing of good farmland, and Xiao built a house there to live.
translations.idiomatic: Yan granted him thirty qing of good farmland, and Xiao built a house and made his home there.

sentences.zh: 時豪右子弟，悉多驕恣，請托暴亂，州郡不能禁止。

translations.literal: At the time the sons of great families were mostly arrogant and willful, using connections to commit violence and disorder, which prefectures and commanderies could not stop.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the sons of powerful families were mostly arrogant and willful, using connections to commit violence and disorder that prefectures and commanderies could not check.

sentences.zh: 曉訓勖子弟，鹹以學行見稱，時論以此多之。

translations.literal: Xiao instructed and admonished the younger generation, and all were praised for their learning and conduct; contemporary opinion held this in high regard.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao instructed and admonished the younger generation until all were praised for learning and conduct. Contemporary opinion held him in high regard for this.

sentences.zh: 曉自河陰家禍之後，屬王途未夷，無復宦情，備在名級而已。

translations.literal: After the family calamity at Heyin, with the imperial path not yet settled, Xiao had no further desire for office and remained on the register of ranks in name only.
translations.idiomatic: After the family calamity at Heyin, with the imperial cause still unsettled, Xiao lost all desire for office and remained on the rolls of rank in name only.

sentences.zh: 及遷都之後，因退私門，外兄范陽盧叔彪勸令出仕，前後數四，確然不從。

translations.literal: After the capital moved he retired to private life; his cousin older brother on his wife's side Lu Shubiao of Fanyang urged him to take office four times in succession, but he steadfastly refused.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital moved he withdrew into private life. His wife's cousin Lu Shubiao of Fanyang urged him to take office four times in succession, but he steadfastly refused.

sentences.zh: 武定末，齊文襄嗣事，高選僚采，召曉及前開府長史房延祐，並為外兵郎。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding, when Duke Wenxiang of Qi succeeded to affairs, he selected officials of high quality and summoned Xiao and former Chief Clerk of the Opening Grand General's Office Fang Yanyou, both appointed as Outer Military Clerks.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wuding, when Duke Wenxiang of Qi took charge of affairs, he sought out men of high quality and summoned Xiao and former Chief Clerk of the Opening Grand General's Office Fang Yanyou, appointing both as Outer Military Clerks.

sentences.zh: 後徙平西將軍、太尉府諮議參軍事，除頓丘太守。

translations.literal: Later transferred as General Who Pacifies the West and Consultative Staff Officer of the Grand Commandant's Office, appointed Prefect of Dunqiu.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to General Who Pacifies the West and Consultative Staff Officer of the Grand Commandant's Office, and appointed Prefect of Dunqiu.

sentences.zh: 天保中，頻曆廣武、東二郡太守，所在有惠政，為吏人所懷。

translations.literal: During Tianbao he successively served as Prefect of Guangwu and Dong commanderies; wherever he went his benevolent governance won the attachment of officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianbao he served in succession as Prefect of Guangwu and Dong commanderies. Wherever he went, his benevolent governance won the affection of officials and people alike.

sentences.zh: 卒於郡，年五十九，贈本官將軍、海州刺史。

translations.literal: He died in office at age fifty-nine, posthumously granted his former rank as general and made Inspector of Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at fifty-nine. Posthumously he was granted his former rank as general and made Inspector of Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 三子，伯山、仲舉、季遠。

translations.literal: He had three sons: Baishan, Zhongju, and Jiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Baishan, Zhongju, and Jiyuan.

sentences.zh: 超字仲舉，以字行於世。

translations.literal: Chao, styled Zhongju, was known by his style name in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Chao, styled Zhongju, was known to the world by his style name.

sentences.zh: 性方雅善制，白析美鬚眉，高簡宏達，風調疏遠。

translations.literal: By nature upright and refined, skilled in propriety, with fair complexion and fine beard and brows, he was lofty, simple, broad-minded, and detached in manner.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and refined by nature, skilled in propriety, with fair complexion and handsome beard and brows, he was lofty, plain, broad-minded, and aloof in bearing.

sentences.zh: 博涉經史，不守章句業，至於吉凶禮制，親表鹹取則焉。

translations.literal: Widely versed in classics and histories, he did not cling to textual commentaries; when it came to auspicious and inauspicious rites and regulations, relatives and kin all took their standards from him.
translations.idiomatic: Widely versed in the classics and histories, he did not bind himself to textual commentaries. In matters of ritual propriety, auspicious and inauspicious observances, relatives and kin all looked to him for guidance.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，仕齊為襄城王大司馬參軍事。

translations.literal: At coming of age he served Qi as Staff Officer in the Grand Marshal's Office under the Prince of Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: At coming of age he entered Qi service as Staff Officer in the Grand Marshal's Office under the Prince of Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 時尚書左僕射元文遙以令長之徒，率多寒賤，奏請革選，妙盡高資。

translations.literal: At the time Left Vice Minister of the Ministry of State Yuan Wenyao observed that magistrates and commandants were mostly poor and low-born, and memorialized to reform selection, fully employing men of high qualification.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Left Vice Minister of the Ministry of State Yuan Wenyao observed that district magistrates and commandants were mostly poor and low-born. He memorialized to reform selection and fully employ men of high qualification.

sentences.zh: 仲舉與范陽盧昌衡等八人，同見徵用。

translations.literal: Zhongju, together with Lu Changheng of Fanyang and seven others, were summoned for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongju, together with Lu Changheng of Fanyang and seven others, were summoned for appointment.

sentences.zh: 以仲舉為司州修武令。

translations.literal: Zhongju was made Magistrate of Xiuwu in Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongju was appointed Magistrate of Xiuwu in Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 仲舉蒞以寬簡，吏人號曰寬明。

translations.literal: Zhongju governed with leniency and simplicity; officials and people called him "Broad and Clear."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongju governed with leniency and simplicity. Officials and people called him "Broad and Clear."

sentences.zh: 于時昌衡為平恩令，百姓號曰恩明。

translations.literal: At the time Changheng was Magistrate of Ping'en; the people called him "Kind and Clear."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Changheng was Magistrate of Ping'en, and the people called him "Kind and Clear."

sentences.zh: 故時稱盧、李恩寬之政。

translations.literal: Hence the era spoke of the Lu and Li administrations of kindness and breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the age spoke of the Lu and Li administrations of kindness and breadth.

sentences.zh: 武平初，持節，使南定。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wuping he held the staff of authority as envoy to Nanding.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wuping he served as envoy to Nanding bearing the staff of authority.

sentences.zh: 州人並是蠻左，接帶邊嶂。

translations.literal: The people of the prefecture were all barbarian peoples of the Left, bordering frontier mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the prefecture were all tribal peoples of the frontier, living along the border mountains.

sentences.zh: 仲舉具宣朝旨，邊服清謐，朝廷大嘉之，還，授晉州別駕。

translations.literal: Zhongju fully proclaimed the court's intentions; the frontier was tranquil and orderly; the court greatly praised him; on his return he was appointed Vice Administrator of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongju fully proclaimed the court's intentions, and the frontier grew tranquil and orderly. The court greatly praised him, and on his return he was appointed Vice Administrator of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 及周師圍晉州，外無救援，行台左丞侯子欽內圖離貳，欲與仲舉謀，憚其嚴正，將言而止者數四。

translations.literal: When Zhou forces besieged Jinzhou with no relief from outside, Left Assistant of the Mobile Imperial Secretariat Hou Ziqin inwardly planned defection; wishing to conspire with Zhongju but fearing his strict integrity, he started to speak and stopped four times.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou forces besieged Jinzhou with no relief from outside, Left Assistant of the Mobile Imperial Secretariat Hou Ziqin inwardly planned defection. Wishing to conspire with Zhongju but fearing his strict integrity, he began to speak and stopped four times.

sentences.zh: 仲舉揣知其情，乃謂之曰：「城危累卵，伏賴於公，今之所言，想無他事，欲言而還中止也？」

translations.literal: Zhongju divined his intention and said to him: "The city is in peril fragile as piled eggs; we rely deeply on you; what you wish to say now — I suspect it is nothing else: you mean to speak but keep turning back?
translations.idiomatic: Zhongju divined his intention and said to him, "The city hangs by a thread, and we rely deeply on you. What you mean to say — is it not that you wish to speak but keep turning back?

sentences.zh: 子欽曰：「告急官軍，永無消息，勢之危急，旦夕不謀，意欲不坐受夷戮，歸命有道，於公何如？」

translations.literal: Ziqin said: "We have appealed urgently to the imperial army but receive no word; in peril so desperate that we cannot wait from morning till evening — my intent is not to sit and suffer slaughter; to surrender to the rightful power — what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Ziqin said, "We have appealed urgently to the imperial army but receive no word. The danger is so desperate that we cannot wait from one day to the next. My intent is not to sit here and be slaughtered — to surrender to the rightful power. What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 仲舉正色曰：「僕射高氏恩德未深，公於皇家沒齒非答。

translations.literal: Zhongju said sternly: "The Minister Gao's grace has not been deep; as for you toward the imperial house, even to the end of your days the debt cannot be repaid.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongju said sternly, "Minister Gao's grace has not been profound, yet toward the imperial house you owe a debt of loyalty that no lifetime could repay.

sentences.zh: 臣子之義，固有常道，何至今日，翻及此言！」

translations.literal: The duty of subject and minister has its fixed path — how has it come to this day that such words are spoken!"
translations.idiomatic: The duty of subject and minister has its fixed path. How has it come to this that such words are spoken today!"

sentences.zh: 子欽懼泄，夜投周軍。

translations.literal: Fearing exposure, Ziqin fled by night to the Zhou army.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing exposure, Ziqin fled by night to the Zhou army.

sentences.zh: 城尋破，周將梁士彥素聞仲舉名，引與言及時事。

translations.literal: The city soon fell; the Zhou general Liang Shiyan, who had long heard Zhongju's name, invited him to discuss current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The city soon fell. The Zhou general Liang Shiyan, who had long heard of Zhongju's reputation, invited him to discuss current affairs.

sentences.zh: 仲舉曰：「世居山東，受恩高氏，今國維不張，還勞師眾，不能死於臣道，豈敢幹非其議。」

translations.literal: Zhongju said: "My family has lived in Shandong for generations, receiving grace from the Gao clan; now the imperial foundation is unsteady yet you still trouble the army — I cannot die in loyal service; how dare I meddle with matters beyond my station.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongju said, "My family has lived in Shandong for generations and received grace from the Gao clan. Now the imperial foundation is unsteady, yet you still trouble the army. I have failed to die in loyal service — how dare I meddle in matters beyond my station?

sentences.zh: 士彥曰：「百里、左車，不無前事，想亦得之。」

translations.literal: Shiyan said: "Baili and Zuo Che — there are precedents; I imagine you understand."
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan said, "Baili and Zuo Che — there are precedents for this. I imagine you understand."

sentences.zh: 見逼不已，仲舉乃曰：「今者官軍遠來，方申吊伐，當先德澤，遠示威懷，明至聖之情，弘招納之略，令所至之所，歸誠有地，所謂王者之師，征而不戰也。」

translations.literal: Pressed unceasingly, Zhongju finally said: "Now the imperial army comes from afar to proclaim its punitive mission; it should first extend virtue and favor, showing majesty and kindness from afar, making clear the supreme sage's intent and expanding a policy of welcome and acceptance, so that wherever it goes there is ground for surrender — this is what is called the army of a true king, conquering without fighting."
translations.idiomatic: Pressed unceasingly, Zhongju finally said, "Now the imperial army comes from afar on a punitive mission. It should first extend virtue and mercy, showing majesty and kindness from afar, making clear the supreme sage's intent and expanding a policy of welcome and acceptance, so that wherever it goes men have reason to submit. This is what is called the army of a true king — one that conquers without fighting."

sentences.zh: 土彥深以為然，益相知重。

translations.literal: Shiyan deeply agreed and came to respect him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan deeply agreed and came to respect him all the more.

sentences.zh: 初，城敗之後，公私蕩然，軍人簿帳，悉多亡毀，戶口倉儲，無所憑據。

translations.literal: At first, after the city fell, public and private affairs were utterly devastated; military registers were largely lost and destroyed, and household registers and storehouses had nothing to serve as evidence.
translations.idiomatic: At first, after the city fell, public and private affairs lay in ruins. Military registers were largely lost or destroyed, and household registers and storehouses had nothing left to serve as evidence.

sentences.zh: 事無大小，士彥一委仲舉，推尋勾當，絲發無遺，於軍用甚有助焉。

translations.literal: Matters great and small Shiyan wholly entrusted to Zhongju; Zhongju tracked and settled accounts leaving nothing out, even the finest detail — of great help to military supply.
translations.idiomatic: Matters great and small Shiyan wholly entrusted to Zhongju. Zhongju tracked and settled accounts with nothing omitted, down to the smallest detail — of great help to military supply.

sentences.zh: 鄴城平，仍將家隨例入關。

translations.literal: When Ye fell he still took his family with the others into the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Ye fell, he still took his family with the others into the Pass.

sentences.zh: 仲舉以親故流離，情不願住，妻伯父京兆尹博陵崔宣猷留不許去。

translations.literal: Because his kin and old friends were scattered, Zhongju did not wish to stay; his wife's uncle by marriage Cui Xuanyou, Governor of Jingzhao in Boling, detained him and would not allow him to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Because his kin and old friends were scattered, Zhongju did not wish to remain. His wife's uncle Cui Xuanyou, Governor of Jingzhao in Boling, detained him and would not let him leave.

sentences.zh: 固辭，乃得還鄴。

translations.literal: He firmly declined and was finally able to return to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined and was at last able to return to Ye.

sentences.zh: 尋有詔，素望舊資，命州郡勒送，仲舉懼嚴命而至。

translations.literal: Soon there was an edict: given his longstanding reputation and senior standing, commanderies and prefectures were ordered to compel his delivery; fearing the stern mandate, Zhongju came.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict was issued: given his longstanding reputation and senior standing, commanderies and prefectures were ordered to compel his delivery. Fearing the stern mandate, Zhongju came.

sentences.zh: 補秋官賓部上士，深乖情願，乃取急言歸。

translations.literal: Appointed Senior Clerk in the Guests Section of the Ministry of Punishments, far from his wishes, he pleaded urgent business and went home.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed Senior Clerk in the Guests Section of the Ministry of Punishments — far from his wishes — he pleaded urgent business and returned home.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，秦王俊鎮洛州，召補州主簿。

translations.literal: During Sui Kaihuang, Prince Jun of Qin held Luozhou and summoned him as Chief Clerk of the Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During Sui Kaihuang, Prince Jun of Qin held Luozhou and summoned him as Chief Clerk of the Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 友人蜀王府記室范陽盧士彥謂仲舉曰：「丈人往經征辟，每致推辭，何為徒勞之任，忽爾降德？」

translations.literal: His friend Lu Shiyan of Fanyang, Recorder of the Prince of Shu's Domain, said to Zhongju: "You sir have been repeatedly summoned and always declined — why now accept a futile post and suddenly lower your dignity?
translations.idiomatic: His friend Lu Shiyan of Fanyang, Recorder of the Prince of Shu's Domain, said to Zhongju, "You sir have been repeatedly summoned and always declined. Why now accept a futile post and suddenly lower your standing?

sentences.zh: 仲舉笑曰：「屈伸之事，非子所知。」

translations.literal: Zhongju smiled and said: "Matters of bending and stretching — these are not for you to understand."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongju smiled and said, "Matters of bending and stretching — these are not for you to understand."

sentences.zh: 尋被敕追赴京，朝廷以仲舉婆娑州裏，責黜左降為隆州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Soon by edict he was recalled to the capital; the court, finding that Zhongju had lingered in his prefecture, censured and demoted him to Administrative Clerk of Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon by edict he was recalled to the capital. The court, finding that Zhongju had lingered in his prefecture, censured and demoted him to Administrative Clerk of Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋以疾歸，以琴書自娛，優遊賞逸，視人世蔑如也。

translations.literal: Soon he returned home on grounds of illness, amused himself with zither and books, roamed in ease and leisurely enjoyment, treating worldly affairs with utter indifference.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he returned home on grounds of illness, amused himself with zither and books, wandered at ease in leisurely enjoyment, and treated worldly affairs with utter indifference.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷舉士，著作郎王劭又舉以應詔。

translations.literal: When the court summoned men of talent, Compiler Wang Shao again recommended him to answer the edict.
translations.idiomatic: When the court summoned men of talent, Compiler Wang Shao again recommended him to answer the edict.

sentences.zh: 以前致推遷為責，除冀州清江令，未幾，又以疾還。

translations.literal: He was rebuked for his earlier evasions and delays and appointed Magistrate of Qingjiang in Jizhou; before long he again returned home on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was rebuked for his earlier evasions and delays and appointed Magistrate of Qingjiang in Jizhou. Before long he again returned home on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 後以資例，授帥都督、洛陽令。

translations.literal: Later, by seniority and precedent, he was granted the rank of Commander-in-Chief and made Magistrate of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later, by seniority and precedent, he was granted the rank of Commander-in-Chief and made Magistrate of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 彭城劉逸人謂仲舉曰：「君之才地，遠近所知，久病在家，恐貽時論，具為武職，差若自安。」

translations.literal: Liu Yiren of Pengcheng said to Zhongju: "Your talent and standing are known far and near; long illness at home may invite gossip in the world; a purely military post would be somewhat easier on you.
